For more information see Overview of Mission Control in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.1/mission-control/overview-of-mission-control-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.2/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the ueba_finding_exclusion_edit capability could store attacker-controlled values in a User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) finding exclusion rule. Splunk Enterprise Security could later run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands from the rule with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could cause Splunk Enterprise Security to read stored credentials and modify lookups and knowledge objects.
The vulnerability is possible because the UEBA finding exclusion workflow does not escape user-controlled rule values before using them in generated SPL.
For more information see Create a finding exclusion rule using UEBA configuration page (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security/create-a-finding-exclusion-rule-using-ueba-configuration-page) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the ueba_ers_execution_post capability could cause the User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Content App to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions through an Entity Risk Score calculation. With this access, the user could expose stored credentials and other data outside the permissions assigned to that role.
The vulnerability is possible because the UEBA Content App does not validate Entity Risk Score calculation values before including them in SPL searches.
For more information see Installing the UEBA Content App for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.5/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/installing-the-ueba-content-app-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Entity risk scoring in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.4/risk-based-alerting/entity-risk-scoring-in-splunk-enterprise-security), and Roles and knowledge objects in UEBA for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.8/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/ueba-content-app-for-on-premises/roles-and-knowledge-objects-in-ueba-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could modify a search macro associated with risk exclusions. Scheduled Risk data model acceleration searches could later run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands from that macro with elevated permissions. With this access, the user who modified the search macro could expose stored credentials and modify indexes or lookup data available to those searches.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk Enterprise Security app metadata grants the "ess_analyst" role write access to the risk exclusion search macro.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.3/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security), and Use search macros in searches (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/search-macros/use-search-macros-in-searches) in the Splunk documentation.

TeamPass is a self-hosted collaborative password manager. Prior to 3.2.1.2, the update_folder action in app/sources/folders.queries.php allowed an authenticated, non-read-only user to re-parent a folder without checking whether the target folder or submitted parentId belonged to the caller's user-accessible_folders set. Selecting a personal folder as the new parent passed the personal-folder guard and set personal_folder on the target, transferring the credential subtree into the attacker's accessible space after the next login and hiding it from the organization, including administrators. The change exposed credential labels, logins, URLs, email addresses, and descriptions, while sharekey-protected passwords remained protected; hiding the subtree also denied other users access. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.1.2.
In JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA before 2026.3, 2026.2.4 code execution was possible in untrusted projects via the Code Provenance plugin

Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows space admins to reach internal hosts because Nextcloud.get_client builds WebDAV clients from Storage.url without calling safe_request. Attackers can create a NEXTCLOUD storage via POST /api/storage/ pointing at internal hosts, import a file, then call GET /api/get_recipe_file/<id>/ to read internal service or cloud metadata responses.

A malicious actor with access to the network could exploit a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability found in UniFi Access Application to obtain information and make unauthorized changes on the host device.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, every network.* procedure is only authentication-protected and does not require the Docker permission, allowing a standard member to list, inspect, create, import, recreate, resynchronize, and delete Docker networks. A member can disrupt service connectivity or alter network configuration, and create/import operations can target an unchecked serverId. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the user login-email change logic. When an external authentication backend is configured (LDAP, Shibboleth, ApacheSecureAuth, or CustomAuth), the login email address serves as the key by which the directory service resolves a user's identity, organization, and role on each login. The __canChangeLogin() method in UsersController only checked the MISP.disable_user_login_change setting and site-admin status; it did not account for whether an external authentication backend was active. As a result, any authenticated non-admin user (including org admins) could change their own login email to an address that matches a higher-privilege account in the external directory. On the user's next login, the external backend would resolve that email to the target directory identity, granting the attacker the organization and role associated with that identity. This constitutes an account-identity capture and privilege escalation: the attacker effectively assumes the identity of any directory account whose email they can guess or discover. The vulnerability requires an authenticated session with a valid API key or session token and a MISP instance configured with at least one external authentication backend. The impact is limited to the scope of the captured directory identity's privileges within MISP.

Frappe ERPNext before 16.35.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in financial reporting endpoints that allows low-privilege authenticated users to generate reports outside their permitted scope. Attackers can send crafted requests to affected reporting endpoints to read other companies' tax and payment data, including personal and corporate identifiers and financial totals.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows restricted and view-only clients to read default project resources by requesting the default project directly. Attackers knowing resource names can read profiles, images, network zone peer keys and stored credentials, and export custom volume or bucket backups to obtain full contents or S3 admin keys.

Obot from 0.8.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power User accounts to reach internal hosts by advertising a malicious OAuth token endpoint in remote MCP server metadata. Attackers can direct token exchange or refresh requests, including redirected GET requests, to cloud metadata services or private-network hosts and read error response bodies.

An insecure password reset vulnerability in the Admin Password Recovery Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to change an administrator or sub-administrator account password by providing the corresponding username and email address. The application does not require verification of account ownership through an email token, OTP, or another authentication mechanism before updating the password, potentially resulting in account takeover.

CAST Imaging is vulnerable to Path Traversal vulnerability in "/api/server-folders" and "/api/server-folders/download" endpoints. These file-management endpoints accept user-supplied filesystem paths and allow selected system commands to be executed at the specified location, but they do not enforce sufficient authorization boundaries or restrict access to a predefined set of resources. An authenticated attacker can enumerate server directories via the "ls" command and retrieve arbitrary files outside of the intended application workspace, such as "/etc/passwd", exposing sensitive data.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

CAST Imaging has multiple path traversal vulnerabilities in various endpoints. The application does not properly validate the path parameters, allowing an authenticated attacker to use "../" sequences to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files.


Critically, by reading "/proc/self/environ", the attacker can obtain environment variables containing sensitive credentials such as Keycloak and PostgreSQL passwords, leading to full server compromise and administrative access.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an organization member with permission to manage custom-property definitions and edit property values to add an attacker-controlled SSH authentication key to the personal account of another member through HTML stored in a single-select custom-property option. Exploitation required another definition manager in the same organization to attempt to remove the poisoned option while it was in use and save the definition with a valid sudo session. Repository access through the added key depended on the permissions of the victim and independent authorization controls. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

Joomla! Core - [20261143] - Core - Information disclosure in GET request task plugin in Joomla 4.1.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The GET request task plugin stored fetched responses in a publicly accessible folder, exposing the response contents.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpd_script_env module) allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust the atom table of an httpd server that serves ESI scripts.

When mod_esi builds the environment for an ESI callback, httpd_script_env:http_env_element/3 checks that a request header name already exists as an atom, then creates the atom http_<header-name> with list_to_atom/1. Atoms are never garbage collected, and each new atom passes the existence check on a later request. So a header named node creates http_node, a header named http_node creates http_http_node, and so on. A stream of requests to any ESI URL grows the atom table until it reaches its limit (+t), and then the whole Erlang VM aborts, together with every application on the node.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

RTU500 contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in its IEC 61850 MMS server implementation. A malicious user with access to the IEC 61850 interface can trigger improper handling of asynchronous control operations involving special response and timing criteria. This may result in access to invalid memory structures, leading to a software exception, loss of IEC 61850 communications, or device reboot.

A path traversal vulnerability in the File Explorer share-link upload component allows a remote attacker with a folder-scoped upload share link to upload or overwrite files in the shared folder's immediate parent directory due to missing trailing validation prior to path canonicalization.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From versions 0.6.23 and above, before 0.8.0, AutoGPT Platform ships a hardcoded default Fernet encryption key in backend/.env.default, which encrypts every user's OAuth tokens, API keys, and integration credentials in the User.integrations column. Anyone with read access to the database of a deployment using the default key can decrypt the stored credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.0.

Use of a default cryptographic key in the instance registration component in Amazon SSM Agent before 3.3.5226.0 on AWS-provided Windows Server AMIs released before 2026-09-09 might allow local users without administrative privileges to obtain the instance's Default Host Management Configuration role credentials via the registration key shared by all instances launched from the same AMI.



To remediate this issue, users should replace affected instances with instances launched from AWS Windows Server AMIs released on or after 2026-09-09, which include SSM Agent 3.3.5226.0 or later. Upgrading the agent in place does not replace the shared key, and deleting the agent's Vault breaks instances managed through Default Host Management Configuration.

React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. In versions prior to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 and 19.3.1, react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack are vulnerable to denial of service. Specially crafted HTTP requests sent to server function endpoints can cause out-of-memory exceptions or excessive CPU usage. This issue is fixed in versions 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 and 19.3.1.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. A high privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to arbitrary command execution.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. A high privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to arbitrary command execution.

sigstore-js @sigstore/oci before 0.8.0 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that leaks registry credentials by replaying OAuth2 password-grant request bodies on cross-origin 307 or 308 redirects. Attackers who can make a trusted token service redirect to their host via open redirect or compromise receive the username and password POSTed by RegistryClient.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.10, 4.0.x before 4.0.7, and 4.1.x before 4.1.7 contain a padding oracle in RSACrypt::decryptWithRSA15() because RSA1_5 decryption lacks implicit rejection, so invalid padding, wrong CEK length, and valid padding take measurably different time. Remote attackers can submit adaptively crafted JWE encrypted_key values and measure these timing differences to recover the wrapped content encryption key.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.12, 4.0.x before 4.0.8, 4.1.x before 4.1.10, and 4.2.x before 4.2.4, and jwt-encryption-algorithm-ecdh-es through 3.2.10, have a ConcatKDF::generate() that performs a single SHA-256 round, deriving at most 32 bytes for ECDH-ES and ECDH-SS direct key agreement. Anyone holding a JWE using A256CBC-HS512 can decrypt it under an all-zero AES key, while A192CBC-HS384 content keys have only 64-bit strength.

Parse Server 2.5.0 before 8.6.121 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.1 does not handle a failure to serialize an object after a beforeSave trigger, leaving the request unsettled and terminating the server process. A remote attacker able to update an object in a class with a beforeSave trigger can send a dot notation key below a non-object field, such as a timestamp, to crash the server for all clients.

Uncaught Exception vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service via a client-selected legacy serializer on binary channel broadcasts.

When an application broadcasts {:binary, data} payloads on a channel topic, any client that connects without a vsn parameter, or with vsn=1.0.0, and joins that topic makes those broadcasts fail. Phoenix.Channel.Server.send/4 encodes each broadcast with every subscriber's own serializer inside the PubSub dispatch loop, calling fastlane!/1 with no rescue, and the negotiated Phoenix.Socket.V1.JSONSerializer raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a binary payload. Every binary broadcast on the topic then crashes the broadcasting process and skips every subscriber dispatched after the attacker. For broadcasts arriving from other nodes the loop runs in the PubSub adapter worker, whose repeated crashes restart the PubSub supervisor and empty the node's subscription registry while sockets stay connected.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.5.7 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

Improper Input Validation vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix (Phoenix.Presence) allows an attacker who can join a channel to cause a denial of service via a non-string presence key.

track/3,4 accepts any term as the presence key, such as a JSON object taken from a join payload. The key is converted with to_string/1 only later, in Phoenix.Presence.group/1, which raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a map. group/1 runs whenever presences are listed and when each presence diff is broadcast, together with the application's fetch/2, which can likewise raise on an unexpected key. Once such a key is tracked, every process that lists presences on the topic crashes, typically each channel that joins it, and presence diffs for the topic are lost.

From 1.7.0 the diff runs in a Task.Supervisor.async task linked to the tracker shard, and Phoenix.Presence.handle_info/2 has no clause for its failure. The shard then terminates, taking down every channel and LiveView process tracked on it and erasing presence state for all its topics. Repeated joins exhaust the restart intensity and take down the application supervisor.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.2.0 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

Cesanta Mongoose 7.22 before 7.24 with the built-in TLS stack contains an out-of-bounds read in mg_timegm() that allows remote attackers to crash the process via crafted X.509 certificate validity months. Attackers can present a certificate with month '00' or out-of-range values during the handshake, before signature verification, causing an unchecked dm array index and denial of service.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.08 until 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker can place NukeViet's internal {@[, ]@}, [@{, and }@] sanitizer markers in an iframe srcdoc value by encoding square brackets as HTML entities. Recursive NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() processing decodes the characters, accepts the forged marker, and later converts it to real markup without normal tag or attribute filtering. Because an unsandboxed srcdoc iframe shares the parent origin and iframe is enabled by default through NV_ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS, stored Contact messages, comments with the editor enabled, or submitted articles can execute JavaScript with the viewer's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit Contact module content containing numeric HTML entities with more than eight leading zeros in a URL-bearing attribute. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() does not decode that form before filterAttr() checks for a javascript: scheme, but browsers decode it when rendering the stored content. With an allowed tag such as the default iframe, the reconstructed script URL executes in the administration origin when staff view the message, permitting session-riding actions while remaining unable to read the HttpOnly session cookie directly. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, the Comment module accepts attacker-controlled base64 content in the status_comment parameter through modules/comment/funcs/main.php; modules/comment/comment.php decodes it with nv_base64_decode() and assigns it to STATUS_COMMENT without output escaping. The required checkss token was derived from the site-wide NV_CACHE_PREFIX rather than NV_CHECK_SESSION, so a token disclosed in public comment markup could be reused across sessions in a crafted URL. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore cause decoded HTML or JavaScript to render in a victim's browser and perform phishing or same-origin actions. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, the public POST /api/global/users/init endpoint on a self-hosted single-tenant deployment accepts an attacker-controlled tenantId and evaluates checkAnyUserExists() in the selected tenant database instead of the legitimate default tenant. An unauthenticated attacker can select an unused tenant namespace to bypass the one-time initialization guard, causing packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts to create a tenant-specific CouchDB database and a global-administrator document without a session or CSRF token. Repeating this operation with unique tenant identifiers can exhaust datastore resources and leave latent privileged records. The created administrator cannot log into the default tenant while multi-tenancy remains disabled, which limits the immediate impact to persistent writes, denial of service, and records that may become usable during later multi-tenant operation or migration. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the orderBy placeholder handling for custom queries in Neo4j Spring Data Neo4j versions 6.1.0 through 8.0.8 and 8.1.0 through 8.1.2 allows a remote attacker to read database contents via blind reads, write read content into new nodes, or, if APOC and APOC file export are enabled, to write query results to a file in the database's accessible file system via crafted sort order parameters. Exploitation requires an application that passes unvalidated user input as the orderBy value to a custom Cypher query using the placeholder directive.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions 12.8.1 through 12.8.3, its buildURL function checked the attacker-supplied source string for parent-directory segments, but when the source begins with the same special scheme as the base, such as http or https, the WHATWG URL parser drops the scheme and resolves the remainder as a relative path. A payload that glues the scheme to a percent-encoded parent-directory sequence therefore passes the check, because the inspected segment reads as the scheme plus the dots rather than a bare parent-directory token, while the proxy forwards the encoded traversal unchanged. An upstream that percent-decodes the request path before resolving dot-segments then serves a path outside the configured prefix, so an unauthenticated client scoped to an upstream prefix, or relying on Fastify route guards in front of the proxy, can escape that prefix and reach sibling or parent upstream endpoints. The per-segment check added in 12.8.1 is what the scheme prefix bypasses, and releases up to 12.8.0 already rejected the decoded form. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree, publish_parts_from_doctree, the {% rst %} template tag, the rst template filter, DocutilsTemplates, and DocutilsView pass lower-trust reStructuredText to Docutils without disabling file_insertion_enabled, raw_enabled, ambient docutils.conf processing, or unsafe URI schemes and without consistently sanitizing doctrees. An attacker who can influence rendered reStructuredText can use include or csv-table directives to read local files or cause server-side URL requests, or use raw HTML and unsafe URI output to inject stored script-capable content. Applications that render only trusted static reStructuredText are not affected unless attackers can influence it. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

MRemoteNG uses single MD5 hash with no salt and no iterations for key-derivation. An attacker who obtains the encrypted data can brute-force
a weak or moderate passphrase offline at extreme speed and then decrypt every stored connection
password. When the default passphrase is in use, no cracking is needed at all; the key is derived from a
publicly known value.


Vendor did not provide the range of vulnerable versions. Only version 1.76.20 was tested and confirmed vulnerable. Other versions may also be vulnerable.

Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory in the Como log viewer in Temenos Application Framework Java (TAFJ) R18.SP76.0 allows remote authenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via path traversal

mini-snmpd is a minimal SNMP agent implementation. Prior to 1.7, the ASN.1 BER parser in protocol.c does not verify that an attacker-controlled field length is no greater than the remaining packet size before decode_str(), decode_oid(), and decode_ptr() evaluate size - len + 1. When len exceeds size, unsigned size_t arithmetic wraps and bypasses the bounds check, allowing the decoder to read beyond the 2048-byte packet buffer. Parsing occurs before the SNMP community string is checked, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can send one crafted request to UDP port 161 to crash the process and potentially disclose adjacent heap memory. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.

OwnPay is a self-hosted open-source payment gateway automation platform. In 0.2.0 and earlier, modules/gateways/alipay/AlipayGateway.php fails open when an Alipay callback lacks a signature or the merchant has no configured public key because verify(array $callbackData, array $credentials) falls back to an undefined mode credential that defaults to test mode, while verifyWebhook() returns true unconditionally. An unauthenticated request to POST /webhook/{gateway} can provide a pending order reference and matching amount, pass both verification gates without a valid payment signature, and cause the order and corresponding payment-received ledger entries to be marked completed. No fixed version is available as of this review.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the BigBlueButton plugin is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) injection when an authenticated administrator configures a malicious BigBlueButton server URL. Processing attacker-controlled XML from that server can read arbitrary local files and perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Sensitive configuration, credentials, source code, and internal network resources may be exposed. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the /dev/incus guest-API image export handler that fails to pin the project parameter to the guest's own project. Container root users with the guest-API image entitlement can supply another project in the project query parameter to export public or cached images, including non-public images pulled from authenticated remotes.

sqlite-mcp is a Model Context Protocol server for SQLite. Prior to 0.1.2, the default read-only mode can be bypassed through execute_query, which accepts a leading SELECT while the SQLite driver executes trailing statements, and through describe_table, which interpolates the caller-controlled table_name into PRAGMA table_info. Either path can issue ATTACH DATABASE, which opens an attached file read-write despite mode=ro and can make the protected database writable, read other SQLite database files, or create a SQLite-format file at a path writable by the server process. Existing non-empty files that are not SQLite databases are refused and left unchanged. The server has no built-in authentication and listens on all interfaces at :8080 by default, so any client that can reach the port can invoke these tools unless an authenticating proxy is in place. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.2.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in OpenKM v6.3.12 allows attackers to execute arbitrary Javascript in the context of the user's browser via a crafted input injected into the Content parameter.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to read protected pages because admin and site scopes share a page cache key. Routine editor activity through the API plugin rebuilds the page index without frontmatter.yaml access rules, exposing members-only page content until the cache is rebuilt.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the job status polling endpoint of jobs.controller.ts that lacks an @Acl decorator. Unauthenticated attackers with a job id can read buffered status messages and completion payloads, exposing signed export download URLs or new base identifiers.

An XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability affects a Storefront REST API in HCL Commerce versions 8, 9.0.1 and 9.1.x.  A remote attacker, using a specially crafted XML, could potentially view internal files or consume memory resources.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.63 through 0.10.0, an external API key or OAuth token that has only the EXECUTE_BLOCK permission can run AutoPilotBlock through the external API and receive a full, unattended AutoPilot turn. This lets the holder use the account owner's stored third-party credentials, library agents, and workspace files, and run AutoPilot's sandboxed shell, which the same key is refused when it requests those directly. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

HortusFox is a self-hosted web application for collaborative plant management. Prior to 6.2, the toggle_boolean_value() handler in app/controller/admin.php passes the name parameter of the /admin/environment/boolean/toggle route in app/config/routes.php to AppModel::updateSingle() in app/models/AppModel.php, which concatenates the parameter into the SQL UPDATE identifier position without validation. An unauthenticated attacker can induce a signed-in administrator to open a crafted link, causing SQL injection that permits expressions and subqueries to read database contents, including an administrator password hash, or modify settings to enable passwordless administrator access. The hash alone does not permit direct login. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.

In ServerSessionBroker of server_session_broker.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In FuchsiaVideoOutputProvider of fuchsia_video_output_provider.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is needed for exploitation.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, can quote a string parameter for the wrong value of standard_conforming_strings when preferQueryMode=simple is set. A statement, trigger or configuration reload can turn the setting off during a session. A parameter value with a backslash and a quote then ends the literal, and the rest of the value runs as SQL. Before 42.7.6 any session with the setting off was affected. The statement cache can also reuse a parse made under the other setting. With allowEncodingChanges=true and the EUC_JP or SJIS client encoding, the yen sign acts as a backslash. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, misreads some quoted text in its query parser. A `}` inside a literal ends a JDBC escape such as `{ts}`, and the rest of the literal is translated as SQL. A dollar quote whose tag has a non-ASCII symbol or space is not recognized. An `E''` string with a doubled quote is scanned as a standard string. `{fn right}` and `{fn timestampdiff}` with a negative argument produce a `--` comment. In each case text that the application quoted correctly can run as SQL with the privileges of the application's database role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

A flaw was found in gpgme. When processing crafted input, an early return following memory reallocation can leave internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory, resulting in a double-free condition during cleanup. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt process memory, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) crash.

Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in the RDM folder duplication endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated low-privileged attacker to overwrite and move arbitrary vault entries and read their history via a client-supplied entry identifier.

The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to permanently delete any comment they authored anywhere on the site — including regular post comments and lesson comments — along with all replies to those comments authored by any other user, including Administrators and Instructors.

The PublishPress Revisions: Duplicate Posts, Submit, Approve and Schedule Content Changes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to permanently force-delete arbitrary trashed posts, pages, and revisions owned by any user, including higher-privileged users. The required nonce is trivially harvested by any Contributor-level user because the static 'revisions-deleted' nonce action is emitted in a redirect header on the init hook before WordPress enforces edit.php's capability check, and once obtained it authorizes deletion of any trashed post or revision on the site.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. From 0.7.0 until 0.8.6, when local registration is enabled and at least one social provider is configured, POST /api/auth/register passes an unparsed request object into api/server/services/AuthService.js, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to persist a forged provider value for a known victim email. The api/strategies/socialLogin.js email-fallback path then accepts the planted record when the victim signs in because it compares the stored provider name without requiring the provider subject identifier. The victim OAuth session and the attacker local-password session become bound to the same user record, giving the attacker persistent read and write access to data created by the victim. The first-user administrator role is an additional conditional impact only on a fresh deployment. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in version up to, and including, 0.9.134. This is due to a timing side channel in the bundled RSA decryption path, insufficient validation of migration receiver backup records, and missing path validation in the cleanup_local_backup() function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover an active migration receiver's RSA modulus, inject a backup record containing path traversal, and cause a later scheduled cleanup to delete an attacker-selected file writable by the web server. Exploitation requires an unexpired receiver key generated by an administrator and a subsequent manual or scheduled backup lifecycle.

Logto is the modern, open-source auth infrastructure for SaaS and AI apps. Prior to 1.46.0, social account linking can use an unverified email returned by the standard OAuth 2.0 or Azure AD connector to select an existing local account. When findSocialRelatedUser matches a victim's email and a request to POST /api/experience/identification enables linkSocialIdentity, an attacker who controls that unverified provider email can link an attacker-controlled social identity to the victim account and sign in as the victim. The issue applies when the provider does not verify email ownership or allows the value to be set freely; Google, GitHub, and default OIDC connector behavior is not affected because those paths expose only verified email. Version 1.46.0 adds an opt-in email synchronization control to the standard OAuth 2.0 connector, while the Azure AD connector has offered an equivalent opt-in control since version 1.43.0. These controls preserve existing behavior by default, so administrators must enable them on affected connectors. A configurable mitigation is available in version 1.46.0.

The GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to donor account account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0. This is due to the plugin not properly validating a donor's identity prior to updating the password of a linked WordPress account. The donation receipt processes an attacker-controlled first name through the V3 template engine and then reprocesses the result through the legacy `{meta_donor_*}` engine, which can disclose the donor's email-access bearer token. The donor-dashboard password endpoint accepts that token by itself and calls `wp_set_password()` for the WordPress user linked to the donor. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reset the password of any WordPress account linked to a GiveWP donor record and gain access to that account. If the linked account is an administrator, the attacker can achieve full site compromise and remote code execution through standard administrator functionality. A published GiveWP form with a usable gateway, enabled donor email access (enabled by default), knowledge of the donor email address, and an account already linked to the targeted donor record are required. NOTE: This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-82676 to satisfy the administrator donor pre-requisite for a targeted administrator user attack.

The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). The attacker-supplied path is stored via the unauthenticated form submission endpoint, but the actual file deletion only occurs when an administrator subsequently deletes the stored entry — a routine housekeeping action that serves as the detonation trigger. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the cbforms_delete_uploaded_files function in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Exploitation requires an administrator to delete the attacker-planted form entry, and the attacker must know or be able to guess the absolute path of a file writable by the PHP process. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Video & Photo Gallery for Ultimate Member plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in versions up to, and including, 1.1.4 This is due to the um_gallery_add_videos() AJAX handler persisting user-supplied videos[] values into the file_name column after only esc_url() — which preserves path-traversal sequences — and the companion um_gallery_delete_photo() helper passing that stored value to unlink() through get_user_image_path() with no canonicalization or allowed-directory check. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution when the right file (such as wp-config.

The Shortcodes and extra features for Phlox theme plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 2.17.22 via the 'extra_template_path' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The slug-based allowlist introduced as the fix for CVE-2023-37888 constrains only the template_part_file filename suffix and does not validate the extra_template_path directory component, meaning path traversal sequences are fully functional against this parameter.

Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('PHP Remote File Inclusion') vulnerability in thembay Aora aora allows PHP Local File Inclusion.This issue affects Aora: from n/a through 1.3.5.

The Toocheke Companion plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization leading to arbitrary post and attachment deletion in versions up to, and including, 2.38. This is due to a missing object-level capability check in the toocheke_tapas_ajax_cleanup_start() and toocheke_tapas_ajax_cleanup_step() AJAX handlers; the toocheke_tapas_cleanup_ajax_guard() method only verifies the primitive delete_posts capability (held by every Contributor) and never calls current_user_can('delete_post', $post_id) or delete_others_posts before passing the attacker-supplied series_post_id to wp_delete_post() and wp_delete_attachment() with force-delete enabled. The required nonce is emitted on the Import: Tapas admin page, which is gated only by edit_posts, so a Contributor can read it. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to permanently delete any importer-created series post, every child 'comic' post attached to it, and every Media Library attachment belonging to those posts — regardless of which user originally created them.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.java includes its private parameter, BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.java renders the complete private-key byte array when isPrivate is true, and BoringSSL.EVP_HPKE_KEY_init_or_throw in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSL.java includes rejected privateKeyBytes in an exception message. Applications that log affected key-pair objects or initialization exceptions can persist complete HPKE private key material in logs or telemetry. Anyone who can read those records can recover the key and may compromise OHTTP message confidentiality or authenticity expectations while the key remains usable. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to improper TLS certificate validation in the GDP Terraform provider, allowing a network attacker with a man-in-the-middle position to intercept sensitive credentials transmitted to the Guardium appliance.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to path traversal in the datasource functionality. An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to delete arbitrary files on the appliance.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to a stack-based buffer overflow when processing a specially crafted PROXY protocol v1 header. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could cause scheduled metric alert searches to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and access credentials stored in cleartext. This requires at least one non-internal metric index on the instance.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not fully validate metric alert filter input before using it in a scheduled search.

In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could submit client-controlled feature settings through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could modify limited response metadata outside the expected server-side configuration.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API processes client-supplied feature settings without enforcing the expected server-side configuration boundary.

In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0 a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could access data associated with another tenant and cause actions to be attributed to that tenant through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk AI Assistant accepted a client-controlled tenant identifier when selecting the authorization context for a request.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an operator of a configured identity provider could authenticate as an existing user associated with another configured identity provider. If that account has the "Administrator" Splunk SOAR role, the operator could control the Splunk SOAR deployment.
Splunk SOAR does not bind external user accounts to the identity provider that provisions them and authenticates accounts by username without verifying provider ownership.
The vulnerability requires more than one configured external identity provider with distinct trust domains and a target username that an operator of a configured identity provider can authenticate through a different provider.
For more information see Configure single sign-on authentication (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/configure-single-sign-on-authentication-for-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Manage roles and permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who holds the "Observer" Splunk SOAR role could access a password-reset credential in a diagnostic log bundle and reset the password for an active local account.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not redact password-reset email bodies before it logs communications between product processes.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the ueba_finding_exclusion_edit capability could create a finding exclusion rule that references an attacker-controlled lookup definition if the role also grants write access to globally shared lookup definitions, as the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role does. The User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Content App could later include the lookup name in a search and run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user who created the finding exclusion rule could expose stored credentials and other data outside the permissions assigned to the "ess_analyst" role.
The vulnerability is possible because UEBA finding exclusion processing does not safely quote lookup names before including them in SPL searches.
For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.3/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Roles and knowledge objects in UEBA for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.8/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/ueba-content-app-for-on-premises/roles-and-knowledge-objects-in-ueba-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could create an attacker-controlled saved search. Threat intelligence lookup generation could later run the saved search with elevated permissions, which could let the user who created the saved search run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with those permissions.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not restrict threat intelligence lookup generation to the intended saved searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Turn on threat matching searches in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.0/threat-intelligence/turn-on-threat-matching-searches-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

Paymenter is a free and open-source webshop solution for management of hosting services. Prior to 1.5.7, the HasConfirmation trait in app/Livewire/Traits/HasConfirmation.php, included by app/Livewire/Component.php across 36 client-facing Livewire components, exposed executeConfirmedAction as a public action that invoked any component method accepted by method_exists. The action could call inherited InteractsWithProperties::fill(), whose data_set() writes arbitrary public properties, including state marked with #[Locked] and dotted paths into hydrated Eloquent models. Depending on the methods and properties exposed by an individual component, an unauthenticated caller could use this path to bypass intended authorization and modify server-side state intended to be immutable or protected from client-side manipulation. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.7.

The WPO365 | SEAMLESS WORDPRESS + MICROSOFT INTEGRATION (WPO365 | LOGIN) WordPress plugin before 45.4 does not ensure the signature validated on a SAML response covers the element the user identity is read from, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a response via signature wrapping and log in as any user, including administrators, when they can supply a single artifact signed by the configured identity provider.

The SAML SSO Login  WordPress plugin through 1.5.2 does not verify that the SAML assertion whose signature it validates is the same assertion it reads the user identity from, allowing unauthenticated attackers who hold a validly signed assertion for any identity to authenticate as any existing user, including an administrator, through XML signature wrapping.

A flaw was found in hypershift-addon. Due to an overly permissive role-based access control (RBAC) configuration that grants permissions to all authenticated users rather than restricting them to the addon service, a low-privileged authenticated user can view, modify, or delete managed cluster resources. This improper authorization allows unauthorized users to alter or disrupt clusters across the entire managed fleet.

A stored cross site scripting attack when viewing email aliases in postfixadmin 4.0 before 4.0.7, and postfixadmin 3.3 before 3.3.17 could be caused by signed in admins able to inject aliases.

The immonex Kickstart plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 1.19.0 via the 'inx-r-cidata (JSON blob containing 'template' and 'template_folders')' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The filename-level sanitization that strips dot-slash sequences applies only to the template filename component, not to the attacker-supplied template_folders directory paths, rendering it ineffective against directory traversal via that parameter.

The The GDPR Framework By Data443 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.2. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete all postmeta rows for every Easy Digital Downloads payment order on the site, destroying order metadata belonging to all customers. Exploitation requires that Easy Digital Downloads 2.x is active and the GDPR Framework's EDD compatibility option is enabled with a delete or delete_and_notify action configured.
Dell PowerStore contains an integer underflow vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to denial of service of a cryptographic service.

An incorrect implementation of authentication algorithm vulnerability in the SSO API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.2.2-72806-5 and 7.3.1-86003-1 (7.2.1-69057 is not affected) allows remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and conduct denial-of-service attacks with prior knowledge of the distinguished name (DN).

A path traversal flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with ansible-galaxy collection install, the install destination directory is derived from the namespace and name fields declared inside the collection artifact's own metadata, which are not validated as well-formed collection identifiers or checked for path containment. A malicious collection artifact -- delivered as a local file, a remote URL, a source directory, a git repository, or as a dependency -- can use a crafted name value to redirect the install destination outside the configured collections path, causing ansible-galaxy to delete an existing directory writable by the invoking user and then write attacker-controlled files to that location.

A path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) was found in ansible-core's ansible-galaxy role installation. An explicit role "name" taken from a role's meta/requirements.yml is used to construct the on-disk installation path without validating that the resulting destination stays within the selected roles directory. A name containing "../" escapes that directory, and an absolute name replaces it entirely. Because ansible-galaxy processes transitive dependencies from an installed role's meta/requirements.yml, a malicious role publisher can cause attacker-supplied files to be written outside the operator's chosen roles directory when the operator installs the role, and, when --force is used, can cause an existing role directory outside that path to be removed and replaced. The impact is bounded by the invoking user's filesystem permissions and requires the operator to install the attacker-influenced content.
Tanium addressed an argument injection vulnerability in Core Content.

A flaw was found in the GLib DMA-BUF path of WebKitGTK. The UIProcess trusted fds.size() as the DMA-BUF plane count when handling AcceleratedBackingStore::DidCreateDMABufBuffer and copied offsets and strides without verifying that those vectors had the same length. A compromised WebProcess can send mismatched vector lengths, causing an out-of-bounds read in the privileged UIProcess. This can disclose UIProcess memory and crash the UIProcess, and may be used as part of a Web Content sandbox-escape chain.

isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.8, git cherry-pick applies tree changes through applyTreeChanges in src/utils/walkerToTreeEntryMap.js without checking whether a leading path component is a symbolic link. If a victim worktree contains a tracked symlink to a location outside the worktree and a cherry-picked tree places a file beneath that path, the write follows the symlink and materializes attacker-controlled blob content at the external destination. This allows arbitrary file writes and can cause data tampering, code injection into interpreted files, privilege escalation, denial of service, or follow-on code execution depending on the selected target path. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.8.

The Okta Swift Management SDK does not percent-encode forward slash (/) characters during path parameter interpolation. If an application supplies input containing relative path sequences (e.g., ../) to an SDK method, standard URL normalization may direct the outbound request to an alternative Okta Management API endpoint.

The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

Music Assistant is an open-source media library manager that integrates streaming services with connected speakers. Prior to 2.8.0, parse_arguments() passes the caller-controlled return_type parameter for config/core/get_value, config/providers/get_value, and config/players/get_value to parse_value() and Python eval() when resolving type parameters in music_assistant/helpers/api.py. Any authenticated user, regardless of role, can reach these commands through the WebSocket /ws endpoint or the REST JSON-RPC /api endpoint, causing arbitrary Python code to run with the Music Assistant server process privileges before command-handler validation, even if the request later fails. A default installation requires no special configuration, and compromise can expose secrets and configuration, alter library data, and control the application container. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.0.

X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to .8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.5, the Security Server writes each downloaded federated global-configuration part under the X-Road instance identifier declared by the part itself without checking that the identifier matches the source ecosystem that signed and delivered it. A malicious or compromised federated ecosystem can provide a validly signed SHARED-PARAMETERS part naming a victim ecosystem, causing the part to be written as the victim's authoritative shared-params.xml. The poisoned configuration can persist across refreshes, add attacker-controlled trust material, and enable impersonation of victim members and Security Servers across every ecosystem federated with the malicious source. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.5.

Dell PowerStore contains an XML External Entity (XXE) Injection vulnerability. A high-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to disclosure of sensitive files and root-level compromise of the appliance.

The Dynific Addons for Elementor (formerly Anywhere Elementor) WordPress plugin before 1.3.1 does not perform a capability check on an AJAX action that stores a configuration value, allowing any authenticated user, including Subscribers, to store a value that is later output without proper escaping in a quoted attribute on an administrator settings page, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the administrator's session.

k8s-mcp-server manages Kubernetes clusters through the Model Context Protocol. Prior to 1.1.0, SERVER_MODE defaults to SSE, with the listener on 0.0.0.0:8080, but main.go creates the SSE server without an authentication option or context function. The GET /sse handler creates a sessionId that is only a correlation value, and the POST /message handler accepts a loadable sessionId without an authorization or Origin check before dispatching tools/call; consequently, any client able to reach the port can enumerate and invoke registered Kubernetes tools without credentials. Read-only mode is disabled by default, leaving write-capable Kubernetes tools available to run with the server's configured cluster privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted PSD (Photoshop Document) image file in LAB color mode, the plugin does not properly validate that a fourth channel is present when the transparency flag is set. This mismatch causes the merged-image path to allocate buffers for three components while performing color conversion with four-component formats, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

Genetec Security Center can expose access control unit credentials in plain text in server log files when specific non-default logging options are enabled. An attacker with local access to the affected log files could retrieve and use these credentials.

Hermes Agent is an open-source autonomous AI agent built by Nous Research for running tool-using workflows across CLI, desktop, and messaging interfaces. From 0.21.6 to 0.23.1, when Bot Desktop is hosted inside a non-local terminal backend, the agent process reads a backend-writable screen environment file without validating keys or values and merges its entries into the environment of processes started on the agent machine. Specifically, when terminal.backend is set to docker or ssh (or a plugin backend declaring supports_streams) with placement auto or terminal, _published() in tools/bot_desktop/sandbox_host.py accepts arbitrary KEY=VALUE lines from the hermes-bot-desktop env file and propagates them via tools/bot_desktop/runtime.py into the browser harness, computer-use helpers, and local terminal children. Code running inside the terminal backend can therefore set variables such as LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, or PATH and gain code execution on the agent machine as the gateway user upon a subsequent browser or computer-use spawn, exposing credentials, tokens, and session history under the Hermes home directory. The default local backend, backends that cannot host a screen (Modal, Daytona, and Vercel), and Hermes Cloud in its default configuration are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.23.2.

In reconnect.shard.cml, there is a possible way to turn off the camera streaming and microphone mute indicator LEDs due to an unnecessary hardware capability grant. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with User execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In LogExportControllerImpl of log_export_fidl.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a service handler that is not unregistered when the object is destroyed. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with User execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In ZxFdServer of zx_fd_grpc_ipc_builder.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a raw pointer to a server object that is not cleared when the server is destroyed. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with User execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In InteropPolicy::OnStateChange of interop_policy.cc, there is a possible way to turn off the camera streaming indicator LED while the camera is still streaming due to a logic error. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with User execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In HDSBrokerFidlImpl::RegisterMessageHandler of hds_broker_fidl_impl.cc, there is a possible way to replace internal message handlers due to a missing check for existing handler registrations. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with User execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In DuoVideoBuffer of duo_video_buffer.cc, there is a possible out of bounds write due to an integer overflow. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with User execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In astro-airflow-mcp 0.5.0 through 0.9.1, the af CLI and the MCP server send telemetry from a Python subprocess that can import modules from the current working directory. If a user runs an af command or an MCP tool call from inside a project that contains an attacker-supplied json.py, that file runs with the user's privileges. Users who only run the tool in projects they trust are not affected. Fixed in 0.9.2; in earlier versions, setting AF_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 prevents it.

A vulnerability was discovered in the ZoneAlarm client for Windows that allows a low-privileged local user to run code with SYSTEM privileges. An attacker must first be able to run code on the target system as a local user.

An out-of-bounds write was addressed with improved input validation. This issue is fixed in iOS 26.7.2 and iPadOS 26.7.2, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, macOS Sequoia 15.8.2, macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, tvOS 27.2. A user may be able to cause unexpected app termination or arbitrary code execution.
A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management. This issue is fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2. Processing a maliciously crafted file may lead to unexpected app termination.

An integer overflow was addressed with improved input validation. This issue is fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, macOS Sequoia 15.8.2, macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, tvOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2. Processing a maliciously crafted USD file may lead to unexpected app termination.
A logic issue was addressed with improved checks. This issue is fixed in Xcode 27.2. An app may be able to gain root privileges.

G DATA Total Security TSNxGService Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the TSNxGService service. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the service to delete a file. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28663.

Krita TIF File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of TIF files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28517.

Krita HEIC File Parsing Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The issue results from the use of a vulnerable version of libheif. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28656.

Krita EXR File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of EXR files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before writing to memory. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28752.

Krita HEIC File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. The issue results from the use of a vulnerable version of libde265. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28657.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of TIFF files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28771.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of PSB files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28905.

Krita ASL File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of ASL files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28906.
