User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The issue results from the use of a vulnerable version of openjpeg. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28646.

codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, automatic import of a repository's .codebase-memory/ artifact allocated a decompression buffer using the attacker-controlled 64-bit original_size value from artifact.json but truncated that value to int when passing the destination capacity to the Zstandard decompressor. A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, the Cypher parser accepted an unbounded number of projection items in RETURN and WITH clauses while projection executors indexed fixed 32-element stack arrays using the parsed count. A query_graph query with more than 32 projection items could therefore write beyond those arrays, and a related result-column path could read uninitialized stack slots even when no node matched. Any caller of query_graph, including an agent whose query is influenced by untrusted content, could cause a reliable server crash and potentially compromise process confidentiality and integrity. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

A flaw was found in crun. When copying files onto a tmpfs mounted with tmpcopyup, crun opens the destination a second time by name. A container that shares a writable volume with the container being created can change that path between the two lookups, so crun copies image files onto host files, including files under /proc/sys.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to local privilege escalation via the SUID-root podman_wrapper binary on the Collector appliance. A local attacker with low-privileged access to the Collector can exploit insufficient argument validation in the SUID binary to execute arbitrary commands as root, resulting in full compromise of the Collector appliance.
In JetBrains Junie before 252.819.35, 253.819.35 code execution was possible via terminal environment settings in project files

A flaw was found in gdm. The CreateRemoteDisplay D-Bus method fails to perform proper authorization checks when initiating a remote display session. A local attacker with access to the login screen environment can invoke this method with an arbitrary username to bypass standard automatic login verification checks. This vulnerability allows the attacker to achieve privilege escalation and start an unauthorized session as any user on the system, including root.

A maliciously crafted SBSAR file, when imported or loaded through the Substance in 3ds Max plugin in Autodesk 3ds Max, can trigger an Out-of-Bounds Write vulnerability. A malicious actor may leverage this vulnerability to cause an application crash, data corruption, or potentially execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

Gortex is a high-performance code-intelligence engine for AI agents and integrated development environments. Prior to 0.55.0, resolveFilePath in internal/mcp/tools_fileops.go accepts absolute paths without checking indexed repository roots, while write_file, edit_file, and move_inline in internal/mcp/tools_move_inline.go omit guardSymlinkWithinRepo before reaching AtomicWriteFile and related write sinks. A caller that can influence MCP tool arguments can therefore create or overwrite files anywhere the daemon user can access, including startup or hook files that execute code on a later trigger. The flaw violates Gortex's repository-confinement invariant and can lead to arbitrary host code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.55.0.

A flaw was found in the file-xmc plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted XMC image file, the plugin does not properly validate the comment subtype before using it as an array index. This missing validation leads to out-of-bounds memory access, invalid free and use-after-free issues. This vulnerability can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 suffer from an Improper Access Control issue in the msfdb database initialisation component whereby a PostgreSQL cluster initialised via msfdb init is configured with trust authentication and a world-accessible Unix domain socket in /tmp, allowing any local user on the same host to authenticate as the passwordless postgres superuser and execute arbitrary operating system commands as the msfdb owner. 


This issue is fixed in version 6.5.10.
A heap buffer overflow in reading encoding files in X.Org libfontenc before 1.11.0 could be used by local attackers able to inject enc files to the X server could crash or escalate privileges.
Tanium addressed an unauthorized code execution vulnerability.

GNU Emacs 31.1 contains a code injection vulnerability in its handling of directory-local variables. A crafted .dir-locals.el can supply a (REGEXP FUNCTION t) entry in auto-mode-alist; when a matching file is opened, Emacs calls FUNCTION before set-auto-mode--dir-local-valid-p validates it, executing arbitrary Emacs Lisp with the privileges of the Emacs process. (Emacs 30.2 is unaffected.)

A stack-based buffer overflow in the replication origin name parsing component in AWS pgactive before 2.1.10 might allow an authenticated remote user to execute arbitrary operating system commands as the database operating system user via a crafted replication origin name.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to pgactive version 2.1.10 or later.

Joomla Extension - regularlabs.com - PHP code injection via content inserted during article preparation in Sourcerer extension < 17.0.2 - Sourcerer decided whether PHP may run based on the author or last editor of the host article and applied that decision to complete code blocks that other extensions, such as Users Anywhere or Articles Anywhere, inserted into the article while it was prepared. A user able to edit a value rendered by such an extension, for example the display name in their own user profile, could therefore have PHP executed in the context of a trusted article. Sourcerer 17.0.2 authorizes each executable block against its own source; Users Anywhere 3.1.0, ReReplacer 16.4.0 and Snippets 11.2.0 supply the source information needed to keep executing eligible saved content.

Joomla! Core - [20261134] - Core - Improper root user check in Joomla 1.6.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - A loose comparison of the configured emergency root user against the username allowed accounts with a numeric username to gain super user privileges.

Dell Virtual Storage Integrator for VMware vSphere Web Client, versions prior to 10.12.0.0, contains a Server-Side Request Forgery SSRF vulnerability in httpRest.js. A low privileged remote attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized access to internal services

Dell Virtual Storage Integrator for VMware vSphere Web Client, versions prior to 10.12.0.0, contains a Use of Hard-coded Credentials vulnerability in ssl_config.properties. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to credential exposure.

Improper input validation in some SPARQL functions available in Apache Jena ARQ allows users to submit SPARQL queries that cause excessive CPU and/or memory usage.  This may be the result of intentionally malicious inputs in the query itself, or an expression applied over data that has been insufficiently validated/sanitised

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.3.0, which fixes this issue.

An improper TLS certificate validation vulnerability exists in the ADM online update service. An unauthenticated attacker capable of performing a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack against the device's firmware update connection can impersonate the update server using an untrusted TLS certificate and supply malicious update metadata. The attacker may cause a crafted firmware image to be installed and execute arbitrary code with root privileges when automatic firmware updates are enabled.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.
ACME challenge routing logic of Zoraxy fails to validate request URIs properly, that allows an attacker to send an arbitrary request to a service on the internal network.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

rConfig Core 8.2.19 before 8.2.22 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass the DeviceIpIsValid loopback guard by supplying unresolved hostnames. Attackers can create a device with a hostname resolving to loopback and device_port_override 6379, causing configuration downloads to send Redis inline commands for remote code execution.

n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Prior to 1.123.90 and 2.14.0, the invitation acceptance endpoint accepts inviter and invitee user IDs without a signed invitation token, allowing any preexisting member to take over a pending new user account. A member with permission to list users can read the ID of a pending account and set its password without authentication, then log in as that user, including as an admin when the invitation has the admin role. Exploitation requires an invitation that has not been accepted yet. This issue is fixed in versions 1.123.90 and 2.14.0.

A flaw was found in the administrative interface of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when Fine-Grained Admin Permissions are used to restrict a group administrator from managing specific sub-groups. Due to an incomplete fix for a previous vulnerability, a restricted administrator can bypass these restrictions by moving a forbidden sub-group to the top level of the hierarchy. This allows the attacker to gain unauthorized control over the groups members, potentially leading to a full takeover of the security realm.

Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a Lua code injection vulnerability that allows LDAP-authenticated users to inject Lua statements into session files via unescaped login names. Attackers can log in with a name containing a Lua long-string terminator followed by code, which executes on a later session request as the Wing FTP service account.

Gogs before 0.14.4 on Windows contains a path equivalence vulnerability in isRepositoryGitPath that allows authenticated users with write access to bypass .git directory protection using NTFS aliases. Attackers can create, rename or upload files via aliases like git~1 or .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION to overwrite .git/config or hooks and execute commands as the Gogs process.

Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows attackers to hijack SSO identities by planting local accounts with unverified victim emails. When emailfallback is enabled, attackers register or edit a local account using the victim's email, causing the victim's first OIDC login to link into the attacker-controlled account and expose their data.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/agents/actions/:agent_id in api/server/routes/agents/actions.js loads an existing action with owner credentials and merges editor-controlled metadata.domain and metadata.raw_spec while preserving metadata.api_key and related OAuth client secrets. A collaborator with EDIT permission can repoint an action to an attacker-controlled host, and a later tool invocation decrypts and sends the retained owner credential to that destination. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.1.0 until 4.5.2, get_eacontent in libatalk/vfs/ea_ad.c subtracts MAX_REPLY_EXTRA_BYTES from a client-controlled FPGetExtAttr MaxReplySize without rejecting values from 1 through 5, and a signed-to-unsigned comparison can then select an untrusted AppleDouble ea_size. An authenticated client on a volume configured with ea = ad can use a pre-existing malformed AppleDouble sidecar to make read copy attacker-controlled bytes beyond dsi->data + 6 into the surrounding struct DSI, including protocol callback pointers. The malformed sidecar must already exist or be created through a separate local, co-export, management, restore, or vulnerability-assisted write path, and practical code execution depends on the target architecture, structure layout, and address uncertainty; runtime command execution was demonstrated on one x86-64 build. Volumes using ea = sys, ea = none, or ea = auto when it resolves to native system xattrs do not reach this path. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

A flaw was found in KubeVirt/containerized-data-importer. When a VirtualMachine with an embedded DataVolumeTemplate carrying the cdi.kubevirt.io/storage.checkStaticVolume annotation and a cross-namespace clone source is created by a tenant, the service-account clone authorization check can be bypassed, allowing a PVC from another namespace to be cloned into the tenant's namespace without the required permissions. This can result in cross-tenant data disclosure.

Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, a BASIC application user, or an unauthenticated visitor to a public write form, can store markup in a shared external datasource that a builder or administrator later evaluates in any Handlebars binding Preview that surfaces the value, including the Data-section Formula column editor or any binding drawer. jsonFormatter.format() in packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts leaves raw strings and object keys unescaped, while packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte inserts the formatted result as raw HTML. The Handlebars SafeString path preserves the attacker-controlled value, and the Builder origin lacks a Content-Security-Policy that would block the resulting script. This permits stored script execution in the higher-privileged builder or administrator session rather than the writer's own role, allowing privileged Builder API actions and workspace data access. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. When a TokenRateLimitPolicy is attached to an HTTPRoute that also has an AuthPolicy - or when a RateLimitPolicy with defaults or overrides is attached to the Gateway or listener of such routes - the shim's action pipeline fails to dispatch the authentication guard at request time, and the request is forwarded upstream. Unauthenticated requests return 200 OK instead of 401, and neither authentication nor rate limiting is enforced. Both policies continue to report Enforced, leaving no status-level indication of the failure.

A hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability exists in affected Ethernet swiches. The use of a shared cryptographic key with insufficient key strength could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker, under certain conditions, to impersonate affected devices and potentially compromise the confidentiality and integrity of communications.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could cause Splunk SOAR to send a stored Elasticsearch password to a host that the user controls.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR reuses a stored Elasticsearch password for a changed Search Settings endpoint without requiring a replacement password.

A missing authorization vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's legacy system settings configuration handler allows a low-privileged authenticated user to execute arbitrary commands with elevated privileges on the underlying OS.

PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2 missing authorization allowed project developers to read arbitrary HashiCorp Vault secrets
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2, 2026.1.6 vCS root credentials could be exposed via change viewer links
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1 missing authorization allowed project viewers to download project settings
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 access keys of parent project AWS connections could be disclosed
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 improper authorization allowed publishing packages to NuGet feeds of other projects
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 improper authorization allowed access to credentials of other projects via build configuration settings
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 an SSRF in AWS connection settings could expose server credentials
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 an SSRF via pipeline repository branch listing was possible

A security vulnerability has been detected in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file mainfunction.cgi of the component Apmcfg Upload. The manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 addresses this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware. Prior to 0.9.0, the ModelReconciler accepts arbitrary absolute paths and file:// URIs in Model.spec.source without restricting them to approved roots. A namespace user who can create or update Model and InferenceService resources can cause copyLocalModel to open an attacker-selected file in the controller pod or cause a HostPathVolumeSource to mount an attacker-selected node file when modelCache.enabled is enabled, which is the default. The selected file is copied into model storage and can expose controller service-account credentials or other node secrets outside the attacker's namespace. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 XXE via Maven settings file upload was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.8 disclosure of password parameter values to project viewers was possible
Tanium addressed an improper input validation vulnerability in Threat Response.

Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 serves page media files, and rendered pages when lazy sessions are enabled, with the visitor's session cookie and a shared-cacheable Cache-Control header. When a shared cache such as Apache mod_cache stores Set-Cookie responses, an attacker can lure a user signed in through the front-end login to open a media URL with a unique query string, then request that URL to receive the cached session cookie and take over the session.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Rymera Web Co Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce woo-product-feed-pro allows Path Traversal.This issue affects Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce: from n/a through 13.5.8.

A server-side request forgery vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed an authenticated user with repository write access to send requests to internal services through Slack webhook validity checks, potentially leading to remote code execution on the appliance. Exploitation required Secret Protection with secret scanning and validity checks for partner patterns enabled. This vulnerability affected all versions prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, and 3.20.12. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

Improper Access Control vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki - OATHAuth Extension. This vulnerability is associated with program files src/Auth/ReauthPrimaryAuthenticationProvider.php, src/Auth/SecondaryAuthenticationProvider.php. This issue affects MediaWiki - OATHAuth Extension: 1.47.

Joomla! Core - [20261141] - Core - XSS in com_installer changelog in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inadequate filtering of remote extension changelog contents leads to an XSS vulnerability in the changelog view.

Joomla! Core - [20261140] - Core - XSS in joomla-dialog header in Joomla 5.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inadequate escaping of the dialog header text leads to an XSS vulnerability in the extension changelog dialog.

Joomla! Core - [20261128] - Core - XSS in com_installer language installation view in Joomla 2.5.7-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inadequate escaping of the language update feed metadata leads to an XSS vulnerability in the language installation view.
SUSE Neuvector before 5.5, 5.5.0 before 5.5.6 and 5.6.0 before 5.6.5 handling of ephemeral containers was not setting some checking callbacks, allowing these to bypass permission checks.

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex_aws (instance metadata token provider).

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/instance_meta_token_provider.ex and program routines ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.request_token/1 and ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.get/1.

ex_aws requests its IMDSv2 session token from the link-local metadata endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) with HTTP redirect following enabled. Because the token request follows 3xx redirects and does not restrict the redirect target to the link-local range, an attacker who can influence the response to the metadata request (for example an on-segment neighbor spoofing the link-local address) can answer with a redirect to an arbitrary host. The library follows the redirect and accepts the arbitrary host's response body as the IMDSv2 session token, caching it and sending it as the x-aws-ec2-metadata-token header on every subsequent metadata and credential request.

This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.3.0 before 2.8.0.

DreameHome for Android (com.dreame.smartlife) before 2.6.4.0 contains a download of code without integrity check vulnerability in RnPluginDownloadManager.java that allows network-positioned attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript within the application by replacing React Native feature bundles that are only validated against a client-stored MD5 checksum without publisher authentication. Attackers can replace both the downloaded bundle and its corresponding MD5 metadata to run modified code with the application's permissions and access to its bridge APIs.

Convoy before 26.6.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in /portal-api single-resource handlers that allows portal link token holders to access other tenants' resources by ID. Attackers with another tenant's resource IDs in the same project can read endpoint signing secrets and webhook payloads, rotate secrets, pause or delete endpoints, and force event re-delivery.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an Improper Input Validation vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to a denial of service condition.

Umami 3.3.0 before 3.5.0 contains a race condition in two-factor authentication attempt limiting that allows attackers holding a user's password to bypass lockout. Attackers can send many concurrent POST requests to /api/2fa/verify that pass checkRateLimit before recordFailedAttempt runs, brute-forcing TOTP or backup codes beyond the five-attempt limit.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to evade stricter ProxyAuth domain rules by sending percent-encoded path separators. Attackers can request paths with encoded slashes, backslashes, semicolons, or dot segments that match a broader rule, reaching restricted paths once the reverse proxy or backend decodes them.

Better Auth (better-auth, @better-auth/kysely-adapter, and @better-auth/drizzle-adapter) before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition with MySQL or MariaDB serial IDs because the inserted row's ID is read via a separate LAST_INSERT_ID() query that may run on a different pooled connection. Under concurrent load, a user signing in can receive another user's session and act as that user.

better-auth 1.3.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the admin plugin's /admin/update-user endpoint that lets roles holding user:update change another user's phoneNumber and phoneNumberVerified fields. Attackers can set their own verified phone number on a higher-privileged account and sign in via phone OTP to take it over.

U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program allows attackers with valid local application credentials to establish an application session by sending JSON POST requests to the application's login endpoint without a Referrer header or completing the intended Keycloak flow. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

SportEase is a web application for managing school sports events, class rosters, and competition teams. Prior to 1.3, an authenticated account with is_profile_complete=false can submit an attacker-selected class_id for any class in the currently active event to PUT /api/user/profile during first profile completion. AuthHandler.UpdateProfile accepts the class without validating the user's legitimate membership and automatically derives and assigns the corresponding {class_name}_rep role while isFirstCompletion is true. The attacker can become representative of one selected class, view roster information including email addresses, and add or remove competition-team assignments. Downstream handlers correctly reject access to other classes, so the impact is bounded to the selected class, but the representative privilege cannot be revoked through the exposed API and requires direct database intervention or another out-of-band remediation method. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes. An attacker who knows the password of a user who has enrolled a second factor can skip the second factor and call PEM's pages and APIs directly, with that user's permissions. A similar issue in pgAdmin 4 was assigned CVE-2024-4215.
From PEM 10.6.1, every authenticated PEM route requires a completed MFA check.

Hanko before 3.2.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability in Saml.IsAllowedRedirect that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the redirect allowlist by appending attacker-controlled domain suffixes to allowed hostnames. Attackers can lure victims through a crafted /saml/auth login link to capture the one-time hanko_token and redeem it without PKCE to hijack the victim's session.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view an affected container could query the Representational State Transfer (REST) API for approvals to retrieve a live external prompt link belonging to another user. Using this link, the user could read the approval prompt without authentication and submit a response, potentially disrupting or altering the automated workflow governed by that approval.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API for approvals exposes the live external prompt link without verifying that the requester owns the approval.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared dashboard. The malicious SPL could run using the permissions of the user who opened the dashboard and could access or modify data available to that user and disrupt Splunk Enterprise availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not preserve quoted search argument boundaries when it processes a dashboard search.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role, should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could add attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) to a shared dashboard. When another user opens the dashboard in Splunk Web, Splunk Enterprise could run the attacker-controlled SPL using the permissions of that dashboard viewer. The attacker-controlled SPL could expose stored credentials, modify indexed data, and reduce availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize special elements in search filter values before it builds optimized search jobs.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could craft a shared Classic Dashboard that runs arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands for another authenticated user. Exploitation requires the dashboard viewer to open the shared dashboard. The injected commands could access data available to the dashboard viewer, modify data available to the dashboard viewer, and partially disrupt Splunk Enterprise.
For more information see Add sparklines to search results (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.6/calculate-statistics/add-sparklines-to-search-results), Configure dashboard permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/simple-xml-dashboards/10.6/manage-and-share-dashboards/configure-dashboard-permissions), and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could create and share a metric alert that causes Analytics Workspace to run a malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) when another authenticated user opens a link to the alert. The malicious SPL could expose data, modify data, or disrupt services available in the affected session. 
The vulnerability is possible because Analytics Workspace does not fully neutralize metric alert names before including the names in SPL.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The user who holds the "power" Splunk role should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Alerts in the Analytics Workspace (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/analytics-workspace/10.4/using-the-analytics-workspace/alerts-in-the-analytics-workspace) and Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS may forward a Cookie header after an HTTP redirect to a host other than the one for which the header was intended. That unintended host can therefore receive cookies containing credentials or other confidential values. Authorization headers are never forwarded to inappropriate hosts and are not the affected secret in this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not format the SSH URL path component as a single argument when constructing remote object-transfer or authentication commands. Shell metacharacters in the SSH URL can therefore escape the intended path argument and cause arbitrary command execution when the remote Git LFS service passes received commands to a shell without adequate sanitization. Git LFS also incorrectly encodes default HTTPS URLs when an SSH URL is configured and the remote host either does not support Git LFS remote commands over SSH or supports HTTP authentication over SSH but git-lfs-authenticate does not return an explicit HTTP URL. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

When the setting for saving requests to non-existent
pages (404) is enabled, JTL-Shop stores the raw requested URL in its
redirect table, and the administration backend renders it without output
encoding in the form used to edit a redirect. An unauthenticated remote
attacker can store script code with a single request, which is executed in the
browser session of an administrator who opens the affected redirect,
allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges. The
setting is disabled by default in new installations but may still be
enabled in older ones.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the OCPP backend settings interface. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29056.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP backend configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29063.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2, 2026.1.6 an XXE was possible in the TFS helper process
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on build and queue pages was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the AWS Credentials build feature was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the NPM Registry build feature was possible
IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to a server-side request forgery.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS on the Docker Container Info tab was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS in the Promote build dialog was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 missing authorization in the Kubernetes integration allowed project viewers to use stored credentials

NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

NocoDB before 2026.04.1 fails to clear reset_password_token and reset_password_expires in users.service.ts when a password is changed, leaving earlier reset links valid. Attackers holding an unexpired reset link, such as from prior mailbox access, can set a new password and regain control of the account.

In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow
.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger
while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a
pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository
context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write,
pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token
exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub
Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

GNU Inetutils FTP Client File Retrieval Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of GNU Inetutils FTP Client. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must interact with a malicious FTP server.

The specific flaw exists within the processing of filenames. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current user. Was ZDI-CAN-29119.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.11.1 before 0.11.3, anyone with an Exa Search Monitor trigger's URL can start one run of the owner's workflow per request with fake event data, even when a secret is set. The workflow runs with the owner's saved credentials and credits, and nothing is returned to the attacker. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

A flaw was found in rsyslog. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can trigger a stack-based buffer overflow by sending a malformed log message containing an embedded IPv4-in-IPv6 address to an instance configured with the mmanon anonymization module. This flaw causes the logging service to crash, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

In Valkey 8.0.x before 8.0.11, 8.1.x before 8.1.10, 9.0.x before 9.0.6 and 9.1.x before 9.1.2, the RDMA transport's pending-data handler walks its connection list with an iterator that caches the next entry. A command processed from inside that loop, such as CLIENT KILL, can synchronously free another client's connection, and closing an RDMA connection did not remove it from the pending list, so the handler then uses freed memory. An authenticated user can use this to reliably crash the server, and the freed heap chunk can be reclaimed with attacker-influenced bytes. Only servers built with RDMA support (USE_RDMA) and configured with an RDMA listener are affected.
Race condition in the Graphics component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.
Race condition in the Networking: HTTP component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161, and Thunderbird 153.8.

In Valkey before 7.2.16, 8.0.x before 8.0.13, 8.1.x before 8.1.12, 9.0.x before 9.0.8, 9.1.x before 9.1.4 and 9.2.0 release candidates, when client eviction is enabled (maxmemory-clients is not 0), an authenticated user who can write to a key that other clients are blocked on (for example with BLPOP, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN or XREAD BLOCK) can trigger a use-after-free. While the clients blocked on that key are served, evictClients() can select and free the client whose command made the key ready, although that command is still executing, and the server then keeps using the freed client. The blocked clients do not have to belong to the attacker. The result is a reliable crash of the server process. Servers with the default maxmemory-clients 0 are not affected.

Server-Side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Server Side Request Forgery.

This issue affects vSRM: from 14.08.1 before 14.08.3.
Various memory-safety issues in dataplane of SUSE Neuvector before 5.5, 5.5.0 before 5.5.6, 5.6.0 before 5.6.5 could be used by remote attackers to trigger crashes.
Tanium addressed a path traversal vulnerability in Core Content.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.3.1, the Mollie payment notification handler in src/Payments/Mollie.php, processNotifyUrl(), uses a payment ID supplied with the notification to retrieve a paid transaction but does not verify that the transaction's order reference matches the order identified by the notification URL or that the transaction amount matches the order total. An ordinary customer can use a paid Mollie transaction from one order to cause a different, higher-value order to be marked paid without paying its full price. The endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated so Mollie's servers can reach it, and the request's order hash alone does not bind the fetched payment to that order. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.1.

n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Prior to 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2, the password reset link and role change operations do not protect the instance owner account from users with a custom instance role. A user whose custom instance role includes user management permissions can obtain a password reset link for the owner and take over the owner account, or change the owner's role, gaining full control of the instance. Exploitation requires the custom roles feature and a custom instance role with user management permissions. This issue is fixed in versions 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2.

A flaw was found in rsyslog. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted log message with an unusual timestamp. When the service processes this message using weekday formatting templates, an out-of-bounds memory read occurs, causing the application to crash.
Improper certificate validation in Microsoft Office PowerPoint allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

A buffer over-read vulnerability in Elasticsearch transport decompression can expose data from other requests. The LZ4 decoder can read beyond the declared compressed block into a shared network buffer. A remote attacker who can reach an affected transport interface can send a specially crafted compressed request and obtain data from outside their own request. Exploitation of the exposed remote-cluster transport interface does not require authentication.

In HttpFileRequestHandler::GetFilePath of http_file_request_handler.cc, there is a possible path traversal due to improper input validation. This could lead to remote information disclosure with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, uses unqualified operators and functions in the catalog queries of DatabaseMetaData, ResultSetMetaData and TypeInfoCache. A role with CREATE on a schema of the application's search_path can add an operator with an exact type match, and the server runs it with the privileges of the application's role. TypeInfoCache also resolves an unqualified type name such as interval by its own ranking. A domain with that name in another schema, even the temporary schema of another session, can be used instead, and its CHECK runs in the application's session. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not close the connection when an unchecked exception interrupts a request. Part of a Bind message stays in the send buffer, and the server reads the bytes that follow as the rest of it. The bytes of a value uploaded later on the same connection can then run as a SQL command. Since 42.6.0 a setBinaryStream() value without a length that is executed again throws such an exception, as does the driver's own retry after SQLState 0A000 or 26000. An application stream that throws an unchecked exception has the same effect in all versions. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains a heap based buffer overflow. An unauthenticated remote attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to a denial of service condition.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains a null pointer dereference vulnerability. An unauthenticated remote attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to a denial of service condition.

TypesenseFilterExpressionConverter does not correctly translate grouped (parenthesized) filter expressions into the Typesense filter syntax.



As a result, the filter sent to Typesense can have a different meaning than the one the application defined, and some conditions may not be applied as intended.



 An application is affected if it uses the Typesense vector store with filter expressions that contain groups and relies on them to restrict results, for example to enforce tenant isolation or access control.



In that case, a remote user may be able to retrieve documents they should not have access to, and the same filter used for a delete operation may remove documents outside the intended scope.

An arbitrary file read vulnerability was discovered in debbugs, a bug tracking system based on the active Debian BTS. versions.cgi failed to correctly sanitize package name inputs in found

and fixed query parameters. Crafted query parameters could cause version.cgi to output any lines of the target file which contained spaces.
Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in myCred myCred mycred allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects myCred: from n/a through 4.0.3.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Aguila Technologies WP Customer Area customer-area allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Customer Area: from n/a through 8.4.5.
Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in Liquid Web / StellarWP BookIt bookit allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects BookIt: from n/a through 2.6.0.8.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in Metagauss ProfileGrid profilegrid-user-profiles-groups-and-communities allows Blind SQL Injection.This issue affects ProfileGrid: from n/a through 6.0.0.6.

The One to one user Chat by WPGuppy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'userId' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.6 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The plugin's permission callback is trivially bypassed because it validates a JWT that the plugin itself signs using an attacker-supplied value from the guppy_guest_account cookie, and the guest code path (userType=0) skips the get_userdata() check that would confirm the userId corresponds to a real WordPress user.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 4.4.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a WCS GetCoverage XML POST request whose BoundingBox element omits the crs attribute, causing xmlGetProp() in src/mapwcs.cpp to return null. msWCSParseRequest() then calls string functions on the null value before normal WCS exception handling, crashing the CGI or FastCGI worker. The analogous KVP or GET path is not affected because it obtains a count-validated, non-null token. A single request can terminate one worker, and repeated requests can exhaust a fixed worker pool and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.00, a network attacker who can alter outbound traffic to the extension store can exploit the HTTP client's disabled sslverify setting to substitute a serialized response. Extension-store handlers pass the response to unserialize() without an allowed_classes restriction, allowing an in-tree GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget to write attacker-controlled content to a chosen path. When a GODADMIN opens or uses the store list, detail, install, or update functions, the substituted response can write a PHP file under the web root and execute code as the web-server user. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.00.

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in Datasolution AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter acymailing allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter: from n/a through 11.1.0.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c interprets the dsi_code and dsi_doff union field as a data offset for all DSI command types instead of limiting that interpretation to DSIWrite. An unauthenticated client can send a non-WRITE DSIFUNC_CMD packet with a nonzero dsi_code smaller than dsi_len, causing dsi_stream_receive to consume only the dsi_code number of payload bytes and leave attacker-controlled bytes in the readahead buffer. The residual bytes become the next DSI header, allowing protocol desynchronization that can close sessions, corrupt protocol state, or trigger an infinite-read denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

A flaw was found in dnsmasq, where a memory handling issue exists in its Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv6 (DHCPv6) relay processing. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a sequence of network packets to a system configured as a DHCPv6 relay. This causes the service to write data to previously freed memory and crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

svglib reads SVG files and converts them to other formats. Prior to 2.3.1, the svg2rlg() renderer recursively expands nested SVG <use> references by deep-copying each referenced subtree; SvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py calls xlink_href_target(), which rejects direct cycles but permits acyclic reference graphs with repeated fan-out. A small attacker-controlled SVG can therefore trigger exponentially increasing node expansion, consuming excessive CPU and memory in any application that renders it without a non-default option; HTML-to-PDF workflows using xhtml2pdf can reach the same renderer when an embedded data:image/svg+xml image in an HTML img element is passed to pisa.CreatePDF(). This issue is fixed in 2.3.1.

Joomla Extension - phoca.cz - Stored XSS through author website in frontend upload in Phoca Download extension 3.0.6-6.1.6 - The author website field of the frontend upload form was validated with an overly permissive URL check and rendered without escaping, allowing users with frontend upload permission to inject HTML attributes into the file and category views.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in RomanCode MapSVG mapsvg-lite-interactive-vector-maps allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects MapSVG: from n/a through 9.0.5.

The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion via Path Traversal in versions up to, and including, 2.4.8 via the `file_path` column handled by the `mbw_board_files_api_body()` function. The plugin stores an attacker-supplied value directly into the files admin table (no realpath, dot-segment, or directory-containment filtering) and later concatenates it onto `MBW_UPLOAD_PATH` before passing the result to `@unlink()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server, including `wp-config.

The VidShop for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including, 1.10.0 via the /vsfw/v1/products/{id} REST API endpoint. This is due to the endpoint's permission_callback (check_public_permission) returning true unconditionally and the get_item() handler only checking that the product and video exist — it does not check the product's post_status or catalog visibility, nor does it verify that the product is actually linked to the supplied video_id. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to enumerate product IDs and read private, draft, and catalog-hidden WooCommerce products' names, short descriptions, prices, variations, attributes, and stock information that would otherwise be hidden from public view.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Backup For WP WP Database Backup wp-database-backup allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Database Backup: from n/a through 7.14.
Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in weDevs WP ERP erp allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects WP ERP: from n/a through 1.17.11.
Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in ReviewX ReviewX reviewx allows XML Entity Linking.This issue affects ReviewX: from n/a through 3.0.1.

The rtMedia for WordPress, BuddyPress and bbPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'custom_fields' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.7.17 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The upload endpoint's only access control is a nonce check, and the 'rtmedia_upload_nonce' value is localized to every unauthenticated visitor on every front-end page via wp_enqueue_scripts, making it freely obtainable without an account.

The King Addons for Elementor – 100+ Elementor Widgets, 4 000+ Elementor Templates, WooCommerce Builder, Mega Menu, Popup Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 51.1.89. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary post meta values — including private contact data, API keys, license keys, and plugin-internal metadata — for any published post by supplying an arbitrary meta key name via the unauthenticated AJAX endpoint. The nonce check present in the handler provides no effective barrier because the nonce is emitted into every front-end page for logged-out visitors via wp_localize_script.

The Lightbox with PhotoSwipe WordPress plugin before 5.19.0 does not escape image link URLs before outputting them in the attributes of the lightbox share menu, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks via comments when the PhotoSwipe 4 frontend is used.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding.

The content of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER or RELATIVE-OID element is passed to unpack "w*" on decode, and the arcs of an OID string to pack "w*" on encode. Perl converts each arc to or from its decimal string in time quadratic in the arc's length, and nothing limits that length.

An attacker who controls the decoded data, or an OID string passed to encode, can exhaust CPU with a single oversized arc.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get.

The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB.

A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding.

Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content.

A BIT STRING with zero content octets passes -1 to substr as the length. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the decoded value is nearly all of the input that follows the element. In the constructed form each zero-length segment copies the rest of the input again, so memory grows with the square of the input size.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a short constructed BIT STRING. The resulting value also contains bytes from adjacent input.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding.

The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size.

An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding.

Binary REAL decoding never bounds-checks the exponent length against the available content. For a minimal one-byte binary REAL, the exponent byte is read from outside the element, making the mantissa length -1. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the mantissa is nearly all of the input that follows the element. The long-form exponent path also omits the extra length octet when sizing the mantissa.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a list of such values, as each mantissa loop iterates over the remaining input. The decoded values are also computed from bytes outside each element.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv.

asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. An inverted boolean guard ($tb || rather than $tb &&) prevents the need-more-data exit from firing once a tag byte has been decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles.

A single truncated BER header sent to a process calling asn_recv doubles the peek buffer until memory is exhausted. Perl's realloc failure is fatal and not catchable with eval.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip.

Every INTEGER or ENUMERATED longer than four content octets reaches os2ip, which iterates over each content octet with $result = ($result * 256) + $octet. Each multiplication operates on a bigint that grows by one octet per step, so decoding an n-octet value takes O(n^2) bigint work. Nothing limits content length before this loop runs.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized INTEGER or ENUMERATED value.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.
