In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, an unauthenticated user who can reach the Splunk App for Stream Representational State Transfer (REST) API on the management port (8089) could upload an Extensible Markup Language (XML) vocabulary file, which lets the vocabulary upload endpoint read local files accessible to the Splunk process or send outbound requests.
The vulnerability is possible because the vocabulary upload endpoint parses uploaded XML without an application-level policy that blocks external entity resolution.
For more information see About Splunk Stream (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.1/introduction/about-splunk-stream) and restmap.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.3-configuration-file-reference/restmap.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an unauthenticated user could gain administrator privileges through a user account that receives an unintended role. A user that holds a role with permission to create or modify users and assign roles must assign the target account a role with a numeric name through the user-management Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the API resolves a numeric role name as a role identifier instead of preserving the requested role name.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user who can connect to a Splunk-to-Splunk (S2S) data forwarding receiver could cause the Splunk daemon to terminate unexpectedly. The unexpected termination interrupts data indexing and access to the management API and Splunk Web until the Splunk Enterprise process restarts.
The vulnerability is possible because the S2S data forwarding receiver does not validate an optional field in forwarded event data, which results in a null pointer dereference when the field is missing.
For more information see Intermediate data routing using universal and heavy forwarders (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/get-started/splunk-validated-architectures/getting-data-in-forwarding-and-preprocessing/intermediate-data-routing-using-universal-and-heavy-forwarders) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could access live event data from the indexing pipeline through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API on a standalone instance or a search head that is not an indexer cluster member.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts an empty shared key during service authentication.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could access RapidDiag process metadata and log file inventory information through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because certain RapidDiag REST API endpoints accept a factory-default shared key for node authentication, which lets requests bypass Splunk user authentication.
For more information see Using RapidDiag (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/troubleshoot/9.0/contact-splunk-support/using-rapiddiag) and Secure Splunk Enterprise services with pass4SymmKey (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.0/secure-distributed-and-clustered-splunk-environments/secure-splunk-enterprise-services-with-pass4symmkey) in the Splunk documentation.

aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.12.1, the QoS 2 transaction handler in amqtt/mqtt/protocol/handler.py, _handle_qos2_message_flow(), can retain transaction state and packet identifiers when a client disconnects before the handshake completes, unlike QoS 1 flows that expire after the default five-second timeout. A remote client can repeatedly begin QoS 2 flows and disconnect without maintaining long-lived connections; anonymous clients can do this with the default configuration, while authenticated deployments remain affected when a client may initiate QoS 2 flows. The retained state grows broker memory until resource exhaustion can terminate the process; no confidentiality or integrity impact is identified. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.1.

Go-Guerrilla SMTP Daemon is a lightweight SMTP server written in Go. In 1.6.7 and earlier, according to the repository advisory's structured affected range, server.go defines the seven-byte cmdXCLIENT token, but the XCLIENT handler slices input[8:] after matching only that seven-byte verb, so a bare command causes an out-of-bounds panic in handleClient and terminates the daemon because that connection goroutine does not recover the panic. The issue is reachable by an unauthenticated client when the non-default xclient_on setting is enabled; no HELO command is required. The repository fix is present in version 1.6.7-1.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade that is pipelined behind another HTTP request on the same cleartext connection arrives while that request's response is still attached to the socket. The shared upgrade listener sees the socket is already claimed and returns early without taking the upgrade, but it does not attach an error listener to the raw socket, and Node.js has already removed its own error listener before emitting the upgrade event. A later socket error on that connection, such as a client connection reset, is therefore unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. A single unauthenticated connection that pipelines an upgrade behind a normal request and then resets is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. Upgrades over TLS are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, an attacker who controls an upstream RPM repository mirrored by a RepoManager instance can provide a package filename through the primary.xml <location href> field; the mirror passes that filename into a shell-interpreted RPM query, allowing shell metacharacters to execute commands as the www-data service account. The target must mirror an upstream repository controlled by the attacker, and the default "Check GPG signatures" option triggers the vulnerable call. The command executes before a later signature-verification failure, so a valid signed package is not required. Fixed in 5.13.3.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

Joomla Extension - phoca.cz - Stored XSS through YouTube links in Phoca Gallery extension 4.2.0-6.1.6 - The YouTube upload feature did not validate the supplied video URL and embedded the derived video ID without escaping, allowing users with frontend upload permission to inject HTML attributes into the gallery detail view.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, DependencyGraph.tree and DependencyGraph.triples walk parsed dependency edges through unbounded Python recursion and do not use a working cycle or depth guard. A crafted CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency file containing a sufficiently long chain can raise RecursionError when the documented traversal APIs are called, aborting the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.

A flaw was found in Moodle's external database enrolment plugin. Insufficient sanitization of data passed to queries against the external database allows an authenticated user with course editing permissions to perform a Structured Query Language (SQL) injection attack. When this non-default plugin is enabled, an attacker can exploit this issue to view, modify, or delete sensitive records within the connected external database.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP UpdateFirmware requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29487.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A FTP URL Path Parsing Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of FTP URL paths during firmware updates. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28960.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Download of Code Without Integrity Check Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. The issue results from the lack of proper verification of firmware integrity prior to installation. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28957.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP GetConfiguration Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. When parsing GetConfiguration requests, the process does not properly validate the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28968.
In JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.6.29 files outside the project directory could be modified by agent file tools

### Summary ui

With `strip_ansi=True`, Pydantic AI Harness's `ToolOutputLimits` capability removes ANSI escape sequences from tool output with a pattern that takes time quadratic in the length of a line. A tool result of a few hundred kilobytes, crafted with many unterminated escape sequences, can occupy the event loop for tens of seconds to minutes, delaying every other request and agent run in the process.

### Details

This affects applications that set `strip_ansi=True` on `ToolOutputLimits` (named `OverflowingToolOutput` before 0.13.0) and run tools whose output an attacker can influence, such as shell commands, file reads, fetched pages or MCP servers. Stripping runs on the event loop before the capability reduces the output, so its own size limits do not bound it.

The assumed attacker can place text in content a tool returns.

### Mitigation

Upgrade `pydantic-ai-harness` to 0.70.0 or later. Until then, leave `strip_ansi` at its default, `False`.

On Pydantic AI v1, the harness cannot be upgraded past 0.4.0. Upgrade to Pydantic AI v2 and `pydantic-ai-harness` 0.70.0, or leave `strip_ansi` off.

The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in versions up to, and including, 1.1.11. This is due to a missing capability check and missing nonce check on the start_zip_creation, start_zip_download, local_sync_get_init_root_files, and local_sync_get_files_by_key AJAX actions in the start_zip_creation_dev() and sibling functions. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite the plugin's prod_site_url setting so it points at an attacker-controlled host and enumerate arbitrary server directories, which when combined with a subsequent administrator-triggered sync results in an unsigned attacker-supplied ZIP archive being fetched, extracted via a WordPress-independent bridge deployed under the web root, resulting in remote code execution on the affected site.

The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the 'file_name' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The authentication bypass requires submitting the JSON boolean `true` as the `prod_key_random_id` value, which coerces against any non-empty stored secret so that the loose `!=` comparison evaluates to false, skipping the rejection branch entirely without knowledge of the secret.

Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere vulnerability in Mamunur Rashid ShopBuilder – Elementor WooCommerce Builder Addons shopbuilder allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects ShopBuilder – Elementor WooCommerce Builder Addons: from n/a through 3.4.3.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Deepen Bajracharya Video Conferencing with Zoom video-conferencing-with-zoom-api allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Video Conferencing with Zoom: from n/a through 4.6.12.

The AppPresser  WordPress plugin before 5.0.0 does not properly escape the contents of its debug log when displaying it in the admin dashboard, and decodes escape sequences after sanitising input, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored XSS attacks against administrators when debug logging is enabled.

Axon is an agent-agnostic context engine that gives AI coding agents continuous memory across sessions, tools, and machines. Prior to 0.1.1, rtk-install in src/axon/context/rtk_bootstrap.py uses _http_download() to fetch a prebuilt rtkx release archive and _extract_binary() to mark it executable, after which compress_text_with_rtk() invokes it without verifying a checksum, signature, or build attestation. If the sammyjdev/rtkx release pipeline or maintainer release credentials are compromised, an attacker can supply a modified binary that executes with the Axon process privileges when a user installs or automatically bootstraps rtkx. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.1.

yt-mcp is a YouTrack MCP server for Claude Code. Prior to 1.18.1, add_attachment in src/yt_mcp/tools/attachments.py accepts a caller-controlled file_path, checks only that the file exists, reads it without directory confinement, and uploads the bytes to a YouTrack issue. A compromised MCP client or an LLM steered by indirect prompt injection can read any file accessible to the server process and exfiltrate secrets through an issue the caller can access. The same release also permits get_project_health to interpolate a caller-controlled project value into snapshot filenames, allowing parent-directory traversal to write JSON files outside the snapshots directory. This issue is fixed in version 1.18.1.

PGPainless is a simple-to-use OpenPGP API based on Bouncy Castle. Prior to 1.7.8 and from 2.0.0 until 2.0.4, pgpainless-sop/src/main/kotlin/org/pgpainless/sop/InlineDetachImpl.kt InlineDetachImpl and pgpainless-core/src/main/kotlin/org/pgpainless/decryption_verification/MessageInspector.kt MessageInspector manually descend PGPCompressedData packets without incrementing or enforcing MAX_LAYER_DEPTH. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply an untrusted OpenPGP message containing deeply nested compressed packet structures to a downstream application using inline-detach or message inspection, bypass the intended 16-layer limit, and force continued decompression and packet processing. The resulting resource consumption can block processing threads, exhaust heap memory, and crash the consuming application. This issue is fixed in versions 1.7.8 and 2.0.4.

OpenID4VP is an open-source credential parsing library for SD-JWT VC and mDOC/mDL formats. Prior to 0.8.1, src/trust/ChainBuilder.ts ChainBuilder.tryBuild() terminates chain construction when an attacker-controlled certificate Subject Distinguished Name equals a trusted anchor subject, without verifying cryptographic closure to the anchor public key. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply a self-signed leaf or intermediate that reuses the trusted Subject Distinguished Name and have credentials signed by the attacker key accepted as issued by the trusted authority. The public src/trust/TrustEvaluator.ts TrustEvaluator.evaluate() path compounds the error by matching a terminus through serialNumber and falling back to anchors[0], which can attribute the forged chain to genuine trusted-authority metadata. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.1.

SharpIppNext is a .NET Standard library for building Internet Printing Protocol clients and servers. Prior to 4.1.0, server-side SharpIppNext implementations using SharpIppServer.ReceiveRequestAsync or SharpIppServer.ReceiveRawRequestAsync pass incoming data to IppProtocol.ReadIppRequestAsync in SharpIpp/Protocol/IppProtocol.cs, where ReadDocumentStream is enabled by default and the remaining document body is copied with CopyToAsync into a MemoryStream without a size limit. An unauthenticated remote client can send an arbitrarily large IPP document body, exhausting process memory and causing an out-of-memory failure or service termination. Client-only implementations using SharpIppClient are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.0.

install-artifact-from-github installs prebuilt native artifacts hosted by GitHub without compiling them locally. Prior to 1.7.0, bin/install-from-cache.js downloads a native .node artifact, allows RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR to select a source, follows HTTP redirects including HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrades, and writes the decompressed response to the artifact path without cryptographic integrity verification before writing or loading it. An attacker who controls a configured mirror, replaces a release asset, or can modify plaintext transport can supply native code that executes when the consumer loads the artifact. Version 1.7.0 adds SHA-256 verification for default-GitHub-source downloads when the consuming package publishes an artifactHashes bag; configured mirrors and packages without a bag remain outside that verification.

ALTCHA PHP is a lightweight PHP library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when a challenge payload omits the signature field, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker can remove the signature, supply attacker-selected low-difficulty challenge parameters, solve the resulting proof of work, and submit a payload that verifies successfully, bypassing the CAPTCHA control. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System V2.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because database backup files are stored within the publicly accessible web root. An unauthenticated remote attacker can download the SQL backup files and retrieve sensitive database contents, including employee personally identifiable information and password hashes.

A vulnerability in the eXtensible ARchive (XAR) GZIP file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to exceed the configured MaxFileSize and cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to inefficiencies when parsing specifically formatted files with the XAR GZIP file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted XAR GZIP file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to effectively cause the ClamAV to exceed the MaxFileSize and potentially get caught in an infinite loop, causing a DoS condition.

A vulnerability in the Object Linking and Embedding, 2nd Generation (OLE2) file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to exceed the configured MaxScanTime and cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to inefficiencies when parsing specifically formatted files with the OLE2 file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted Microsoft Compound File Binary (CFB) file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to effectively cause the ClamAV OLE2 parser to get into an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the Ultimate Packer for eXecutables (UPX) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.   This vulnerability is due to improper length checks, when unpacking the UPX files, which may result in an out-of-bounds read of heap memory. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted UPX for decode. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV decode process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the debug logging functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper handling of logging values. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a file to be scanned by the software that has debug logging enabled. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the LZX data algorithm for Microsoft Compiled HTML Help (CHM) file scanning in ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper boundary checks when applying the LZX data algorithm to CHM files during the decoder stage, which may result in buffer overflow. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted CHM file for scanning. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in Object Linking and Embedding, 2nd Generation (OLE2) file parser for ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to logic error when parsing specifically formatted files with the OLE2 file parser. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by by sending a crafted Microsoft Compound File Binary (CFB) file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to allocate all available memory, causing the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the InstallShield file parser of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to incomplete error checking when the InstallShield File Parser is performing a scan. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted InstallShield file to be scanned. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate due to an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the Yoda'a Crytper (yC) Portable Executable (PE) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. .
 This vulnerability is due to lack of proper error checking for negative values when processing the PE file to be unpacked. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a PE file to be unpacked. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in Microsoft Compiled HTML Help (CHM) file scanning of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to a logic error when scanning the CHM file and following the internal file pointers. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted CHM file for scanning. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV decode process to terminate due to an infinite loop, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the phishcheck functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper allocation of memory during processing of URLs. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a URL to be processed by the software. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 DoS via agent command results was possible

The Magic Login Mail or QR Code plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation via Administrator Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 2.07. This is due to the `curpageurl()` function falling back to the raw `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']` value — with no validation against the site's configured origin via `home_url()` or `site_url()` — when `get_the_permalink()` returns empty or false, allowing an attacker-controlled Host header to become the URL origin of the magic-login link generated by `generate_url()` and delivered to the target via `wp_mail()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to intercept the one-time uid and token pair sent to a targeted Administrator's email and replay them against the real site, causing `autologin_via_url()` to call `wp_set_auth_cookie()` and establish a full Administrator session on the targeted account. Exploitation requires the `[magic_login]` shortcode to render on a path where `get_the_permalink()` returns empty or false (such as a 404 page or a block-theme header template part), the web server to forward non-canonical Host headers, the attacker to know the target administrator's email address, and the administrator to click the attacker-originated magic-login link. Successful exploitation gives the attacker control of a distinct, already-privileged Administrator account; it does not promote the attacker's original account. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

tcp_pkt_linearize() in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c is used by th_get() whenever a received TCP header is not contiguous in a single net_buf. While pulling the header bytes out of the following fragments, the loop called net_buf_unref() on an emptied fragment without first detaching its frags pointer. net_buf_unref() walks the whole fragment list, so the payload buffers still linked behind that fragment were freed as well, and the stale pointer was then reinstalled into the packet as buf->frags, producing a use-after-free and a later double free during packet teardown. The same loop also advanced to second->frags unconditionally: when the fragment still held payload after the header remainder was pulled, it was spliced out of the packet without ever being unreferenced, permanently leaking that buffer and silently dropping the data it carried.

The defect is reached from tcp_recv() via th_get() on every received TCP segment, before connection lookup or any header validation, so a single unauthenticated segment that matches a listening socket is sufficient. An attacker only needs the TCP header to straddle a net_buf boundary, which they can arrange from off-link: IPv6 extension headers are accepted on receive and their length is added to the header offset by th_get(), so a Destination Options header of a suitable length places the TCP header across the boundary of the fixed-size receive buffers (CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE). Packet chains assembled from several sources - IPv4/IPv6 reassembly, 6LoWPAN/802.15.4 reassembly, tunnel or virtual interfaces that strip an outer header, or drivers producing scatter-gather chains - can additionally present a short interior fragment that the loop empties exactly, which is the case that frees the remainder of the packet while it is still in use.

The reliably reachable consequence is exhaustion of the receive buffer pool: each crafted segment leaks one net_buf from the fixed CONFIG_NET_BUF_RX_COUNT pool, the buffers are never reclaimed, and once the pool is empty the device can no longer receive network traffic until it is rebooted. Where a fragment is emptied exactly, the impact rises to memory corruption: freed pool buffers are written through by the remainder of the loop, their contents may be delivered to the application, and the packet is double-freed on teardown.

The fix saves and clears second->frags before the net_buf_unref() so only the emptied header fragment is released, and advances to the next fragment only when second->len == 0, keeping any fragment that still holds payload in the packet. This restores the detach-before-unref ownership pattern used elsewhere in the stack, for example in net_pkt_trim_buffer().
Tanium addressed an insertion of sensitive information into a log file vulnerability in TanOS.

The Team VCard generator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.0 via the 'photo' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 1.6 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, an MQTT v5.0 client connecting with a will-delay-interval that subsequently disconnects with a shorter interval causes all delayed wills to be suppressed.

An attacker that is able to send a crafted network packet to the affected component may trigger an integer overflow during module size validation. This may cause insufficient bounds checking and result in out-of-bounds memory reads, potentially leading to a denial of service condition due to process termination.

The rus to lat advanced plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to blind SQL Injection via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL
pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA
records.

Impact summary: The impact is limited to a client crash (potential Denial
of Service).

CWE: CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference

Description: A DANE-enabled TLS client that supports TLSA records with at
least one of the PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) usages alongside the DANE-TA(2)
usage may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer if the server claims a trusted
CA's certificate to be its end-entity certificate and has an unusual mix of
associated TLSA records.

DANE SMTP clients should not be affected since only the
DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) TLSA record usages are specified applicable
in SMTP.  For example, the Postfix MTA is not affected, while the Exim
MTA does not at present use OpenSSL's DANE implementation.

Use of DANE in validation of RFC7250 raw public keys (RPKs) is also
unaffected, as these only use DANE-EE(3) TLSA records.

Only applications that support combining the DANE PKI with a traditional PKI
are potentially affected.  A DANE-enabled browser or similar, that uses
OpenSSL's DANE API could be affected.

FIPS impact: no
The DANE API is outside the FIPS module boundary.

The AppPresser – Mobile App Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'appp_cam_file[name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.0 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Although the AJAX handler is registered for unauthenticated users, the only authorization gate is a nonce check, and the required nonce is only emitted to logged-in users viewing a page containing the [app-camera] shortcode, making Subscriber-level access the effective minimum requirement for exploitation.

Issue summary: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData
message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with
the square of the message size.

Impact summary: An attacker who can submit a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message
to an application that verifies it with CRL checking enabled can occupy a CPU
core for seconds to minutes, causing Denial of Service. Applications that
leave CRL checking disabled are not affected.

CWE: CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity

Description: With CRL checking enabled, OpenSSL compares each CRL distribution
point of a certificate against the issuing distribution point of every
candidate CRL. For a nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution point, the full name
is the CRL issuer name with the relative name appended. Since the change that
deferred this computation, crl_crldp_check() rebuilds that full name for each
candidate CRL and frees it again.

CMS_verify() and PKCS7_verify() take both the distribution points and the
candidate CRLs from the message, and this scoring runs before any signature is
checked. An application is exposed only if it sets X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK on
the store and does not pass CMS_NOCRL or PKCS7_NOCRL; CRL checking is off by
default. In TLS the CRLs come from the local store, so a peer controls only
the distribution point count.

The cost grows with the product of the distribution point count, the CRL count
and the issuer name length, all chosen by the message author; a few hundred
kilobytes can occupy a CPU core for tens of seconds. Verification still fails
as it should, with no crash, no incorrect result and no memory growth.
Requiring CRL checking is what limits the severity.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

The Dokan: AI Powered WooCommerce Multivendor Marketplace Solution – Build Your Own Amazon, eBay, Etsy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.3. The vulnerability exists because the `matches_mcp_endpoint()` function applies an unanchored regular expression (`#/(?:woocommerce|dokan)/mcp(?:/|$)#`) against the entire `REQUEST_URI` including the query string, meaning any request that contains the literal substring `/dokan/mcp/` or `/woocommerce/mcp/` anywhere in its URI — including inside a query parameter value — is incorrectly treated as a trusted internal MCP context, causing `scope_product_permissions()` to unconditionally return `true` on WooCommerce's `woocommerce_rest_check_permissions` filter regardless of whether the caller is authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read full authenticated WooCommerce REST product records for any published product — including private underscore-prefixed meta, purchase notes, downloadable file URLs for paid digital products, catalog-hidden products, and edit-context representations — across the `/wc/v1`, `/wc/v2`, `/wc/v3`, and `/wc-analytics` REST namespaces. The bypass is triggered by appending a query parameter whose value contains the literal string `/dokan/mcp/` to any WooCommerce REST product endpoint (e.g., `/wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id}?x=/dokan/mcp/`); note that percent-encoding the slashes prevents the bypass, as the unencoded literal slash characters are required for the regex to match.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.

Issue summary: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious
QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

Impact summary: A malicious remote QUIC peer can trigger an out-of-memory
condition causing a Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-84784 was not complete. It
failed to ignore retransmissions of the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame. The QUIC
implementation created and inserted a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for every
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame it received and there was no limit
on how many RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames were queued.

This issue allows a malicious remote QUIC stack to trigger an unbounded
allocation of memory and eventually an out-of-memory (OOM) condition.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, using the mosquitto_ctrl utility in interactive shell mode to interact with a malicious server could result in a crash of the utility if the server sent a hostile response.
In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the mosquitto_ctrl utility would crash if attempting to interact with a hostile broker and the broker sent a non-string "error" value.

In Eclipse versions 1.5-1.6.13, 2.0.0-2.0.22 and 2.1.0-2.1.2, the client library libmosquitto does not reject Will messages with payloads greater than 65535 bytes when calling `mosquitto_will_set()` or `mosquitto_will_set_v5()`. This results in up to 65535 bytes of uninitialised heap memory being transmitted as the Will.



This can be mitigated by only passing payloads with a maximum length of 65535 bytes.

In the Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider 10.2.0 through 15.3.0, `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` turned off TLS certificate verification for its connection to Amazon S3 by default (`s3_verify=False`), whatever the AWS connection's own verification settings were. An attacker positioned on the network between an Airflow worker and S3 could intercept that traffic, read the signed requests and alter the listed object keys and the copied file contents. Deployments are affected when a Dag uses `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` without setting `s3_verify`. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-microsoft-azure 15.3.1 or later, which uses the AWS connection's verification settings by default.

The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 only enforces two-factor authentication on the interactive login flow and not on other authentication paths, allowing an attacker who already has a user's valid password to authenticate as that user without completing the second factor.

Summary

MCUboot enforces several security-critical invariants on the boot, image-swap, and validation paths using assert(). In a standard release/production build (NDEBUG defined) assert() expands to a no-op, so an invariant the code intends to halt on instead falls through, and execution continues with the bad or inconsistent state. Where the guarded condition is attacker-influenceable through the flash-write boundary (serial-recovery / DFU), this is a security check that is simply absent in release builds.

This is one root cause (assert-as-security-guard, no-op under NDEBUG) with one fix approach (replace the security-critical asserts with real fail-closed checks), so it is filed as a single advisory covering the enumerated sites.

Worst reachable instance — inconsistent swap status completes the swap without validation

In the swap-resume status read, an inconsistent status (erased_sections > 1) is detected, logged, and — when MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT is disabled — is meant to abort, because "there is no way to be sure the swapped primary slot is OK." The abort is assert(0):

boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:181-194 — if (erased_sections > 1) { ... #if !defined(MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT) / ... abort! / assert(0); #endif }, then execution falls through to compute bs->op/idx/state from the inconsistent status (lines 197-208) and return 0 (success).
boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:266-280 — identical pattern; falls through to bs->op/idx/state and return 0.
boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:227-241 — same invalid/assert(0) pattern for the scratch backend.

Under NDEBUG with primary-slot validation off, the inconsistent status is neither aborted (assert is a no-op) nor re-validated (validation off), so boot_complete_partial_swap() finishes the swap on inconsistent metadata and the primary slot is booted without a signature check. An attacker who can write the swap-status trailer can craft the inconsistent status.

Reachability (threat model). Secondary slot + scratch trailers are A2-writable by definition (that is what a DFU upload is). Under MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY the primary trailer is A2-writable too: boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:978 opens flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0) (== primary) and writes from offset 0 bounded by area_size, so it can paint the primary swap-status/magic. This is how the A2 (recovery/DFU, unauthenticated by design) attacker influences the guarded condition. Property violated: P1 (image authenticity / secure-boot bypass) when un-revalidated content is booted, and P6 (boot/recovery availability).

Second reachable instance — resume-path swap_size from an unguarded trailer

boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1190-1193: the swap resume branch does fap = boot_find_status(...); assert(fap != NULL); rc = boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); assert(rc == 0);. boot_find_status() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_misc.c:166-204) searches {scratch, primary} and, on no-valid-magic-match, returns the last-iterated area (primary), not NULL — so assert(fap != NULL) cannot fire even in debug, and under NDEBUG neither assert fires. swap_size is then read from an A2-writable (serial-recovery primary, or scratch) trailer with no fail-closed handling. This is the same swap-metadata-trust family as the recorded resume/swap_size disclosure.

Reachable-security sites (center the fix here)

1. boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:193 — inconsistent-status assert(0), falls through to complete swap. A2 + !VALIDATE_PRIMARY. [worst]
2. boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:278 — same, swap-offset backend.
3. boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:239 — same, swap-scratch backend.
4. boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1191 and :1193 — resume assert(fap != NULL) / assert(rc == 0) guarding swap_size read from an A2-writable trailer; compounded by boot_find_status() never returning NULL.

(Truncated. The full description is in the advisory: https://github.com/mcu-tools/mcuboot/security/advisories/GHSA-cr9j-p626-pwcc)

Joomla! Core - [20261144] - Core - CSRF token leak in install from web in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The install from web feature submitted the CSRF token of the administrator to third-party sites.

Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.0 until 3.1.14, a listener performing DTLS 1.2 resumption accepted a session created by an outbound client connection without checking which role created it. A malicious server previously contacted by the application can retain the outbound session secret, select the client-side cached session through its session key, and present it to the application's reachable listener when both connections share a SessionStore. The attacker must first complete an outbound connection. WebRTC users are not affected. The listener can accept application data without running its normal PSK callback or client-certificate authentication checks, allowing a peer trusted only for an outbound connection to gain unauthorized listener access. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.14.

Relative path traversal in ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 object key to escape the intended bucket or key prefix.

When ex_aws builds a path-style S3 request, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex joins the bucket name and the object key into a single path string and then normalizes it, collapsing . and .. segments the way a filesystem path would. Because the bucket is the first segment of the combined string, a leading ../ in the object key pops the bucket off the path. With bucket mybucket and a key of ../victim/secret.txt, the combined /mybucket/../victim/secret.txt normalizes to /victim/secret.txt, so the request (signed with the application's own credentials) is sent to bucket victim. The same mechanism collapses ../ within a key, defeating any isolation an application enforces by prepending a trusted prefix.

Only the default path-style configuration is affected; requests built with virtual_host: true do not run this normalization. Because S3 treats object keys as opaque and does not resolve .. itself, the client-side normalization introduces a traversal that would not otherwise exist. Any application that derives an S3 object key from untrusted input and relies on the bucket, or a key prefix, as a tenant or trust boundary is exposed to cross-bucket or cross-prefix read and write, depending on the operation and the credentials' permissions.

This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, checkResetPasswordCode() in src/Auth/Models/User.php compares a submitted reset code with the stored 42-character token using a normal string comparison, which can return after the first differing byte instead of taking constant time. The password-reset flow exposes this comparison to remote requests, but the endpoint is rate-limited to six requests per minute per IP, and the advisory reports no live exploit or practical token-recovery demonstration. Recovering a high-entropy reset code through the constrained timing signal could permit an unauthorized password reset. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not refuse a NUL character in a startup parameter. The StartupMessage is a list of NUL-terminated strings, so a NUL in the database name, user, currentSchema, options or ApplicationName adds further parameters. %00 in a URL decodes to a NUL. Someone who controls part of the URL or a property can choose another login role or add replication=database, although the connection still has to pass the authentication of that role. On a server that trusts the client, the attacker can log in as any role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not enforce TLS for some settings that ask for it. When sslmode is not set, an ssl value such as 1, on, yes or verify-full gives sslmode=prefer, or no TLS before 42.2.5. A service given in the Properties instead of the URL is ignored, so the sslmode of its pg_service.conf entry is lost. BaseDataSource.setUrl() keeps an sslmode, channelBinding or gssEncMode that was set before it. An attacker on the network path can then read and change the traffic. Versions 9.4.1208 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

better-auth 1.4.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an improper authentication vulnerability because email-change links record the old and new addresses but not the requesting user. Attackers can open a still-valid link issued for their own account after a victim registers the attacker's released old address, gaining a session and changing the victim's email to one they control.

Better Auth 0.4.9 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an OAuth sign-in authentication flaw that treats unverified provider emails as verified, including string "false" email_verified claims, unchecked generic OAuth profile/ID-token subject mismatches, and ignored Zoom provider options. Attackers holding a victim's address unverified at an affected provider can sign in, link to the victim's local account, and obtain its session.

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, when Fastify routing is configured to be case-insensitive, the router folds the request path to lower case in a way that maps certain non-ASCII Unicode characters to ASCII letters, but @fastify/express matches Express mount paths against the decoded path without applying the same folding. The two disagree, so a request that spells a letter of a mount path with an equivalent Unicode character is routed to the protected handler while the path-scoped middleware mounted on that path never matches and is skipped. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, though only when the application enables case-insensitive routing and the mount path contains an affected letter. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

A flaw has been found in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file /usr/sbin/restore_config.cgi. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The vendor explains: "I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know." This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

The WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary directory deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the singleDeleteCache function in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires either the Custom Permalinks plugin or the GeoDirectory plugin to be co-installed, as these provide the necessary mechanism to write a traversal-bearing permalink value into the database that WP Fastest Cache then consumes without validation.

Poweradmin is a web-based DNS administration tool for PowerDNS server. From 4.0.0 until 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1, lib/Domain/Service/MfaService.php verifies email second-factor codes through MfaService::verifyCode() without limiting failed attempts, and lib/Application/Controller/MfaVerifyController.php logs failures without throttling them. An attacker who knows the user's password can repeatedly guess the six-digit code during its ten-minute validity period when email MFA is enabled, potentially bypassing the second factor; the advisory notes MFA is disabled by default and that the practical request rate was not measured. This issue is fixed in versions 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1.
In JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA before 2026.3 untrusted projects could read files of other open projects via the built-in web server
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2, 2026.1.6 agent Push authorization keys were predictable
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.5 untrusted build approval for GitHub fork pull requests could be bypassed

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions 8.3.0 through 9.3.6, the internal helper that normalizes a path-scoped middleware's mount path only handles string inputs, but the use method also accepts an array of mount paths and passes it through unchanged, so the normalization silently does nothing. As a result, a trailing slash on an array element survives into the generated route-matching regular expression, and an element that is exactly the root path, meaning a catch-all mount, is dropped entirely. Requests to subroutes of the affected mount paths then skip the path-scoped middleware, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, while Fastify's router still dispatches them to the handler, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach protected routes. Applications are affected when they mount middleware on an array of paths in which an element ends with a slash, including one introduced by a plugin prefix that ends with a slash, or is exactly the root path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid array mount paths with a trailing slash element for security relevant middleware.

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, or keep routing case-sensitive, which is the default.
Ruby before 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10 has a heap-based buffer overflow during case conversion. One byte can be written outside a buffer for, for example, ISO-8859-1 or Windows-1252.

The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog. Prior to datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0, the Datadog Single Step Instrumentation injector stores helper tooling in a predictable host directory. On Linux or Kubernetes systems with SSI enabled and at least one Java service instrumented through SSI, a local unprivileged attacker with shell access to the same host can influence that tooling and execute code with the privileges of the instrumented Java service. Services that use dd-java-agent without SSI and non-Java language runtimes are not affected. This issue is fixed in datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0.

The Chainguard SDK is a public Go SDK for integrating with the Chainguard platform. Prior to 0.1.107, auth/aws.VerifyToken trusts the Chainguard-Audience and Chainguard-Identity headers without requiring those headers to be covered by AWS SigV4 SignedHeaders. An attacker with a fresh STS GetCallerIdentity request signed by a victim can rewrite the unsigned binding headers and replay the proof to another relying party, causing the relying party to authenticate the victim’s AWS identity for an attacker-chosen audience and identity. Code that only uses auth/aws.GenerateToken is unaffected because the generator signs the binding headers, and exploitation requires a signed request within its validity window. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.107.

The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 via the '_cf7mls_db_form_data_id' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete arbitrary stored Contact Form 7 submissions from the database. Exploitation requires the companion CF7 Database plugin to be active and the per-form "Save every step, not just the final submission" option to be enabled.

The Bizuno Accounting – ERP/Accounting/CRM (for WordPress) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Password Reset Token Disclosure in all versions up to, and including, 7.4.5 via the `bizUser` parameter of the `validateReset()` function on the `portal/api/lostPW` endpoint. This is due to `portalCtl::goAPI()` failing to call `loadBusinessCache()` before invoking the handler, which causes `isMailConfigured()` to read an empty business cache and return false regardless of the site's actual mail configuration, causing the fully-qualified reset URL — containing the victim's live reset UUID and numeric user ID — to be embedded directly in the HTML response rather than delivered by email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain a valid password-reset token for any Bizuno account, including administrators, directly from the HTTP response and submit it to the `portal/api/lostVal` endpoint to rewrite the victim's password and achieve full account takeover. The administrator email address required to initiate the reset is frequently exposed by the plugin's own login error messages and the public `/bizuno/` portal page, making exploitation trivial against most installations.

An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated user whose numeric user ID matched an enterprise's numeric ID to manage that enterprise's GitHub Apps and generate private keys without enterprise membership. GitHub App ownership checks compared numeric IDs without checking the owner's account type. Exploitation required control of a session for the colliding user account and an enterprise-owned GitHub App. A generated private key could be used to authenticate as the App and access repositories where it was installed, within its granted permissions. On standard fresh installations, the documented collision involved the non-loginable built-in ghost account; the reported GHES reproduction used site administrator impersonation. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

VeraCrypt through 1.26.31 on Linux contains an improper path restriction vulnerability in the elevated CoreService, which passes the path and owner UID from a SetFileOwnerRequest directly to chown() in CoreUnix::SetFileOwner without target validation on Linux. An attacker with an active elevated CoreService session and same-UID access who reopens the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> can take ownership of arbitrary system files such as /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, achieving full root compromise.

VeraCrypt before 1.26.30 on Linux contains a command injection vulnerability in CoreUnix::CheckFilesystem that allows a local attacker with same-UID access and an active elevated CoreService session to execute arbitrary commands by injecting an unsanitized VirtualDevice value into a shell command string. Attackers can reopen the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> and supply a crafted VirtualDevice value such as /dev/null; <command> to achieve arbitrary command execution as root.

Devin Desktop Uncontrolled Search Path Element Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of Devin Desktop. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the Electron framework. The product loads a script file from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of a target user. Was ZDI-CAN-33385.

Python Packaging Authority pip Configuration File Incorrect Permission Assignment Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of Python Packaging Authority pip. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability. User interaction on the part of a target user is also required.

The specific flaw exists within the way configuration files are stored. The issue results from incorrect permissions on files. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of a target user. Was ZDI-CAN-25377.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the OBJ exporter that allows attackers to corrupt memory via NaN vertex components breaking comparator ordering. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file with NaN texture coordinates or vertex colors that, when exported to OBJ in libc++ builds, writes file-controlled data past a heap buffer and crashes the application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in OpenGEXImporter.cpp because InternReadFile does not reset cached importer state between files. Attackers can supply OpenGEX files to applications reusing one Importer instance, causing freed node, camera, and material pointers to corrupt heap memory and crash.

The controllers.json loader of @symfony/stimulus-bridge loads the package.json file of each package listed in controllers.json with require(). Node resolves this path through the exports field of the package, which can map ./package.json to a script. require() then runs that script during the Webpack or Symfony Encore build.

This is a build-time vulnerability: it doesn't affect browsers or end users. A malicious or compromised package listed in controllers.json can run code on the developer machine or the CI server. This works even when the package manager doesn't run install scripts. This code can read the files and environment variables of the build, like CI secrets, and change the built assets.

The loader now reads the resolved file and parses it as JSON, so that a mapped script fails to parse instead of running.

The @symfony/stimulus-bridge npm package includes a Webpack loader called lazy-controller-loader that supports "magic comments" placed above a Stimulus controller import, for example /* stimulusFetch: 'lazy' */, to control lazy loading behavior. To read those options, the loader extracted the raw text of any stimulus* comment and evaluated it as JavaScript using Node's vm.runInNewContext(). The Node.js node:vm module is not a security sandbox, and a crafted comment can break out of the VM context using well-known techniques to run arbitrary Node.js code within the build process.

This is a build-time vulnerability: it does not affect browsers or end users. The code executes on the developer machine or CI/build server during a Webpack or Symfony Encore build. Realistic attack vectors include a malicious Stimulus controller introduced through a compromised dependency, or a pull request that triggers an automated CI build. An attacker who can get such a file into the build can read files and environment variables available to the build process, exfiltrate CI secrets, tamper with generated build artifacts, and run commands with the permissions of the build user.

The loader no longer evaluates comment content as JavaScript. It now parses each comment as an object expression using a real JavaScript parser and extracts only plain literal values. Any non-literal value, such as a function call, an identifier, or a sequence expression, is rejected and reported as a build error instead of being executed. Legitimate option values like 'lazy' and 'eager' continue to work without any changes required on the user's side.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a double free vulnerability in the fill_marker() function of libavformat/imf_cpl.c that frees a Marker label without clearing the pointer when default scope allocation fails. Attackers can supply a crafted Composition Playlist with a Marker Label lacking a scope attribute, triggering a second free in imf_marker_free() under memory pressure and causing memory corruption or a crash.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ogg_buffer_data() in libavformat/oggenc.c because ogg_buffer_page() leaves a full page current after failed allocation. When page allocation fails, a memset with length (size_t)-1 or an overflowing memcpy writes past the segment table, causing heap memory corruption and crashes when writing Ogg output.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in modplug_read_header() in libavformat/libmodplug.c that allocates the buffer using max_size instead of sz. When max_size is set to 0, attackers can supply crafted module files that avio_read() copies into a zero-sized buffer, causing memory corruption, crashes, or possible code execution.
Tanium addressed a local privilege escalation vulnerability in Emerging Issues Content.
Tanium addressed a local privilege escalation vulnerability in Emerging Issues Content.
Tanium addressed an improper input validation vulnerability in Core Content.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in PLYImporter::LoadFace and PLYImporter::createFromeTriStrip that fails to validate face vertex indices against the vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file whose out-of-range indices cause GenVertexNormalsProcess::GenMeshVertexNormals to write normals outside the heap buffer, crashing the application or potentially enabling code execution.

G DATA Total Security Backup Service Uncontrolled Search Path Element Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the Backup Service. The service restores archives from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28666.

MaxKB is an open-source AI assistant for enterprise. Prior to 2.10.7-lts, custom Tool Init Param definitions accept attacker-controlled props_info.rules[].validator strings through POST /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool and PUT /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool/{tool_id}, store them without restriction, and pass them to eval() when the parameter form renders. An authenticated user with the default USER workspace role can store JavaScript and trigger execution by opening the tool's Debug screen before entering or submitting a parameter value. The same Init Param form is exposed to accounts with edit permission on the tool, but execution by a different account was not independently verified. The confirmed script runs in the MaxKB origin; access to another user's bearer token and authenticated account authority is plausible only if that user renders the malicious form. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.7-lts.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

The fix for CVE-2026-25854 was incomplete.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.19 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.53 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.116 through 9.0.123.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat could occur during a request dispatch if the request depended on a security-role-ref provided by the dispatch target.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fixes the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with access to the configured load balancer account could replace a load balancer helper that Splunk SOAR later runs with root privileges during cluster lifecycle operations. If a Splunk SOAR administrator performs a cluster lifecycle operation, Splunk SOAR could execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the load balancer.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify the integrity or ownership of the load balancer helper before running it with root privileges.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with local access to the affected host could obtain a live Splunk SOAR session token or decrypted asset configuration when another user starts an App Editor debug action.
The vulnerability is possible because App Editor debug actions expose sensitive runtime information to other local users on the affected host.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Updates data. If another user who can access the System Update Status report selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the System Update Status report does not validate destination, signature, and vendor-product values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and System Update Status (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/system-update-status) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk App for Payment Card Industry Compliance versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role could add attacker-controlled values to lookup data used by the Primary Functions report. If another authenticated user later selects the value in the Primary Function Summary panel, the Splunk App for Payment Card Industry Compliance could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the value. With this access, the first user could expose or modify data available to the user who selected the value.
The vulnerability is possible because the Primary Functions report does not safely escape report values before including them in drilldown searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Reports (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/user-manual/8.7/using-the-splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/reports) in the Splunk documentation.

Authorization bypass through a user-controlled key in the PuppetDB facts terminus used by Puppet Server allows a client holding any valid agent certificate to overwrite the facts, including trusted facts, that PuppetDB stores for a different node. In Puppet Enterprise deployments where task permissions are scoped to node groups defined by facts or trusted facts, this can allow a user to run tasks on nodes outside their permitted scope.

VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 on non-macOS, non-Windows builds contains stack-based buffer overflows in aacs_resolve_path() in src/file/path.c from length checks against the wrong buffer. Local attackers can place a symlink with a long target on a disc path a user opens to overflow resolved_path[] and link[], crashing the process or potentially executing code if mitigations are bypassed.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Prover9Parent.config_prover9 and Mace accept a relative binary_location and pass it to find_binary as path_to_bin, disabling the bare-name absolute-path guard. A local attacker who can plant prover9 or mace4 in the resolved working directory can cause subprocess.Popen to execute that binary with the invoking user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
