OpenRemote is an open-source internet-of-things platform. Prior to 1.31.0, an authenticated user who obtains another user's MQTT session ID can disconnect that session across realm boundaries through the GET route GET {realm}/disconnect/{sessionID}. In manager/src/main/java/org/openremote/manager/security/UserResourceImpl.java, disconnectUserSession ignores the requested realm and calls mqttBrokerService.disconnectSession(sessionID) without checking session ownership; model/src/main/java/org/openremote/model/security/UserResource.java exposes the route without an @RolesAllowed restriction. The earlier cross-realm read-method guards did not cover this disconnect method, and same-realm users can also disconnect sessions they do not own. Session IDs are not trivially brute-forceable but may be exposed through monitoring, logs, or correlated API calls, and the unauthorized disconnect can disrupt MQTT connectivity across tenant boundaries without directly disclosing session data. This issue is fixed in 1.31.0.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Verification mail rate limit reset in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The rate limit for verification mails was reset on every form render, rendering the limit ineffective.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Predictable and reusable email verification codes in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Email verification codes were derived from the email address, did not expire after use and could be guessed without attempt limits, allowing bypass of the email verification.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing access check in reload task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The public reload task did not check form and field access levels, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve results of SQL field statements of restricted forms.

When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1 dataclass makes it considered as already validated, resulting in field values not being validated. The __init__() method of Pydantic V1 dataclasses stores all the provided keyword arguments in the instance __dict__ before validation, so a __pydantic_initialised__ keyword argument overrides the internal flag used to skip validation of already validated instances. As a result, data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data. The issue was fixed in Pydantic 1.10.27. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Path traversal in file upload in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - File names of uploads were not reduced to their base name when the option to retain original file names was enabled, potentially allowing files to be written outside the upload directory.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Access restriction bypass for form submissions in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Form submissions did not check the access level of the form, allowing guests to submit forms restricted to specific user groups.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Wi-Fi Configuration Server Missing Authentication Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to modify Wi-Fi configuration on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of Wi-Fi configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29068.

SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions.

The SOAP extension reads an uninitialized array position when decoding an encoded array whose arraySize attribute is empty, whitespace-only or non-numeric, or when such dimensions come from a WSDL definition. Four bytes of unrelated heap data can then be used as an integer key in the decoded array. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a crafted request to a SoapServer endpoint, and a malicious SOAP server with a response to SoapClient. Heap memory is disclosed only if the application returns or otherwise exposes the decoded array.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

MISP, a threat intelligence sharing platform, contains a vulnerability in its cryptographic key management for protected (PGP-signed) events. Two related defects allow a revoked PGP key to remain effective for signing and validating protected events.

First, the validateProtectedEvent() method in the CryptographicKey model iterates over the event's stored cryptographic keys to verify a PGP signature but does not check the revoked flag on each key. A key explicitly marked as revoked is still used to validate signatures, meaning an entity whose key has been revoked can continue to sign protected events and have them accepted by the MISP instance.

Second, the captureCryptographicKeyUpdate() method, responsible for synchronizing the key list when a sync user edits a protected event, contained a query bug (find('first') instead of find('all')) that caused only the first stored key to be considered. As a result, revocations of additional keys were never persisted, keys absent from the pushed list were not removed, and entries lacking an explicit fingerprint were mismatched and incorrectly deleted. Additionally, the revocation logic did not enforce the invariant that a revocation, once stored, is never lifted by subsequent pushes.

A third minor issue: a signed protected event submitted without any cryptographic keys triggered an unhandled 500 error rather than a proper rejection response.

Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated sync user with permission to add or edit protected events on the MISP instance. The impact is that revoked keys retain signing authority, key revocations propagated by sync partners are silently dropped, and the integrity of the protected-event trust chain is compromised. In a multi-instance MISP deployment, events signed by revoked keys can propagate to other instances, extending the integrity impact across the sync network.

SOAP use-after-free when processing DTD entity references.

The SOAP extension frees the document type definition (DTD) of a parsed XML document while attribute values can still refer to entities it owns, and can then read freed memory. Removing the DTD also bypasses the SOAP server's rejection of documents that contain one. An unauthenticated remote attacker who can send a crafted request to a SOAP endpoint, or who controls a WSDL or schema document loaded by the application, can crash the PHP process and cause denial of service. Memory disclosure and code execution have not been confirmed.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Double free during DOM XML serialization.

The XML serializer of Dom\XMLDocument and Dom\HTMLDocument can share ownership of a generated namespace prefix between the namespace-prefix maps of an element and a descendant, so the prefix is used after being freed and then freed a second time. The document does not need to be malformed. An application that parses attacker-controlled XML or HTML with these classes and serializes it with saveXml() can be crashed, and repeated requests can cause denial of service. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input.

The Uri\Rfc3986\Uri class does not correctly handle the output-size limit and errors of the uriparser library when converting a URI back to a string. For a URI whose string representation reaches approximately 2 GiB, toString(), toRawString() and other serializing operations can return a truncated or invalid string instead of an error. An application that accepts attacker-controlled URI data of that size, has enough memory to process it and trusts the result may make incorrect validation or routing decisions, and the large allocations can exhaust memory. parse_url() and Uri\WhatWg\Url are not affected.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

In Eclipse Yasson versions 3.0 to 3.0.5, a race condition (CWE-362) exists in the handling of @JsonbNumberFormat. Yasson creates one java.text.NumberFormat instance per annotated property and shares it across all threads that use the same Jsonb instance. NumberFormat is not thread-safe, and the deserializer called parse() on it without synchronization. When multiple threads deserialize concurrently, a thread can receive a numeric value that belongs to another thread's input, receive an incorrect value, or fail with an exception. A remote attacker who can send concurrent requests to an application that deserializes untrusted JSON this way may cause incorrect data to be processed or cause another user's value to be returned. Exploitation requires that the application use @JsonbNumberFormat with a shared Jsonb instance and that the attacker win a timing race. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.6 by synchronizing access to the shared NumberFormat instances.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.0, failed Railpack builds and database backups propagate an execution error containing the full command, exposing application environment variables, database passwords, and S3 access keys embedded in those commands. When the corresponding App Build Error or Database Backup notification setting is enabled, the disclosure can send secrets to email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, or webhooks; the same secrets are written separately to persistent Dokploy container logs, which may be accessible to more principals than the affected service. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.

MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the Galaxy import/sync functionality (captureGalaxy in app/Model/Galaxy.php). The captureGalaxy() method matched an incoming galaxy payload to an existing galaxy by UUID and unconditionally overwrote the matched record, regardless of whether the importing user belonged to the owning organization or whether the galaxy was a system-provided default galaxy. Any authenticated user holding the perm_galaxy_editor role could therefore: (1) demote a default galaxy by setting its default flag to false, (2) reassign the galaxy's org_id and orgc_id to the attacker's organization, effectively taking ownership, and (3) modify other galaxy fields (name, description, distribution, version). Additionally, the role-level permission check (perm_site_admin or perm_galaxy_editor) was executed after the captureOrganisationAndSG() call, meaning organization and sharing-group data was already captured before the authorization decision was made. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with the perm_galaxy_editor role and the ability to submit a galaxy import payload containing a UUID that matches an existing galaxy. The security impact is loss of data integrity across the MISP instance: default galaxy definitions are corrupted, cross-organization ownership is silently transferred, and the integrity of shared threat-intelligence galaxy metadata is compromised for all users of the instance.

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the GalaxyCluster model's captureCluster() function, which handles the import and synchronization of Galaxy Clusters. Prior to the fix, any authenticated user holding the galaxy editor role could replace an existing locked Galaxy Cluster by supplying its UUID in an import request, regardless of which organization owned the cluster. The function unconditionally called captureOrganisationAndSG() before the save operation, overwriting the cluster's org_id and orgc_id fields with the importing user's organization, effectively transferring ownership of the cluster to the attacker's organization. Additionally, the save operation was not restricted to a specific set of fields, allowing arbitrary field modification.

The vulnerable behavior required the attacker to possess a valid MISP account with the perm_galaxy_editor role and to know or discover the UUID of a target cluster belonging to another organization. No site-admin or owner-organization privilege was enforced for the update path. The result was that a low-privilege galaxy editor in one organization could modify the content (value, description, distribution, etc.) of clusters owned by other organizations and seize ownership, corrupting the integrity of shared threat-intelligence data across the MISP instance.

The vulnerability was reported by ENISA and CERT.pl. The fix introduces an explicit authorization gate that restricts cluster updates to the owner organization, a sync user who can see the cluster via sharing-group rules, or a site administrator, and enforces a field allow-list that excludes org_id and orgc_id from update writes, preserving original ownership.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to require client certificates ("ssl_verify_client on") in a non-default stream virtual server, a remote attacker could bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to determine registered email addresses by observing differing sign-up endpoint responses. Attackers can submit addresses to signup in users.service.ts and compare error messages to identify existing accounts and pending Enterprise invitations, even under invite-only signup.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message. Attackers can submit sign-in requests where validateUser in auth.service.ts skips password comparison for saltless invited accounts, confirming the email address has an account.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths under nc/uploads/data-export. Attackers can derive paths from the table id, base, table and view titles, and export time to read full exports, including fields hidden from public shared views.

Parse Server before 8.6.119 and 9.x before 9.10.8-alpha.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows LiveQuery clients without the master key to subscribe to installation and internal classes. Attackers can receive installation IDs and device tokens of other devices when these classes are in liveQuery.classNames, then modify those installations to redirect push notifications.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the EXR decoder that is triggered when a specific memory allocation fails. Attackers can supply crafted EXR images processed under memory pressure to trigger the use after free, causing crashes or memory corruption.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the MSL decoder that can be triggered when processing crafted MSL image files. Attackers can supply a specially crafted MSL image to cause memory corruption, potentially crashing the application or leading to further compromise.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the RLA decoder that returns images containing uninitialized data. Attackers can supply a crafted RLA image to cause the decoded output to include uninitialized memory, potentially disclosing heap information.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MNG decoder that allows attackers to expose uninitialized memory by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit malicious MNG files for processing to leak uninitialized memory contents, potentially revealing sensitive data from the process.

The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.14 via the `draft_post()` function. This is due to the function storing the `post_content` parameter via `wp_insert_post()` without the protected-shortcode allow-list check that was introduced in 4.3.14 for the sibling `submit_post()` handler — a gap that `wp_kses` filtering does not close, as it strips only HTML tags while leaving shortcode text such as `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` intact. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to embed a registration shortcode in a post and cause any site visitor who subsequently registers through the rendered form to receive Editor-level access. The render-time `wpuf_modify_shortcodes` filter that is designed to neutralize protected shortcodes provides no protection here because posts created via the `wpuf_draft_post` AJAX endpoint carry no `_edit_last` post meta, causing the filter to return the content unchanged and allowing the shortcode to render and execute fully.

nVision sends user's token via query parameters of GET requests. An attacker who obtains valid token can gain access to the victim's account and perform actions on their behalf.


This issue was fixed in version 18.

MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform) contains an authorization bypass in the SharingGroup model's captureSGExisting method. The authorization check used a logical AND condition that effectively exempted users with the sync permission (perm_sync) from the membership verification. Specifically, the original condition 'if (!checkIfAuthorised(...) && !perm_sync) return false' meant that any user holding the sync role would pass the check regardless of whether they were actually a member of the target sharing group.

A sync user who knows or can discover the UUID of a non-local sharing group could exploit this flaw through the /sharing_groups/add endpoint or by embedding a SharingGroup object in pushed sync data. The attacker could rewrite the sharing group record to add their own organisation as a member or insert an all_orgs server entry for their MISP instance, thereby gaining read access to all events contained in that group. This exposes threat intelligence data that was intended to be restricted to the group's legitimate members.

The vulnerability requires an authenticated account with the sync role and knowledge of a valid sharing group UUID. No user interaction is required. The impact is unauthorized disclosure of shared threat intelligence events and limited integrity modification of the sharing group record.

The Cypress/PSoC6 flash-map backend in boot/cypress/cy_flash_pal/cy_flash_map.c guards every flash access with assert() against the wrong struct field. flash_area_read(), flash_area_write(), and flash_area_erase() check assert(off < fa->fa_off) and assert(off + len < fa->fa_off), comparing the area-relative off against the partition's absolute base address fa->fa_off instead of its length fa->fa_size. Because fa_off is a large absolute address, realistic out-of-partition offsets pass the check even in a debug build, and under NDEBUG the asserts are removed entirely. The access then proceeds as memcpy() (or a flash row op) at fa->fa_off + off with no enforcement.

The MCUboot core does not bound image-region offsets itself; it relies on flash_area_read() returning an error. During pre-authentication image validation, bootutil_img_hash() in boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_img_hash.c loops over ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size + ih_protect_tlv_size — all attacker-controlled header fields of the still-unverified update image — calling flash_area_read(), and the TLV iterator in boot/bootutil/src/tlv.c reads attacker-derived offsets the same way. An attacker who can stage a crafted image in the secondary/update slot (via OTA, DFU, or serial recovery, depending on the product) declares an oversized ih_img_size, causing reads far past the partition. A correct backend would reject these and fail validation cleanly; the Cypress backend does not.

The out-of-bounds access is in the source address of the copy — the destination buffer is correctly sized — so there is no memory corruption, no information disclosure to the attacker (the data is only folded into a hash that still fails the signature check), and no authentication bypass. The realistic impact is a bus fault or hang when the computed absolute address lands on an unmapped or peripheral region of the PSoC6 address map: the bootloader crashes instead of rejecting the bad image, an availability (denial-of-service) impact. The defect is specific to the Cypress/PSoC6 port; mainline Zephyr/sim/mynewt backends are unaffected. The identical broken guard in the write/erase primitives is a latent out-of-bounds-write gap, but no attacker-controlled out-of-bounds offset was found to reach those (serial-recovery uploads are bounded by the core), so the reachable memory-safety bug is the out-of-bounds read.

MISP contains a DOM-based cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Pivot Explorer component. The bundled pivotick visualization library (version 1.2.0) rendered all string values it received as HTML markup rather than as plain text. As a result, user-controllable data fields, including attribute comments, attribute values, and reference relationship types, were interpreted and executed as HTML/JavaScript in the Pivot Explorer tooltip and sidebar panels.

An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify MISP attributes could embed malicious HTML or script payloads in these fields. When another user (or the same user) opened the Pivot Explorer and viewed the affected event data, the injected markup would execute in the victim's browser context, potentially allowing session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim.

Preconditions:
- The attacker must have authenticated access to create or modify MISP attributes (comments, values, or reference relationship types).
- The victim must open the Pivot Explorer and interact with or view the affected event data in the tooltip or sidebar.

Security impact: Successful exploitation allows arbitrary script execution in the victim's browser within the MISP application origin, enabling theft of session credentials, manipulation of displayed data, and execution of privileged API calls on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the event report element rendering pipeline. The client-side sanitization function used to prepare values for doT templates only escaped ampersand, less-than, and greater-than characters. However, the templates place these values inside double-quoted HTML attributes. Because double-quote and single-quote characters were not escaped, a user with the ability to author or modify report element values could inject a quote character to break out of the attribute context and inject arbitrary HTML or JavaScript that executes in the viewing user's browser.

Preconditions:
- The attacker must be an authenticated user with permission to create or edit event report elements (e.g., a report author).
- A victim must open or view the crafted report in a browser.

Security impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the victim's MISP session.
- Potential theft of session tokens, sensitive data, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its map attachment rendering. When a GPX or GeoJSON file is uploaded as an attachment to a MISP event, the waypoint names (GPX) and property names and values (GeoJSON) are inserted into Leaflet map popups without HTML escaping. Because Leaflet renders popup content as raw HTML, any markup or script embedded in those fields is executed in the browser of every user who views the map and interacts with the affected marker or icon.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with permission to upload attachments to a MISP event crafts a GPX or GeoJSON file containing malicious HTML/JavaScript in waypoint names or GeoJSON property keys/values.
- A victim user views the event map and clicks the affected marker or GeoJSON icon, triggering the popup.

Impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application, potentially leading to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.
IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive credentials due to the use of a hard-coded cryptographic key.
IBM Financial Transaction Manager (FTM) 3.2.13.0 through 3.2.13.0 Interim Fix 006 stores potentially sensitive information in environment variables that could be read by a local user.

The EU Order Withdrawal Button for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution requires an Administrator or Shop Manager to open the Withdrawals Preview modal and click the injected note element, which the attacker can enlarge via a retained style attribute to cover the entire note area. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

Adobe Experience Manager is affected by a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this issue by manipulating the DOM environment to execute malicious JavaScript within the context of the victim's browser. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must visit a crafted webpage. Scope is changed.
Sandbox escape in the Marionette component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161.

odf-kit is a TypeScript and JavaScript library for working with OpenDocument Format files. In versions 0.9.8 through 0.14.1, the odsToHtml() renderer inserts document-controlled cell formatting and row height values into HTML style attributes without escaping them. An attacker can craft an ODS file that injects arbitrary HTML attributes or elements, allowing JavaScript execution in the host page's origin when an application inserts the converted output as HTML. This issue is fixed in version 0.14.2.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to perform state-changing actions by exploiting missing Origin header validation and absent CSRF tokens. Attackers can lure authenticated users to a same-site attacker page that submits forged POST requests to stop, start, or delete stacks, modify settings, and change credentials.

The Fastcache by Host.it plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 's' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. This code path is only reachable when both the Light Images feature and the DOMDocument entity-decode branch are enabled (lightimgs_status = 1 and img_processing_entity_decode = 1), which reflect the default plugin configuration.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, client/src/components/Chat/Input/MCPConfigDialog.tsx renders the remote MCP details.description value through dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, allowing a malicious MCP server to execute script when a user opens the configuration dialog. The secondary client/src/components/Banners/Banner.tsx sink similarly renders administrator-controlled banner.message HTML without sanitization for all users. Script execution occurs in the LibreChat browser origin and can expose browser-context data or alter displayed content. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

G DATA Total Security AVKProxy Link Following Denial-of-Service Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the G DATA ANTIVIRUS Proxy Service. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the service to create a file. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create a persistent denial-of-service condition on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-28662.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.5.13 and 4.6.02, an unauthenticated attacker can place a multiply encoded value in the news module search q parameter. $nv_Request->get_title() decodes and sanitizes the input once, but modules/news/funcs/search.php subsequently applies urldecode() after sanitization. The resulting raw keyword reaches the {KEY} search-input attribute through search_theme() and the no-results element through search_result_theme() in the default and mobile themes, permitting attribute or tag injection and same-origin JavaScript execution when a victim opens the crafted search URL. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.13 and 4.6.02.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.5, MapServer's WMS OpenLayers output, selected by FORMAT=application/openlayers or template=openlayers, substitutes a request-derived online-resource value into a single-quoted JavaScript string in src/maptemplate.c. The prior remediation for GHSA-xqj6-vjqr-33vv used msEscapeJSonLikeString() to protect the JavaScript string but did not neutralize angle brackets, so attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto values can still terminate the script element at the HTML parser layer. Deployments that expose attacker-controlled PATH_INFO or map= values reaching the same string are also affected. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in a victim's browser under the MapServer origin when the victim loads the crafted output. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

FlowIntel contained a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability affecting fourteen web routes that performed destructive or state-changing operations. The affected routes accepted HTTP GET requests in addition to (or instead of) POST, which bypassed the Flask-WTF CSRF token validation that is only enforced on non-GET requests.

The vulnerable operations included:
- Case deletion and case merging
- Organisation removal from a case
- Task deletion (case and template)
- Case template and note template deletion
- Connector, connector instance, and icon deletion
- Custom tag deletion and status change
- Taxonomy and galaxy status changes

An attacker who could induce an authenticated user to follow a crafted link or load a page containing a cross-site navigation (e.g., an image tag or redirect) could trigger any of these destructive actions using the victim's session cookie, without the victim's explicit consent or awareness. No special privileges beyond a valid authenticated session with the appropriate role (editor or admin) were required on the victim's account.

Security impact: unauthorized deletion or modification of cases, tasks, templates, connectors, icons, custom tags, taxonomies, and galaxies belonging to the victim or the organisation, resulting in loss of data integrity.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, allowlisted_pickle_load keys dangerous NumPy globals by export name, allowing submodule-local numpy.lib file input/output callables to evade the denylist under the broad module allowance used by TransitionParser. A crafted pickle can invoke recfromtxt to read a local file or open_memmap to create or truncate an attacker-selected file when a victim loads an untrusted model. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, LoginFormAuthenticator accepts unsafe destinations for the login success redirect and login failure redirect. An attacker can direct a user to an attacker-controlled domain after authentication succeeds or fails, enabling phishing and potential token theft. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

When Private data source connect (PDC) or a secure SOCKS proxy is used, the MQTT data source plugin does not apply TLS to broker connections for the tls, ssl, tcps, mqtts and mqtt+ssl schemes. The configured TLS settings are ignored, and the broker username and password are sent unencrypted on the hop between the proxy and the broker. The server certificate is not verified, and a configured client certificate is not sent.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2, 2026.1.6 reflected XSS on the Edit VCS Root page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1 reflected XSS on the Cloud Profiles page was possible

The Fancy Lightbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation without administrator interaction requires that the attacker first have one comment approved so that a subsequent payload comment is auto-published; the injected script only executes when a user clicks the malicious image link inside the comment. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 reflected XSS on the Slack connection test page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the build Report Tab dialog was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the Promote build dialog for dependent builds was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4 stored XSS in the JVM update warning on the Agent Summary page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 reflected XSS in the notification rule form was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 reflected XSS on the Clean-up Rules page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 reflected XSS on the Build Chains tab was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 reflected XSS in Kubernetes cloud profile namespace and deployment choosers was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.5 reflected XSS on the Test History page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 reflected XSS in the inspection profile selector popup was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 reflected XSS on the Build Log page was possible
