Server-side request forgery in Amazon OpenSearch Service service software before R20260720 might allow an authenticated user with permission to manage snapshots to make the service send requests to network destinations of their choosing via the snapshot repository endpoint setting. This issue is addressed in service software R20260720. Customers should update their domains to R20260720 or later.

Canvas 7.0.0 before 7.2.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Contributors to inject scripts by exploiting a libxml2 parser differential in PostBody::clean(). Attackers can publish posts with slash-separated event handler attributes rendered unescaped in show.blade.php, hijacking Editor or Admin sessions to escalate their role to Admin.

Joomla! Core - [20261155] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_fields in Joomla 3.7.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Permission checks for custom fields and field groups used the context of the request instead of the context of the changed record, allowing users to move or change fields of other components.

Joomla! Core - [20261154] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_workflow stages in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Permission checks for workflow stages used a wrong asset name, so stage specific permissions were ignored when changing the state of or deleting a stage.

Joomla! Core - [20261150] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_menus publishing dates in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inadequate ACL checks allowed users without edit state permission to change the publishing dates of menu items.

Joomla! Core - [20261149] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_contact publishing dates in Joomla 1.6.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inadequate ACL checks allowed users without edit state permission to change the publishing dates of contacts.

Joomla! Core - [20261145] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_media file creation in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inadequate ACL checks in the media manager allowed users without create permission to create new files by using the override option.

Joomla! Core - [20261139] - Core - DoS in email cloaking plugin in Joomla 1.6.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inefficient processing of email links in the email cloaking plugin can lead to excessive CPU usage when rendering content.

Joomla! Core - [20261138] - Core - DoS in InputFilter email punycode conversion in Joomla 3.5.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inefficient processing of email addresses in the text filter can lead to excessive CPU usage.

Joomla! Core - [20261135] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_menus site modal in Joomla 3.7.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Inadequate ACL checks in the frontend menu item modal allowed users without backend access to read menu item titles and to change the default menu item.

Joomla! Core - [20261116] - Core - Information disclosure in com_config webservice endpoint in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The application configuration webservice endpoint did not remove protected values such as passwords and secrets from its response.

Joomla! Core - [20261102] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_newsfeeds delete action in Joomla 1.6.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - An improper access check allows users without delete permission on a category to delete trashed newsfeeds.

Cockpit CMS through 2.14.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with content create or update permission to inject script via unescaped linked item _id values. Attackers can save an item whose link _id contains a double quote and HTML markup, executing script when administrators view the content dashboard or collection list.

Server-Side Request Forgery in the SSO SAML configuration feature of the TXOne StellarOne web console allows an authenticated administrator to issue server-side requests to arbitrary destinations, including internal services. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex_aws (S3 request URL construction).

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/request/url.ex and program routines ExAws.Request.Url.build/2, ExAws.Request.Url.sanitize/2 and ExAws.Request.Url.get_path/2.

ex_aws does not percent-encode reserved characters in S3 object keys when it assembles the request URL. A literal ? in an object key survives unencoded: build/2 inserts the operation path verbatim and URI.to_string/1 emits it without encoding, and sanitize/2 then splits the flattened URL on the first ?, treating everything after it as the query string. Because the split runs before uri_encode is applied to the path, the ? is never neutralized, and the recovered query is re-inserted without any encoding.

An attacker who controls part of an object key (for example a download or upload keyed by a user-supplied filename) can therefore truncate the key past application-appended suffixes, causing the request to address a different object than the application intended, and can inject live S3 sub-resource operations (such as ?acl, ?tagging or ?versions) into the request. The manipulated URL is signed and transmitted normally, so the tampering is authorized like any legitimate request.

This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.2 before 2.8.0.

A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Wi-Fi connection handler of ADM allows an authenticated administrator to corrupt heap memory and terminate the affected CGI request by supplying an oversized Wi-Fi pre-shared key.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Insufficient bounds checks in the Link Aggregation handler of ASUSTOR ADM allow an authenticated administrator to submit an excessive number of interface tokens. Crafted requests can corrupt memory and terminate the affected privileged CGI process.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the initialization component of ADM. When the NAS is uninitialized, the endpoint accepts an unauthenticated sid query parameter and inserts its URL-decoded value into an inline JavaScript string without proper JavaScript-context encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when opened by a user, executes arbitrary JavaScript in the ADM management origin. Successful exploitation may allow manipulation of the setup page and execution of same-origin requests in the victim's browser. The vulnerability is limited to the first-run initialization state.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the IP block management component of ADM due to insufficient input validation and bounds checking. This vulnerability may allow an authenticated administrator to cause memory corruption, potentially resulting in application crashes or denial of service (DoS).
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A potential stack-based buffer overflow exists in ADM Defender Firewall configuration handling. Before the fix, firewall policy processing used string operations without sufficient destination-size checks and did not consistently validate array bounds. Malformed or oversized configuration data may cause an out-of-bounds write and corrupt stack memory.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An externally controlled format string vulnerability in the Snapshot CGI components of ADM allows an authenticated administrator to cause repeatable premature termination of affected privileged CGI requests by supplying crafted input.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A format string vulnerability has been reported in the Internal Backup of ADM. User-controlled input from the source_folders parameter is passed by internalbackup.cgi to a shared string-copy routine in libbackup.so.0.0 and used directly as the format-string argument to snprintf() without corresponding variadic arguments. This may allow an authenticated attacker to disclose process memory addresses or trigger unintended memory writes that terminate the affected CGI process.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.
The log viewer of Zoraxy admin panel fails to neutralize the output properly, that may cause an arbitrary script to be executed on the administrator's browser.

Dynamic Product Gallery for WooCommerce before 3.6.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to inject arbitrary JavaScript via the product_id attribute of the [wc_product_dgallery] and [wc_product_dynamic_gallery] shortcodes. The parse_shortcode_product_dynamic_gallery() function passes product_id only through esc_attr(), and get_gallery_main() prints it unescaped into the a3-wc-dynamic-gallery-init-inline-script inline script as part of a JavaScript variable name, so a value such as 342;alert(document.domain)// breaks out of the declaration. The injected script executes in the browser of any user who views the post, including editors or administrators who preview or approve it.

Fusion through 1.3.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass private-address protection by submitting URLs to the POST /api/feeds/validate endpoint. Attackers can supply a public URL that redirects or links to loopback, private, or link-local addresses, making feedfinder request internal services and leak parsed titles in responses.

Anchr before 3.7.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to host HTML files by uploading them through the image upload feature with a spoofed image content type. Attackers can upload an .html file served via GET /api/image/:id from the Anchr origin, running script that steals the victim's localStorage session token for account takeover.

In ParseAdvertisingReports of extended_low_energy_scanner.cc, there is a possible out of bounds read due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to local information disclosure with System execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

The AIL Framework web application contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its dashboard templates. In the home dashboard (dashboard.html), the hunter trackers dashboard (trackers_dashboard.html), and the objects dashboard (objs_dashboard.html), object global identifiers (GIDs) derived from filenames or message IDs were interpolated directly into inline JavaScript event handler attributes (onmouseenter/onmouseleave) within HTML anchor tags. Because the GID value was placed inside a single-quoted JavaScript string literal within an HTML attribute, an attacker who could control the GID value (for example, by crafting a filename or message ID containing a single quote) could break out of the string context and inject arbitrary JavaScript code that would execute in the context of any user viewing the dashboard.

Additionally, in dynamically generated JavaScript code within the same templates, object identifiers were concatenated into HTML strings and inline event handler registrations without sufficient encoding, presenting a similar injection surface. The AJAX tooltip lookup also concatenated the raw GID into a URL without encoding, which could be leveraged for further manipulation.

The vulnerability requires that an attacker be able to influence the GID value stored in the application (e.g., through a file upload or message creation with a crafted name) and that a victim subsequently visits one of the affected dashboard pages and hovers over the affected object link. Successful exploitation allows execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session, potentially leading to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim.

MISP is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in its correlation management functionality.

The top-correlation cache regeneration and occurrence count regeneration actions were accessible via bodyless GET requests and were triggered from the admin interface using plain hyperlinks rather than POST forms. Because these state-changing operations did not require a POST method and were reachable through simple URL navigation, an attacker who can induce an authenticated administrator to visit a malicious page or click a crafted link can trigger these operations without the administrator's explicit consent.

Impact:
- Unintended triggering of resource-intensive correlation regeneration processes
- Potential disruption of correlation data processing and increased server load
- No direct data disclosure or corruption is evidenced

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

MISP contains a vulnerability in its password reset (forgot password) functionality where the base URL used to construct the reset link sent by email could be derived from the HTTP request's Host header rather than from an explicitly configured value.

An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted request with a malicious Host header. If the application's base URL was not explicitly configured (MISP.baseurl or MISP.external_baseurl), the bootstrap would derive it from the request, and the resulting password reset email would contain a link pointing to the attacker-controlled domain. When the victim clicks the link, they are directed to the attacker's site, enabling credential phishing or token theft.

Preconditions:
- The password reset feature (allow_password_forgotten) is enabled
- MISP.baseurl and MISP.external_baseurl are not explicitly set to trusted values
- The victim initiates or is targeted for a password reset

Impact:
- Phishing: victim is redirected to an attacker-controlled URL instead of the legitimate MISP instance
- Potential credential compromise if the victim enters credentials on the attacker's site
- No direct compromise of the MISP server itself

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

A vulnerability has been found in KeudellCoding User Location Map up to 1.2.5. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file resources/humhub.usermap.js of the component MapView Widget. The manipulation of the argument displayname leads to cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 1.3.0 addresses this issue. The identifier of the patch is c49a5fcdb289808378836c19d4da199913798a50. The affected component should be upgraded.

Question2Answer through 1.8.8 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the qa-include/ajax/version.php admin version-check handler that allows authenticated administrators to make the server send arbitrary HTTP GET requests. Attackers can supply a loopback, private-network, or cloud metadata address in the uri POST parameter with isCore=true to read internal service responses returned in the Ajax output.

A security flaw has been discovered in yangzongzhuan RuoYi up to 4.8.3. Affected is the function renderUserCards of the file ruoyi-admin/src/main/resources/templates/system/role/view.html of the component Role Management User-View. The manipulation of the argument Username results in cross site scripting. The attack may be launched remotely. The patch is identified as 04db82c3c85593921ab8be48a4b3016866eaa97e. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.

A vulnerability was detected in osCommerce 4.14.63493. The affected element is an unknown function of the component Backend Administration List Controller. Performing a manipulation of the argument order[0][dir] results in sql injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security vulnerability has been detected in osCommerce 4.14.63493. Impacted is the function actionOrdersbatch of the file lib/backend/controllers/OrdersController.php of the component Orders Batch Processing. Such manipulation of the argument orders leads to sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Frappe before 15.126.0 and 16.x before 16.55.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows Dashboard Manager users to pollute Object.prototype by storing __proto__ keys in Dashboard Chart custom_options. When any user, including administrators, views a dashboard rendering the chart, Object.assign merges attacker properties into Object.prototype, altering Frappe desk client behavior for that session.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.19.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the sanitize-svg function that allows authenticated users to bypass filtering through unescaped re-serialization. Attackers with file edit permission can upload SVGs using entity-encoded or CDATA-wrapped markup or attribute quote breakouts to execute JavaScript in the Penpot origin when victims open them.

Sustainsys.Saml2 before 1.0.4 and 2.x before 2.11.1 contains an improper signature verification vulnerability that allows attackers to tamper with signed parameters by exploiting mis-parsing in CheckSignature() of Saml2RedirectBinding.cs. Attackers can append data after an extra '=' in RelayState of an intercepted or replayed Redirect-binding message, causing applications to trust the tampered value.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in Notifier#invite that allows authenticated users to inject HTML or markdown into invitation emails through unescaped profile names. Attackers can set profile first or last names containing raw HTML, links, or images so invitation emails sent from the pod render spoofed content in recipients' mail clients.

A security flaw has been discovered in Skyvern-AI Skyvern 1.0.56. The affected element is the function classify_url of the file skyvern/forge/sdk/browser_egress_policy.py. The manipulation results in server-side request forgery. The attack may be performed from remote. Upgrading to version 1.0.57 is sufficient to fix this issue. The patch is identified as 10b8d829c2750ebf62f2b70dec0e288297e752dd. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability was identified in Skyvern-AI Skyvern 1.0.56. Impacted is the function classify_url of the file skyvern/forge/sdk/browser_egress_policy.py. The manipulation leads to server-side request forgery. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 1.0.57 is recommended to address this issue. The identifier of the patch is 10b8d829c2750ebf62f2b70dec0e288297e752dd. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the CRM module because notes on Leads and Opportunities are saved without passing through the HTML sanitiser. Authenticated users with the Sales User role can save a note containing a crafted payload that executes in another user's session when they open the record, acting with that user's permissions.

Vikunja from 0.9.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows project admins to view share creators' email addresses via the link share list endpoint. Attackers with admin permission can request the project shares endpoint and read the shared_by email field, exposing addresses of creators including former project members.

Admidio from 5.0.16 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with folder upload rights to store JavaScript by uploading SVG files served inline. Attackers can upload a script-bearing SVG that downloadFile() serves as image/svg+xml inline without nosniff or CSP, executing on the Admidio origin for viewers including unauthenticated visitors.

Admidio before 5.0.18 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to keep account access after a forgot-password reset because User::setPassword() deletes sessions using the visitor ID instead of the reset user's usr_id. Attackers already holding a victim's session or remember-me cookie can continue using it after the victim resets the password, keeping authenticated access to the account.

Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject JavaScript by saving a crafted value in their STREET profile field. Attackers can break out of the unencoded title attribute in members_assignment_data.php with an onmouseover handler that executes in the session of role managers hovering over the address icon.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Icon API: Menu submodule of the Drupal 7 Icon API module. When a menu item is configured with the Title Wrapper option enabled, the value of the Title Wrapper Class field is output directly into an HTML attribute without sanitization or escaping. A user with the "administer menu icons" permission can inject a payload such as `title" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)` that is rendered verbatim on every page displaying the affected menu item, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who interacts with the menu link. This can lead to session theft, account hijacking, and further attacks against site users.

This issue affects Icon API 7.1.0.

Kartones flask-calendar before commit bfde72e contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because task_details_for_markup returns unescaped content rendered with the |safe filter. Authenticated shared calendar members can store script in task details that executes for other members, letting attackers read and modify their private calendars.

Pydici through 2026.11.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by storing HTML in contact names rendered unescaped in the contact detail mermaid diagram. Attackers with contact edit permission can store malicious markup that Contact.relationData() interpolates and contact_detail.html renders with the safe filter, executing script in victims' sessions.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with edit rights to bypass the sanitize-svg-element blocklist using namespace-prefixed SVG elements. Attackers can upload SVGs containing elements like x:script or attributes like x:onload, which are served inline as image/svg+xml to run JavaScript in victims' Penpot sessions.

Joomla Extension - joomlatools.com - Server-side request forgery in URL uploads in DOCman extension < 6.2.2 - The URL proxy and URL upload features were available to users below manager level and fetched arbitrary addresses, allowing server-side requests to internal or private network resources.

A vulnerability has been identified in webauthn-kotlin versions 1.1.0 through 1.1.3, where an exported device-credential authentication activity launches attacker-supplied intents without validation, potentially allowing a malicious application on the same Android device to access application-protected data, depending on the host application’s content-provider configuration.

An improper export control defect in ChatEventDispatchActivity (com.vivo.agent.business.chatmode.activity.ChatEventDispatchActivity) of Vivo Assistant allows a local malicious application to execute voice commands without user interaction via a crafted Intent, which may lead to unauthorized phone calls, SMS sending, access to private data such as location and calendar entries, and modification of system settings

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in example data generation and BreezingForms import in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Example data generation and the BreezingForms import did not check the core.create permission for the affected forms, allowing backend users to create records without permission.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Improper per-form authorization for field management in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Field creation, editing and ordering checked permissions against a user-supplied form ID instead of the form the field belongs to, allowing backend users to manage fields of other forms.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing authorization and CSRF checks in reset and check-in tasks in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The tasks to reset submitted data and to check in forms lacked authorization checks and CSRF protection.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in form creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The createForm task of the form creator did not check the core.create permission, allowing backend users without create permission to create forms.

InfoScan uses hard-coded cryptographic keys and initialization-vector values in its database-encryption implementation. The application uses these values to encrypt the MongoDB password before storing it in the Windows registry. Because the cryptographic material is embedded in the distributed application, an individual with access to the encrypted registry value and the application code may be able to recover the database password.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - IDOR in backend data export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The backend export did not correctly verify permissions for the exported form, allowing backend users to export data of forms they are not authorized to access.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by crafting og:video:secure_url values. Attackers can post links to pages whose allowlisted-prefix video URL contains a quote and onload handler, executing script in readers' sessions when they click the video preview.

Modoboa before 2.13.0 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability that allows Resellers or users with domain add or change permission to inject rspamd DKIM selector map entries by supplying an unvalidated dkim_key_selector through the relay domain API. Attackers can embed a carriage return in the selector to override another tenant's domain selector, causing rspamd to sign its outgoing mail with a nonexistent selector and fail DKIM verification.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the fulltext and vector index query generator of the sharded property database in Neo4j Enterprise Edition 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 allows an authenticated user holding ACCESS, CREATE INDEX and NAME MANAGEMENT privileges to inject Cypher that is accepted for execution on a property shard, in the session of any user who later queries the index, via a crafted index name containing a single quote. The impact is bounded by the privileges of the querying user.

flowintel contains a CSV injection vulnerability in its audit log CSV export functionality. Attacker-influenced text recorded in audit logs could be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas when an administrator opened the exported CSV file in a spreadsheet application.

The vulnerable behavior allowed an attacker who could influence audit log content (for example by generating network traffic that is captured and logged) to embed formula-like strings (such as =CMD() or =HYPERLINK()) into audit entries. When the resulting CSV export was opened in a spreadsheet application, these strings could be executed as formulas, potentially leading to data exfiltration, data manipulation, or execution of further malicious actions within the spreadsheet context.

Preconditions:
- An attacker must be able to influence content that is recorded in flowintel audit logs.
- An administrator or user must export the audit logs to CSV and open the file in a spreadsheet application that interprets formulas.

Security impact:
- Potential information disclosure from the spreadsheet or linked resources.
- Potential integrity impact on data within the spreadsheet application.
- No direct compromise of the flowintel application itself.

Affected version: <4.1.0

ScreenTinker before 3.2.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the GET /api/kiosk/:id/render endpoint that allows users with kiosk page edit rights to store javascript: URLs in page buttons. Attackers can trigger script execution in the dashboard origin when an administrator activates the button, hijacking the victim's session and taking full control of the instance.

An incorrect
permission assignment vulnerability in Omada SDN Controller prior to 6.2.20 may
cause a database backup generated during the uninstall workflow to remain
readable by other local users on the host. 





Successful
exploitation requires local, low-privileged access to the affected host and a
retained uninstall backup. An attacker meeting these conditions could access
the backup and disclose controller data without controller credentials.

Obot from 0.14.0 before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Power Users to bypass outbound protections by supplying unspecified addresses, IPv6 transition addresses, or registry icon URLs. Attackers can add remote MCP servers pointing to 0.0.0.0, ::, or NAT64/6to4/Teredo addresses embedding blocked IPv4 addresses to probe internal services for reachability.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in winCRM. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow a remote user to send a specially crafted URL to the victim and steal their session data by allowing JavaScript code to be injected in 'Tarea' parameter in '/Tareas/TareasCrear?ddv=cal'.

cPanel & WHM 11.134.0.13 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the mpidentity parameter of /mailman/listinfo. Attackers can send crafted requests with a script-context breakout payload in mpidentity to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-06-08.

Retool versions 3.253.0 before 3.253.19, 3.254.0 before 3.284.12, and 3.285.0 before 3.300.4 contain a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in the custom-component-collections.html postMessage handler that imports received code without origin validation. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted postMessage events that load attacker-controlled code via data:text/javascript URIs to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-04-22.

Bagisto 2.1.0 before 2.2.1 contains a client-side template injection vulnerability in the search page where the 'query' parameter is rendered unescaped inside a Vue app root. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted VueJS template expressions to the /bagisto-common/search endpoint via the 'query' parameter to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

phpLDAPadmin 1.1.0 before 1.2.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the dn parameter of cmd.php?cmd=template_engine. Attackers can supply an unparseable dn value that pretty_print_dn returns unescaped in the 'No such entry' error, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Tiki Wiki CMS Groupware 12.12 through 12.14, 15.5 before 18.10, 19.0 before 21.9, 22.0 before 24.3, and 25.0 contain a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the objectId parameter of tiki-ajax_services.php. Attackers can send a crafted GET request with the comment controller and list action to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

SLiMS Senayan Library Management System 9.4.0 before 9.4.2 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the destination parameter of /index.php?p=member, which is echoed unmodified into the login form action attribute. Unauthenticated attackers can craft a malicious destination value to inject script and hijack PHPSESSID sessions of victims who access the link. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

JoomBri Careers 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the 'keyword' parameter of the /for-jobseekers/search-jobs endpoint in com_jbcareers. Attackers can craft malicious URLs using an attribute-breakout payload with onfocus and autofocus to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Reddit Top RSS through commit 5e38bfd contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the unescaped score GET parameter. Attackers can craft links with a score value that closes the input value attribute in html.php, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

PMB 7.3.1 before 7.3.15 and 7.4.x before 7.4.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script through unescaped POST parameter names. Attackers can send crafted parameter names to opac_css/index.php extended_search, which empr.inc.php and languages.inc.php reflect into hidden form inputs to execute JavaScript. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Gnuboard5 5.0.1 before 5.3.3.3 and 5.4.0.1 before 5.4.0.2 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the arr_ajax_msg parameter. Attackers can craft GET requests to /plugin/sms5/ajax.sms_emoticon.php, where common.php's @extract($_GET) injects the value into the echoed JSON output, executing script in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Latvijas Valsts radio un televīzijas centrs (LVRTC)
eParakstītājs 3.0 version 1.10.0-resolute allows an unauthenticated remote
attacker to cause HTTP GET requests from a user's workstation by convincing the
user to open a crafted signed eDOC file. Automatic certificate validation
retrieves a signer-controlled Authority Information Access (AIA) caIssuers URL
and follows redirects without restricting the destination, enabling blind SSRF
to loopback and private-network services. Additionally, unrestricted loading of
local file URIs (such as file:///dev/zero) causes unbounded memory buffering
resulting in Denial of Service (OutOfMemoryError). In automated server
verification pipelines with UI:N, impact scales up to CVSS 8.6 High.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with media upload rights to bypass the upload sanitizer. Attackers can upload SVG files with inner extensions like .svg.defaults, payloads that crash the fail-open sanitizer, or unblocked .xml/.xhtm files to run script when administrators open the raw file URL.

NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into rich text cells, which are sanitized only with DOMPurify's default policy. Attackers can place a page-sized spoofed sign-in form or remote image in a cell to harvest passwords and disclose viewer IP addresses in expanded records, gallery and kanban cards, and shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in mention text. Attackers can break out of the single-quoted data-id attribute in comments or rich text cells to overlay or rearrange the interface for other viewers.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privilege control panel users to inject JavaScript by poisoning cached license data. Attackers can store a malicious licensed domain via the app/process-api-response-headers endpoint, which executes unescaped in administrators' dashboard license-mismatch warnings.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a data tampering vulnerability in the Distributed Pixel Cache that allows adjacent attackers to modify pixel data in transit between client and server. Attackers who can observe or modify the network path between a configured DPC client and server can tamper with pixel data to alter the resulting image.

WWBN AVideo from 11.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with streaming permission to inject HTML by supplying an unvalidated url parameter to plugin/LiveLinks/play.php. Attackers can embed a --> sequence to escape the HTML comment in liveVideo.php, creating a shareable link that executes JavaScript in any visitor's session.

The SUSE NeuVector image scanner before version 4.331 writes each per-scan task request to a temporary file on disk with mode 0644 (world-readable). This could allow local attackers to gain the registry access credentials of the scanned images.
Tanium addressed an improper input validation vulnerability in Core Content - MSSQL.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. From 3.48 until 3.69.1, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py reads untrusted model or skill output from workspace/run*/outputs/ and embeds it with json.dumps into viewer.html inside an inline script without escaping HTML metacharacters. A crafted output can close the script element and execute JavaScript when an operator generates and opens the viewer. The maintainer also confirmed that DOM-based injection through renderGrades and renderBenchmark innerHTML survives transport-only escaping, so affected render sinks must neutralize the content. Executed script can read embedded prompts and outputs, alter the viewer DOM, or modify saved feedback. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user could trick a user that holds a role with the ueba_can_view_ui capability into opening a link that the unauthenticated user creates for the User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Overview dashboard. When the user opens the link, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who opens the link. The commands could expose or modify some data available to the user who opens the link and partially disrupt search processing.
The vulnerability is possible because the User and Entity Behavior Analytics Overview dashboard does not escape dashboard filter values from the link before substituting the values into SPL searches.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see UEBA dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.8/analytics/ueba-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

Mattermost Plugins versions <=12.-1 11.0.11 11.11.7 11.2.10.0 fail to verify that the caller can post in a run's channel when executing a checklist slash command which allows an authenticated run participant to post arbitrary messages into a private channel they are not a member of via the checklist item run endpoint. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00730
In JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.9.22 command injection was possible via file names in code review

An unencrypted RSA private key for a default HTTPS certificate is included in GeoVision GV-EBD4700 firmware V1.11 (A02-GV-EBD4700_V1.11_2026_10_13.zip) at /program/www/ssl_cert.pem and copied to /config/ssl_cert.pem during initialization. When HTTPS is enabled using the default certificate, a network on-path attacker who obtains the firmware image can use the exposed private key to present an identical certificate and intercept HTTPS traffic. HTTPS is disabled by default .


  *  

Only impacts deployments where an administrator enables HTTPS and retains the default certificate. Because the private key is publicly distributed in the firmware image, an on-path attacker can impersonate the device with an identical certificate fingerprint, bypassing fingerprint checks and stored certificate exceptions (potentially capturing credentials if a user clicks through the expired-certificate warning).

SolarWinds Serv-U is affected by denial-of-service 
vulnerability that may allow users with privileged access 
to cause too much memory usage, causing the server to 
reject new connections. A specific configuration is 
required, and an SMTP server must be set up.

Uncontrolled resource allocation in Elasticsearch mapping updates can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with index-management privileges can submit specially crafted mapping updates that are expanded into multiple large in-memory representations. The amplification during request parsing and mapping updates can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node.

An issue in Kibana allows Elasticsearch transforms in directly uploaded integration packages to run with Kibana's internal system identity instead of the installing user's privileges. A user with Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges in a single Kibana space could access or modify data they are not authorized to access, including agent policies from other spaces. This could disclose sensitive information or lead to command execution on managed Elastic Agent hosts.

An unauthenticated stored and reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the embedded web interface of Frontier Smart Technologies Venice X FS2340 running IR4.9 allows a network attacker with access to the interface to inject attacker-controlled JavaScript that may execute in the browser of a user accessing affected content.



Successful exploitation may allow the attacker to access information available within the browser's security context or perform actions through the affected web interface with the privileges of the affected user.



During authorized security testing, certain crafted JavaScript and code-injection payloads were also observed to cause the embedded web interface to crash and become temporarily unavailable on some tested software versions. This behavior represents a denial-of-service condition affecting the embedded web management interface; no device-level denial of service was established.

Aether Project AMF supports termination of NAS signalling, NAS ciphering & integrity protection, registration management, connection management, mobility management, access authentication and authorization, security context management. Prior to 3.1.6, a malformed NGAP PathSwitchRequest can contain a UESecurityCapabilities information element whose extensible APER bit-string representation has no bytes even though decoding reports no error. In ngap/handler.go, HandlePathSwitchRequest checks only whether the element is present before six index-zero reads of its encryption and integrity algorithm fields, causing an unrecovered panic in the NGAP receive goroutine and terminating the AMF. The described attacker is a rogue or compromised gNB on the N2 interface and additionally needs a registered UE's AMF-UE-NGAP-ID; a bare over-the-air UE cannot trigger the issue. This issue is fixed in version 3.1.6.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2, 2026.1.6 out-of-band data exfiltration via DNS resolution was possible in the Kotlin DSL sandbox
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 project administrators could read OAuth connection secrets of ancestor projects
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4 the Perforce Administrator Access password could be written to the server log

Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 3.2.4, the application/controllers/Lotw.php import() workflow passes the lotw_download_url configuration value to curl without scheme validation, accepts file:// content, and writes the response to a predictable path under ./uploads/ that can be retrieved through an unauthenticated HTTP request. A standard user can trigger the LotW import, although changing lotw_download_url normally requires installer administrator access, and related vulnerabilities can remove that prerequisite. The same missing status-validation pattern affects the LotW lotw_users fetch helper and per-user download helper. This exposes files readable by the www-data user, including environment data, mounted secrets, and application configuration. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.4.

A vulnerability in the web management and file transfer component of AOS web could allow an authenticated remote attacker to perform arbitrary file reads. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to access sensitive files on the underlying system, potentially exposing configuration data or credentials.

The WP Maps – Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, Mapbox, Store Locator with Search, Filters & Listings plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'csv_columns' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

The Meow Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'limit' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.9 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not verify that the acting user is authorised to modify the target post when saving a template, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to overwrite the content and type of an arbitrary post, including another user's published page, removing it from the front end.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the MPEG-4 Visual parser that allows attackers to read global memory via an uninitialized frame_rate_code index into Mpegv_frame_rate. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file that forces stream finalization before parser synchronization, crashing the process or leaking adjacent memory into the reported frame rate.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From versions 0.6.15 through 0.10.0, the value of a host-scoped credential header was exposed to other hosts via HTTP redirects. SendAuthenticatedWebRequestBlock attaches a host-scoped credential's headers to a request, but once a redirect took that request to a different origin, only three fixed header names (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie) were removed. A host-scoped credential's header names are free-form (the UI suggests X-API-Key), so a credential carried under any other name followed the redirect to the new origin. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

This vulnerability is associated with program files modules/ext.checkUser.tempAccounts/ipReveal.js. This issue affects MediaWiki - CheckUser Extension: from 1.46.0 before 1.46.3, 1.47.

This vulnerability is associated with program files modules/ext.checkUser/checkuser/checkUserHelper/buildUserElement.js. This issue affects MediaWiki - CheckUser Extension: from 1.45.0 before 1.45.7, from 1.46.0 before 1.46.3, 1.47.

This issue affects MediaWiki - CheckUser Extension: from 1.46.0 before 1.46.3, 1.47.

Astra WordPress theme before 4.14.0 contains an improper input neutralization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with contributor-level privileges to inject unescaped CSS by submitting a crafted overlay-opacity value in the ast-page-background-meta or ast-content-background-meta REST fields. Attackers can store a malicious payload that, when rendered, causes an uncaught TypeError leading to a fatal error and HTTP 500 denial of service on PHP 8.0+, or injects arbitrary CSS into the page's style block on PHP 7.x enabling UI redress and content spoofing.

ExAws.S3 constructs S3 ACL grant headers (such as x-amz-grant-read and x-amz-grant-full-control) in format_grant_header/1 by interpolating grantee identifiers into a quoted, comma-separated list without escaping. Grantee email and id values are wrapped in double quotes and joined with a comma, but double-quote, comma, and CR/LF characters in the value are not neutralized. An application that passes an attacker-influenced grantee value (for example an email address taken from a "share this object" feature) into an ACL grant option (grant_read, grant_write, grant_read_acp, grant_write_acp, or grant_full_control) lets the attacker close the quoted token and inject an additional grantee, such as the attacker's own canonical id or the predefined AllUsers group URI, into the header. S3 then applies the injected grantee, granting an arbitrary principal the same permission (up to full control or public access) in an unintended ACL grantee-injection and privilege-escalation issue.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability in the game assistant module. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality and integrity.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in vpk_read_header() in libavformat/vpk.c that computes a last block size not divisible by the channel count. Attackers can supply a crafted VPK file with a large channel count so the last audio packet exposes leftover heap memory contents.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an XML injection vulnerability in write_adaptation_set() in libavformat/webmdashenc.c that writes stream language metadata unescaped into the AdaptationSet lang attribute. Attackers can supply crafted WebM files whose track language contains quotes or angle brackets to inject attributes or elements, controlling segment URLs and representations in generated MPD manifests.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in rfc4175_handle_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_rfc4175.c that leaks heap contents into decoded video frames. Attackers can send RTP streams containing only some scan lines of a frame, leaving av_malloc buffer bytes uninitialized and exposing process heap memory in displayed, stored or re-streamed video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in amf_get_field_value2() in libavformat/rtmppkt.c that NUL-terminates truncated AMF strings at the declared length instead of bytes read. A malicious RTMP server, or connecting client in listen mode, can send truncated onStatus or _error strings to leak uninitialized stack memory through log messages.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an XML injection vulnerability in ttml_write_header() in libavformat/ttmlenc.c that writes stream language metadata unescaped into the xml:lang attribute. Attackers can supply media files, such as Matroska subtitle tracks with crafted Language values, to inject markup into converted TTML documents and alter downstream parsing or rendering.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in vmd_read_packet() in libavformat/sierravmd.c that leaves 16 packet bytes unwritten for Indeo3 frames. Attackers can supply a crafted VMD file with Indeo3 video to expose leftover heap contents in demuxed packets, such as stream-copied output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in nist_read_header() in libavformat/nistspheredec.c, where an inverted ff_alloc_extradata() return check leaves the embedded-shorten extradata byte uninitialized. Attackers can supply a crafted NIST SPHERE file declaring pcm,embedded-shorten coding to leak an uninitialized heap byte into copied output or trigger a NULL pointer write on allocation failure.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MXG demuxer's mxg_read_packet() that allows attackers to leak uninitialized heap memory through truncated marker segments. Attackers can supply a crafted MXG file ending in a truncated APP13 segment with a large declared length, causing uninitialized heap contents to be emitted as audio packet payload, for example into remuxed output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory use vulnerability in asfrtp_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c that allows malicious RTP sources to leak heap contents by supplying an oversized ASF packet length. Attackers controlling an RTSP server with an x-asf-pf payload can set len_off beyond the RTP payload so the ASF demuxer returns stale heap memory as demuxed media data.

The Zephyr TFTP client in subsys/net/lib/tftp/tftp_client.c does not check where the reply to its request comes from. After sending a read or write request to the configured server, send_request() accepts the first UDP datagram that arrives on the client's socket from any address and port. It then calls zsock_connect() to that sender, so the sender becomes the peer for the rest of the transfer. RFC 1350 requires a client to discard datagrams whose source does not match the transfer ID it expects.

A host that can send a UDP datagram to the client's ephemeral port before the real server replies can take over the transfer. It can reply from its own address and does not need to spoof the server. A host on the same network segment that sees the request can do this easily. An off-path attacker must guess the randomized ephemeral port and win the race, which is easier when the server is slow or unreachable. No authentication or user interaction is needed beyond the device starting a transfer through tftp_get() or tftp_put(), for example from an application or the net tftp shell command.

For tftp_get(), the attacker chooses the entire content handed to the application's data callback. For tftp_put(), the whole upload buffer is sent to the attacker. There is no memory corruption. TFTP itself has no authentication, and after the fix an attacker who can spoof the server's IP address can still interfere with a transfer. The fix checks the server's address on the first reply and the full address and port on every later datagram, and drops mismatches without using up the transfer's retries.

MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Overmind server preview's analyst data badge component. When rendering the analyst data link for a remote attribute, the remote server's UUID value was inserted into an inline JavaScript event handler using only HTML entity encoding, which is insufficient to prevent breakout from the JavaScript string context within the HTML attribute.

An attacker who can control or influence the UUID value of a remote attribute (for example, through a malicious or compromised upstream MISP server sharing data via Overmind) could inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the context of the victim's MISP session when the analyst data badge is clicked.

Preconditions:
- The victim must be authenticated to a MISP instance with Overmind enabled.
- The victim must view a remote event preview containing the crafted UUID.
- The victim must interact with (click) the analyst data badge element.

Security impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session.
- Potential theft of session credentials, manipulation of page content, or initiation of unauthorized actions on behalf of the authenticated user.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a stored cross-site script (XSS) vulnerability in the event review page used for merge, import, and enrichment workflows.

Object references displayed on this page include the UUID, name, and meta-category of the referenced object. These values originate from imported data (another event, a module result, or an import file) and were rendered into the HTML output without any encoding or sanitization.

An attacker who can supply or influence imported MISP-format data can embed arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the referenced object's UUID, name, or meta-category fields. When a user views the review page, the malicious script executes in the user's browser context.

Preconditions:
- The attacker must be able to introduce data into a MISP instance (e.g., via import, module enrichment, or event merge).
- A victim user must open the affected review page in a browser.

Security impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application.
- Potential theft of session tokens, manipulation of user actions, or exfiltration of sensitive threat-intelligence data visible on the page.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the feed and server event preview pages. When a remote MISP instance (configured as a feed source or connected server) supplies object or reference UUIDs and IDs containing special characters, these values are rendered in the preview HTML without proper escaping.

The vulnerable behavior occurs in two contexts:

- HTML element identifiers and text content: Remote UUIDs and IDs are inserted into DOM element IDs and visible text without HTML encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML markup.
- Inline JavaScript event handlers: Remote UUIDs and IDs are embedded into onClick handler strings using only HTML escaping, which does not protect against JavaScript string-literal breakout. A crafted value containing a single quote can terminate the string and inject arbitrary JavaScript.

An attacker who controls a remote MISP instance (feed or server peer) can craft UUID or ID fields with a malicious payload. When an authenticated user on the victim instance views the corresponding event preview, the injected script executes in the user's browser within the MISP application origin, potentially allowing session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

A weakness has been identified in phpBB up to 3.3.19. Affected by this vulnerability is the function phpbb_get_user_rank of the file includes/acp/acp_ranks.php of the component Ranks Handler. This manipulation of the argument rank_image causes cross site scripting. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor confirms: "We have reviewed the report and intend to address the issue as part of our ongoing security hardening efforts. Given that exploitation requires authenticated administrative access, we consider this a low-priority issue. We will aim to include a fix in our next release and will notify you once it is available."

Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 contains a security bypass vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers to evade 'tagsecure' URL checks by escaping URLs in tags file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw fetch an attacker-controlled URL leaking environment variable values.

Kitty 0.43.0 before 0.51.0 contains a terminal escape sequence injection vulnerability that allows attackers to emit escape sequences by crafting malicious file or archive member names. When a victim highlights such an entry in the choose-files kitten preview panel, unsanitized names are written raw, enabling OSC 52 clipboard overwrites, OSC 8 links, window title changes, or screen spoofing.

A weakness has been identified in twogood unshield up to 1.6.2. Impacted is the function unshield_get_cab_descriptor of the file lib/libunshield.c of the component Cabinet Descriptor Parser. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack requires local access. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

OceanWP WordPress Theme before 4.2.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the oceanwp_edd_terms_list() function in inc/edd/edd-helpers.php, which allows authenticated users with EDD download category creation permissions to inject malicious JavaScript by crafting a category name that breaks out of an unescaped HTML title attribute. Attackers can create a category name containing an event-handler payload that executes in the browser of visitors who interact with the category link on the public EDD archive page, potentially compromising an administrator's session if they view the affected page while authenticated.

A weakness has been identified in continuedev continue 2.0.0/2.1.0. Affected is the function validateSearchAndReplaceFilepath of the file gui/src/util/clientTools/editImpl.ts of the component Edit Tool. Executing a manipulation can lead to path traversal. The attack requires local access. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Improper following of a certificate’s chain of trust in the remote-attestation verifier used to establish trust with Meta AI's confidential computing backend in WhatsApp for iOS before 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac Desktop before v2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android before v2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android before v2.26.23.70 could have allowed someone positioned within Meta infrastructure to bypass the hardware root of trust by presenting clients with a VCEK certificate signed by a key other than the hardware manufacturer’s. Any such VCEK Cert would first have to be published to the third-party binary transparency ledger used by WhatsApp Private Processing. The ledger shows that every published VCEK certificate chains to the hardware root of trust, confirming no exploitation.

flowintel contains multiple related flaws that allow an authenticated attacker to inject arbitrary HTML or script into pages viewed by other users.

- Timeline rendering: the timeline library's autolinking feature rewrote already-sanitised case notes and imported MISP attribute values into generated HTML link elements. Crafted text containing quote characters could break out of the generated attribute context, altering the surrounding markup and enabling script execution in the victim's browser.

- Search highlighting: the highlight injection logic used a regular expression to locate text between angle brackets and spliced <mark> elements into the resulting string. Because the pattern could match inside HTML attribute values, the rewrite could corrupt or inject content into attributes of already-sanitised markup, again leading to DOM-based cross-site scripting.

- Content-Type confusion: three analyser selection endpoints returned session-stored JSON strings with a text/html content type. A browser receiving such a response will parse and render the body as HTML, so any HTML or script embedded in the stored value is executed in the victim's context.

Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated user with the ability to create or import case content (notes, MISP attributes) containing specially crafted quote or angle-bracket sequences. The victim must subsequently open the affected case timeline, run a search, or request one of the selection endpoints.

Impact: successful exploitation yields DOM-based cross-site scripting in the victim's browser session, potentially allowing disclosure of case data, session manipulation, or execution of arbitrary actions under the victim's identity.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

A weakness has been identified in OSGeo shapelib up to 1.6.3. This vulnerability affects the function DBFCloneEmpty of the file dbfopen.c. This manipulation causes null pointer dereference. It is possible to launch the attack on the local host. Patch name: f79050a900d2a05529501b2b714b8f89067db071. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.
IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information due to improper access control.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.0, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared data model calculation. When a user who can run a search against the shared data model runs one, the injected SPL can run using the permissions of the user who ran the search. This could expose sensitive credentials to the user who created the shared data model.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not safely neutralize data model calculation fields before it includes them in generated searches.
For more information see About data models (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/build-a-data-model/about-data-models) in the Splunk documentation.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data used by the Credit Card Data Found dashboard. If another user who can access the dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Credit Card Data Found dashboard does not validate source and destination values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Credit Card Data Found (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/credit-card-data-found) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the edit_timeline capability could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a legacy investigation timeline entry. Another user that holds a role with the manage_all_investigations capability could later open the investigation and select Run Search from the timeline. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run the SPL stored by the first user using the permissions of the user who selected Run Search. The SPL stored by the first user could access data or perform actions available to the user who selected Run Search.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not treat stored investigation search content as a literal search before building the Search page link.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.3/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Add details to an investigation in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-7/user-guide/7.3/investigations/add-details-to-an-investigation-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's Device Configuration History page allows an authenticated attacker with view permission on a device to execute arbitrary JavaScript in another authenticated user's browser by enticing the victim to open a specially crafted link.
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 app widgets could perform API requests on behalf of viewing users without their consent

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows administrators with product editing permission to inject script via the products_name field. The unescaped name is rendered in the h1 heading of product detail and reviews pages, executing script in the browsers of shoppers and logged-in customers.

flowintel allows users with editor-level access to author case and task fields, including aggregated tags. When these records are exported as CSV, the field values are written verbatim into the output file.

Because no sanitisation is applied to user-supplied text before CSV serialisation, an attacker can store values that begin with spreadsheet formula triggers (such as =, +, -, @, or their fullwidth Unicode equivalents, or leading control/whitespace characters). When a victim opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application (e.g. Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc), the stored text is interpreted and executed as a live formula rather than displayed as literal text.

This can lead to unintended data manipulation within the spreadsheet, potential data exfiltration via formula functions, or execution of downstream commands depending on the spreadsheet application and its configuration.

The vulnerability requires the victim to actively open the CSV file in a spreadsheet application; the flowintel application itself is not directly compromised.

Affected: <4.1.0

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the unsanitized products_model field. Attackers with product editing permission can store JavaScript that executes in browsers of other administrators, storefront visitors, and customers viewing carts and order history.

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie builds the match regular expression for each path-scoped middleware from its mount path without collapsing duplicate slashes, even when the application enables the ignoreDuplicateSlashes router option. Under that option Fastify's router collapses duplicate slashes in both the registered route and the request path, so a mount path containing a doubled slash is served by the router at its single-slash form while the middleware's compiled match still requires the doubled slash and never matches. A path-scoped middleware such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting is therefore skipped while the router dispatches the request to the protected handler, without any authentication required. Applications are affected when they enable ignoreDuplicateSlashes and a middleware mount path reaches middie with a duplicate slash, most commonly when a plugin prefix that ends with a slash is joined to a mount path that starts with one. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid mount paths and plugin prefixes that introduce duplicate slashes.

A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.

SemanticMediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with the smw-patternedit right to inject script by seeding markup reference names in MediaWiki:Smw_allows_pattern. Once an editor annotates the matching Allows pattern value, AllowsPatternValue emits it unescaped on Special:Browse, executing JavaScript in every viewer's session.
PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V 1.1 is vulnerable to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in admin/search-invoices.php via the searchdata parameter.

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to sanitize terminal escape sequences when rendering server logs via {{mmctl logs}}, which allows an unauthenticated attacker to hijack a system administrator's clipboard or spoof terminal output via a crafted HTTP request whose logged content is later viewed with {{mmctl logs}}. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00753
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS in the Shared Resources build feature was possible
Dell PowerStore contains a CSV Injection vulnerability. A high-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to code execution on another user's workstation.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the orders_status_name parameter in admin/orders_status.php. Attackers with per-page order status access can store payloads that execute in other administrators' browsers when the unencoded status name is displayed.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the cross_sell_group_name parameter in admin/cross_sell_groups.php. Attackers with per-page access to cross-selling groups can store a script payload that executes in other administrators' browsers, including full administrators, when they view the group listing.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated memory when BGRO image data is imported. Attackers can supply crafted BGRO data for processing to crash the application or leak adjacent heap memory contents.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a null pointer dereference vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the process by using the -subimage option on a single-image list. Attackers can supply input producing an image list with only one image while -subimage is applied, causing a denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the TIFF decoder that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted TIFF image. Attackers can provide a malicious TIFF file that, when encoded in a specific output format, triggers a heap buffer over-write causing memory corruption.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the MVG decoder that allows attackers to read out-of-bounds memory by supplying a crafted file. Attackers can provide a malicious MVG file for processing to trigger the over-read, causing application crashes or exposure of heap memory contents.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability on Windows that allows attackers to evade path-based security policies by mixing forward slash and backslash separators. Attackers can supply crafted image file paths using alternate separators to read or write image files that the configured policy is intended to block.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to read from disallowed paths due to a missing policy check when decoding MPC files. Attackers can supply crafted MPC files that reference restricted locations to access files the configured security policy should block.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated heap memory by triggering the -copy operation. Attackers can supply crafted images or arguments processed with -copy to crash the application or disclose adjacent heap memory contents.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a stack overflow vulnerability in the MSVG decoder that allows attackers to crash the application by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit a malicious image for processing to exhaust the stack and terminate the application, causing denial of service.

SolarWinds Serv-U was found to be vulnerable to an 
unauthenticated HTTP response header injection
