victim's browser session.

When the rsyslog's `imuxsock` is parsing the TAG field from a message with a accepted shorter timestamp, the cursor used to read the message fields and the remaining message length to be read are left in a inconsistent state in relation to the content in the raw message, leading the module to read one byte past the end of the buffer holding the message.

The Simply Schedule Appointments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.13.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The stored payload is only rendered when an administrator navigates to the hidden support page (/wp-admin/admin.php?ssa-support-admin=1) and triggers the 'Fix appointment durations' action, a condition reliably engineered by the attacker by smuggling a '+1 day' suffix in the start_date field to create a persistent duration mismatch that routes the malicious booking through the vulnerable echo path. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (initial store via wp-comments-post.php) / CSV cell on import' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires an administrator to approve the attacker's review, then export and re-import it using the plugin's default column mapping, with the import taking the INSERT branch — which occurs automatically on any site whose database table prefix is not the literal 'wp_', when the CSV has no comment_ID mapping, or when the original review has been trashed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
A race condition was addressed with additional validation. This issue is fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2. An app may be able to access sensitive user data.

The Okta Client SDK for Python (okta-client-python) includes client authentication values (client_secret or JWT assertions) as query parameters in the front-channel authorization URL when executing the authorization code flow without Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR). When PAR is disabled, unsupported by the authorization server, or fails, the SDK falls back to standard authorization URL construction, transmitting these parameters via user-agent requests.

In Splunk Enterprise for Windows versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user that holds a role with the edit_user capability could create multiple user accounts that share the same user directory. This could expose user-specific configuration between those accounts, let one account modify configuration used by another account, or disrupt features that depend on separate user directories.
The vulnerability is caused by improper validation of usernames before Splunk Enterprise performs Windows filesystem operations. Windows removes trailing periods from directory names, so distinct usernames can resolve to the same user directory.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') vulnerability in Kayaport Ödeme Kuruluşu A.Ş. BulutTahsilat – Virtual POS Infrastructure allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

This issue affects BulutTahsilat – Virtual POS Infrastructure: through 2026-11-05.

The Kirki – Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (title attribute of <abbr>)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to run the Kirki Convert (migration) workflow on a page containing the attacker's approved comment, as the browser-side DOM parser decodes the kses-allowed abbr title attribute value into a raw XSS payload that is then persisted without sanitization and later rendered unescaped. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The OneLogin SAML SSO WordPress plugin before 3.7.1 does not validate a user-supplied parameter before using it to redirect an already-authenticated user, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect a logged-in user to an arbitrary external domain via a crafted link (e.g. for phishing).

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki - GuidedTour Extension. This vulnerability is associated with program files modules/ext.guidedTour.lib.internal.js. This issue affects MediaWiki - GuidedTour Extension: 1.45, 1.46, 1.47.

An unauthenticated attacker can trick a local user into generating an offline boot application from a malicious CODESYS project, causing the affected products to write files in arbitrary directories on the engineering workstation. The destination path is derived from attacker-controlled project data, whereas the file name and file contents are generated by the affected products and are not attacker-controlled.

Incomplete cleanup during VMRUN error handling could allow access to a Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP) guest register state, potentially resulting in information disclosure and impacts to confidentiality.

vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the authenticated user's two-factor authentication without requiring password confirmation. Because the state-changing operation was reachable via GET, an attacker with a basic account could embed an image element (or any other GET-triggering markup) in a comment pointing to that endpoint. When a victim with 2FA enabled viewed the comment, their browser silently issued the GET request, disabling the victim's second factor of authentication. No CSRF token was enforced on the GET path, and no password was required to confirm the action. Second, the comment detail page (/comment/<uuid>) rendered unpublished comments to any visitor who possessed the URL, bypassing the moderation workflow that was intended to keep such content hidden until approved. The API correctly restricted access, but the web view did not enforce the same authorization check. The combined effect allows an attacker to degrade a victim's account security (removal of 2FA) through a single page view and to read content that was not yet approved for public release.

A vulnerability was detected in smartalock wireguard-lwip up to cfba91666590e86bd67842c71cedf9a423be823a. This affects the function wireguard_generate_unique_index of the file src/wireguard.c of the component Session Index Allocator. The manipulation of the argument receiver_index results in allocation of resources. The attack is only possible with local access. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in intrusion detection data. Another user who holds the "pci_user" role could later select the corresponding row in the Intrusion Detection and Prevention System Alert Activity Details panel. The report could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the row. The commands could access data and perform actions available to the user who selected the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Intrusion Detection and Prevention System Alert Activity report does not treat intrusion detection values as literal search values when it builds the details drilldown search.
For more information see Reports (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/user-manual/8.7/using-the-splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/reports) and Configure users and roles (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-the-app/configure-users-and-roles) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data that populates the System Misconfigurations report. Another user with access to the report could later select a related row. The System Misconfigurations report could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the row. The commands could access or modify data available to the user who selected the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the System Misconfigurations report does not treat values from the Vulnerabilities data model as literal search values when it builds drilldown searches.
For more information see System Misconfigurations (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/system-misconfigurations) and Configure users and roles (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-the-app/configure-users-and-roles) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data that populates the Malware Activity report. Another user with access to the report could later click a related row. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who clicked the row. The commands could access data and perform actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Malware Activity report does not treat values from the Malware data model as literal search values when it builds drilldown searches.
For more information see Malware Activity (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/malware-activity) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject malicious content into a Splunk Web view. When another authenticated user opens the affected view in Splunk Web, the injected content executes unauthorized JavaScript code within the viewing user's browser session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Web does not properly validate content in a view definition before rendering the view.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient sanitization of objective identifiers in the SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) objectives report allows an authenticated user with content upload permissions to inject malicious scripts. When another user views the report, the injected script executes in their browser session, potentially allowing the attacker to access sensitive information or perform unauthorized actions on their behalf.

Mattermost versions 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1, 11.7.x <= 11.7.12 fail to validate the format of configured database connection strings before redacting them, which allows a party with access to a generated Support Packet or server log files to recover plaintext database credentials when the connection string is configured in a non-URL format.. Adobe Experience Manager is affected by a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability that could be abused by a low-privileged attacker to inject malicious scripts into vulnerable form fields. Elasticsearch ES|QL data-source and dataset registration can write storage credentials or pre-signed URL signatures to the audit log in plaintext. In affected versions, request definitions are not appropriately filtered before request-body or URL-query auditing. An attacker with access to these logs can obtain credentials for the customer's external storage. The issue affects deployments with ES|QL federation enabled and audit logging configured to record the affected request information.

The UiChemy – Convert Figma, Prompts and AI Builds to Elementor, Gutenberg and Bricks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'head' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.67 through 0.11.2, an External API key created while a user was a member of an organization keeps working in that organization after the user is removed. A former member holding such a key with the WRITE_GRAPH and WRITE_LIBRARY scopes, or USE_TOOLS for schedules, can add workflows, library entries, and schedules to the organization, where remaining members can see them. The key gives no read access to the organization's data. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.67 to 0.11.2, organization and team billing-manager roles intended only for spend management are treated as ordinary members across workflow, run, library, and marketplace routes. Although the role matrix in autogpt_platform/autogpt_libs/autogpt_libs/auth/permissions.py withholds run access and workflow creation, those routes do not enforce the matrix and their underlying membership lookups ignore the caller's role. As a result, a team billing manager can read team workflows and other members' runs (including inputs, outputs, and per-node data), while an organization billing manager can view shared workflows and runs and create workflows and marketplace listings; neither can modify or delete other members' workflows. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, AutoPilot prices block calls using model-supplied input but executes them with the server-resolved credential. Supplying a syntactically valid placeholder credential causes the price rule to evaluate to zero, skipping both the balance check and debit while still running paid blocks on the operator's credential. An issue was discovered in Kibana where a user with the Synthetics All privilege in one space can access Fleet agent policy metadata from other spaces through a product API endpoint. This could lead to the unauthorized disclosure of operational metadata across spaces the user is not authorized to view.

Elasticsearch ES|QL query responses can disclose dataset storage locations and provider identity details to users who are allowed to query a dataset but cannot read its definition. Storage paths and storage-client error text can appear in read-failure messages or query-profile plan strings. An authenticated dataset reader can obtain this information without permission to view the dataset configuration. This issue does not disclose stored credentials or the dataset contents beyond the caller's query access.

Incorrect authorization in Elasticsearch columnar indices can bypass field-level security for geo_shape values. An authenticated user with access to an affected index can obtain denied geometry values through the internal source-geometry representation even when field-level security excludes the corresponding field. This discloses field data that the user is not authorized to read.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability. An unauthenticated remote attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to cause denial of service condition.

Improper access control in the PAM provider endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated non-administrator PAM user to read provider configuration metadata via a missing permission check on the provider details route.

The CoE entry gate accepts frames with mbxheader.length as low as COE_MINIMUM_LENGTH (8), but a normal SDO Download requires at least COE_HEADERSIZE (10) bytes of CoE payload to carry its header fields. With mbxheader.length of 8 or 9, the segmented-transfer branch misevaluates due to unsigned wrap, leaving the declared SDO size unclamped. copy2mbx then reads that many bytes starting past the end of the actual payload and writes them into the object buffer.

EOE_set_ip reads each network parameter field (MAC, IP, subnet, gateway, DNS IP, DNS name) from the mailbox payload before checking whether the payload is large enough to contain them. The single bounds check at the end of the function does not prevent the reads from happening. A master can send a Set-IP frame with all flags set and mbxheader.length equal to the minimum, causing all reads to access memory past the end of the payload.

The WSMS (formerly WP SMS): SMS Notifications, OTP Login and WooCommerce SMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 7.2.14. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to send arbitrary SMS messages to attacker-chosen phone numbers from the site's trusted sender ID, incurring per-message gateway charges to the site owner and enabling SMS spam or phishing campaigns.

The Salon Booking System – Appointment Booking for Salons, Barbershops & Spas plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 10.31.16. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite arbitrary users' user meta fields, including the _sln_phone and _sln_sms_prefix meta of administrator accounts, and create bookings attributed to arbitrary users. This is exploitable on default installations because reCAPTCHA is disabled by default, causing the booking endpoint's permission check to return true for any authenticated user without a meaningful authorization gate.

Rocket.Chat's POST /api/v1/chat.sendMessage endpoint improperly validates nested message properties, allowing authenticated users with standard privileges to inject arbitrary message metadata that is persisted and trusted by the server and clients. This can lead to persistent room-level denial of service, stored HTML/iframe injection, unauthorized modification of other users' private starred messages, permission bypass and attribution spoofing for pinned messages, forged edit attribution, and invisible user mentions.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, sl_createCNIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c assumes every element of kMDQueryItemArray points to an eight-byte uint64_t and copies sizeof(uint64_t) bytes from the indexed p->dd_talloc_array element without validating the element's talloc type or allocation size. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can use FPSpotlightRPC to supply a mixed-type sl_array_t containing a shorter boolean, nil, or string element, and an unauthenticated client can reach the same path when the optional guest UAM and a guest-accessible volume are enabled. The resulting eight-byte read extends beyond the shorter element's heap allocation and supplies an internal CNID filter; no confidentiality channel, write primitive, or code execution was demonstrated, while a production crash would require additional heap placement conditions. The container-type validation added for CVE-2023-42464 does not validate each element inside an accepted sl_array_t and therefore does not resolve this issue. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the HTML bookmark import action in app/Actions/ImportHtmlBookmarks.php uses the global Link::whereUrl() lookup instead of restricting duplicate detection to the importing user. An authenticated user can submit a chosen URL and distinguish the skipped response count from the queued count to learn whether any account has saved that URL, including as a PRIVATE bookmark. The oracle reveals URL existence but does not directly return the bookmark contents or owner. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

The GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 4.16.7.2. This is due to missing nonce validation on the `give_render_donor_view()` function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reassign an arbitrary GiveWP donor record to an arbitrary WordPress user via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link. The resulting association changes donor-account ownership and can satisfy the linked-donor precondition for a separately tracked account-takeover vulnerability (CVE-2026-82675).

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.1, 11.7.x <= 11.7.14, 11.10.x <= 11.10.4 fail to restrict the broadcast scope of group WebSocket events to sessions permitted to read the group which allows an authenticated user, including guests, to obtain the display name, description, member count and member IDs of non-referenceable groups via the received_group event emitted when a group is created, updated, deleted or restored. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00731

Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Andy Moyle Church Admin church-admin allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Church Admin: from n/a through 5.1.11.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in PublishPress PublishPress Revisions revisionary allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects PublishPress Revisions: from n/a through 4.3.3.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Liquid Web / StellarWP The Events Calendar the-events-calendar allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects The Events Calendar: from n/a through 6.18.4.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Awesomemotive Charitable charitable allows Cross Site Request Forgery.This issue affects Charitable: from n/a through 1.8.15.1.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in ThemeGrill Masteriyo - LMS learning-management-system allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Masteriyo - LMS: from n/a through 3.5.1.

Mattermost versions 11.2.x <= 11.2.4 fail to validate that the redirect target on the web app landing page that prompts users to open links in the desktop app stays on the Mattermost origin which allows an unauthenticated attacker to redirect a user to an arbitrary external site via a crafted link. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00893

The Recipe Card Blocks Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.2 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to overwrite the post_content of arbitrary posts on the site, including Administrator-owned published posts, bypassing the edit_others_posts and edit_published_posts capability checks. This vulnerability is only exploitable when the wpzoom_rcb_settings_synchronize_recipe_post setting is enabled, and requires the target post to contain at least one Recipe Card block whose twin can be matched to the attacker's draft recipe post.

The PDF Poster – Let visitors read PDF’s without leaving the page plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.5 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to retrieve the titles and identifiers of other users' private, draft, pending, and scheduled pdfposter posts, and retrieve the title of any arbitrary post by ID across the entire site.

The Recipe Card Blocks Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.1. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to overwrite the stored post_content of any post or page on the site, including published posts and private drafts authored by administrators or other users.

The PayPlus Payment Gateway plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 8.3.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to generate PayPlus payment page links for arbitrary WooCommerce orders belonging to any customer, overwrite those orders' payment method and PayPlus-related order meta, and trigger PayPlus API calls using the store's credentials — including, when a POS EMV device is configured, initiating a charge request to the store's physical POS terminal. The exploit requires no nonce and no special capability beyond being logged in, as the authorization block is unreachable on the AJAX path due to the inverted isset() predicate.

The Contact Form Email plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.72. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to view and delete all stored contact form submissions, create, rename, delete, and clone forms, alter plugin database tables, and persistently rewrite the reporting options to silently email a CSV of all submissions to an attacker-controlled address on every subsequent request. The nonce intended to authorize state-changing POST requests is minted into the same management page the attacker can already render, so it provides no effective authorization barrier against a Subscriber-level user.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The OpenID Connect (OIDC) logout endpoint continues to honor post-logout redirect rules for disabled clients rather than rejecting the requests. If a disabled client retains permissive redirect configurations, a remote attacker can exploit this issue by supplying an arbitrary redirection target in a logout request, leading to an open redirect that can be used in phishing attacks.

A flaw was found in Hawtio. An authenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request URI to monitored endpoints. The FlightRecordingDownloadFacade servlet filter uses an inefficient regular expression pattern that causes catastrophic backtracking when processing certain long requests. This issue leads to excessive CPU utilization, causing handling threads to hang and degrading service availability.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The Account API endpoint for sharing resources fails to verify whether owner-managed access is enabled and accepts permission scopes not assigned to the resource. An authenticated user can exploit this vulnerability to generate pre-granted permission tickets, causing Keycloak to bypass policy evaluation and issue access tokens with unauthorized scopes.
Greenbone gvmd before 26.43.0 does not restrict certificate creation. Even the Observer role, documented to be read-only, can execute create_tls_certificate.

In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, /api/index.php/eventattendees discloses attendee and project data regardless of the caller's permissions. Only 22.0.0 and later (where api_eventattendees.class.php exists) are affected. A remote authenticated user can obtain column values one character at a time.
IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to conduct a server-side request forgery due to a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.
IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.13 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to delete API keys belonging to other users due to improper authorization checks.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.0, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold a role with either the list_indexer_cluster capability or the edit_indexer_cluster capability could download the cluster manager configuration bundle through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API and access configuration and app files that the cluster manager stages for indexer distribution.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API does not require the list_indexer_cluster or edit_indexer_cluster capability before it sends the configuration bundle.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
For more information see Cluster endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/leverage-rest-apis/rest-api-reference/10.6/cluster-endpoints/cluster-endpoint-descriptions) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could view credentials configured for email notifications in a saved search shared with that user.
The vulnerability is possible when email notifications use authentication credentials because the Saved Searches Representational State Transfer (REST) API returns those credentials in clear text.
For more information see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/leverage-rest-apis/rest-api-reference/10.6/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions), Manage knowledge object permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.6/get-started-with-knowledge-objects/manage-knowledge-object-permissions), and Email notification action (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/alert-and-respond/alerting-manual/10.6/configure-alert-actions/email-notification-action) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could turn on the AI chat training-data consent setting through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The missing authorization is possible because the affected configuration endpoint does not enforce authorization checks.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with edit permission on a workbook could configure a service-level agreement at only the workbook phase or task level. Splunk SOAR then flags the task as overdue immediately and does not display the configured deadline in the work queue. The incorrect deadline status could obscure genuine deadline breaches.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR treats an absent phase-level or task-level service-level agreement as immediately due when it compares the configured due times.
For more information see Define tasks using workbooks (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/7.0.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/define-tasks-using-workbooks) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit and run playbooks could view child playbook status and loop-state metadata for playbook runs outside the authorized scope for that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook status API does not bind the requested run to the current execution context before it returns metadata.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view and edit containers could import a container archive that makes artifacts appear to be part of a case or have notes when no corresponding case associations or notes exist. This could cause Representational State Transfer (REST) API clients and filters to use incorrect artifact state.
The vulnerability is possible because container archive import accepts artifact workflow state from the archive instead of deriving that state from associated cases and notes.
For more information see Splunk SOAR REST API reference (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with playbook edit permission could cause later playbook conversions to include spurious branch conditions. This can prevent downstream blocks from running in affected converted playbooks.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook converter retains branch conditions from previous conversions.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with asset edit permission could change the approval requirements and effective automation user for an asset without Splunk SOAR recording field-level audit details for those changes. This could weaken investigation and accountability for changes to security-sensitive asset settings.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not include the asset approval voting fields and effective automation user field in its field-level audit coverage.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit artifacts could cause indicator correlation data to retain stale field associations, which can produce incorrect correlation results and event counts.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not remove stale indicator associations when an artifact changes.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the System Settings view permission but not the Assets view permission could view asset and tenant metadata in the ingestion history view.
The ingestion history view does not restrict summary results to assets and tenants that the user can view.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who holds a role with permission to view system settings but not assets could view asset, app, and container-label metadata in Ingestion filters.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR returns Ingestion filter metadata without applying asset authorization and tenant restrictions.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.5.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings view permission but not the Assets view permission could view asset names, asset identifiers, app names, tenant names, and ingestion schedule settings for polling assets in the ingestion schedule view.
The vulnerability is possible because the ingestion schedule view does not verify the Assets view permission before it returns data derived from assets.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to view and modify containers with an allowed label could add artifacts to containers that the user cannot view or modify.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API artifact-creation workflow does not preserve the authorization boundary for the selected container.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view, edit, and run playbooks and access to at least one container label could retrieve a callback handle from a playbook run outside the container-label scope granted to that account.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify that the requested callback handle belongs to the parent playbook run that launched the child playbook.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Data access automation API (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/python-playbook-api-reference/8.8.0/automation-api/data-access-automation-api) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated Splunk SOAR user with permission to edit and run playbooks could read action status and callback state from a playbook run outside the authorized container-label or tenant scope for that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook API uses mutable runtime context to identify a playbook run instead of preserving the server-provided context.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit and run playbooks could modify a child playbook callback handle associated with another playbook run, which could alter the callback behavior of that run.
The vulnerability exists because the Playbook API does not verify that callback-handle updates belong to the related parent and child playbook runs.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for containers on only a subset of container labels could modify container pins outside the container labels that the role permits.
The vulnerability is possible because the Container Pin Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not enforce the container label authorization boundary when handling requests.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.1/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user holding a role with the edit_token_http capability could create a persistent HTTP Event Collector (HEC) token that cannot be disabled or deleted via the Representational State Transfer (REST) API or Splunk Web. As a result, the token remains active and can continue ingesting events even after administrative attempts to revoke it.
The vulnerability is possible because HTTP Event Collector token creation accepts names that later management operations cannot process.
For more information see authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.5-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf) and Set up and use HTTP Event Collector in Splunk Web (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/get-data-in/get-started-with-getting-data-in/10.6/get-data-with-http-event-collector/set-up-and-use-http-event-collector-in-splunk-web) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could read private index configuration values for other users through the deployment server Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The deployment server REST API does not limit a supplied repository location to configured deployment repositories before it reads indexes.conf stanzas.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, and 10.2.9, a low-privileged user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could access file path and metadata listings from search head knowledge bundles via the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This unauthorized access could expose sensitive metadata, including Splunk platform usernames, private knowledge-object configuration file names, installed application directories, and the file path names of security-sensitive configuration and key files.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API actions that list bundle contents and denied files use a capability available to the "user" role instead of requiring distributed-search administration capabilities.
For more information see Knowledge bundle replication overview (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/distributed-search/10.6/knowledge-bundle-replication/knowledge-bundle-replication-overview) in the Splunk documentation. For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.17, a user that holds a role with the edit_own_objects capability but does not hold the edit_view_html capability could create or modify a private Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) view through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API applies the edit_own_objects capability when it creates or modifies private HTML-based views instead of requiring the edit_view_html capability.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 improper authorization allowed read-only users to change issue fields via agile boards

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient authorization checks in the quiz random question filter web service, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify random question settings in quizzes they do not have permission to manage. This flaw allows unauthorized users to alter assessment configurations across courses they do not oversee.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz overrides web service allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to modify user and group overrides for quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to improperly alter exam access, deadlines, or testing conditions across unauthorized courses.

A flaw was found in Moodle's single view grade report web service. A missing authorization check allows authenticated students to view the names of all grade items in a course, including those configured to be hidden. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when viewing and restoring wiki page versions, an authenticated user can access content from courses they are not permitted to view. This issue allows an attacker to inspect restricted course material and copy it into their own wiki pages, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. An improper authorization check when displaying individual glossary entries allows an authenticated user to view approved glossary items from courses they do not have permission to access. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure of restricted educational materials.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient permission checks and input validation in the quiz question bank callback, an authenticated user can access and view questions from question banks they do not have permission to access. Furthermore, this issue allows users to trigger arbitrary class instantiation (creating unintended application objects), potentially leading to further unauthorized actions.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient validation when saving activity settings, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify activities in courses they are not authorized to access. This flaw allows unauthorized changes to course materials, compromising the integrity of course content.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing capability check in the grade items web service, an authenticated user with a student role can view the names of all grade items in a course, including those intended to be hidden. This flaw leads to unauthorized information disclosure of hidden course assessment details.

A flaw was found in Moodle. The grade feedback web service does not properly verify group and course enrolment permissions. An authenticated user with non-editing teacher privileges can exploit this vulnerability to access grade feedback and user profile details across groups or courses they are not authorized to view, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4 missing authorization allowed users to remove all build configuration assignments from an agent
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 missing authorization in statistics chart export allowed viewing data of project
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4 an SSRF via connection tests was possible for users without project edit permissions
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 missing authorization allowed reading Qodana reports of other projects

djangocms-moderation provides an approval workflow mechanism for organizations that require content approval before publication. Prior to 2.4.0, CollectionCommentAdmin and RequestCommentAdmin in the Django admin use changelist_view and changeform_view to scope comment access through caller-controlled object identifiers and model-level view_collectioncomment or view_requestcomment permissions without invoking ModerationRequest.user_can_view_comments() or an equivalent collection participant check. An authenticated staff user with either view permission can enumerate collection or moderation-request identifiers and read full comment messages for workflows they do not participate in. The exposure affects confidentiality of internal editorial discussions; comment creation, modification, and deletion remain protected, and integrity and availability are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.0.

django-filer is a file and image management application for Django. Prior to 3.5.0, the delete_files_or_folders action in filer/admin/folderadmin.py checks global Django model-level deletion permission but omits check_folder_edit_permissions and check_files_edit_permissions when FILER_ENABLE_PERMISSIONS is enabled. An authenticated staff user who has a global delete_file, delete_folder, or delete_image permission but is limited to read-only access by FolderPermission can therefore delete files, folders, and descendants from the restricted folder. Deployments using the default disabled per-folder permission system are not affected, and the issue does not create a read-confidentiality impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.5.0.

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the Access Control Policy's download_file_attachment check across several post- and file-serving code paths (bulk post retrieval, channel bookmarks, and persistent notification delivery), which allows an authenticated channel member denied a specific file's download to obtain that file's metadata and a rendered preview thumbnail via those endpoints and events.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00785

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to enforce the configured GitLab group/namespace restriction on the permalink code-preview feature and the {{get_projects}} MCP tool, which allows an authenticated user with a connected GitLab account to retrieve repository file content or project metadata from projects outside the restricted group via a crafted GitLab permalink or MCP tool call. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00750

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to enforce playbook membership management permissions when creating a new playbook which allows a low-privileged user to grant the playbook_admin role to an arbitrary user via a crafted playbook creation request. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00749

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the MFA requirement on the update and delete user endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has not configured MFA to modify or delete their own account via the API despite system-wide MFA enforcement being enabled. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00744

Mattermost versions 11.8.x <= 11.8.5, 11.7.x <= 11.7.10, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fails to validate the type of card property fields which allows a board
Editor to make a board or card permanently unopenable for all users via a crafted PATCH
request storing a non-string property name or value.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00743

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the channel Access Control Policy's file download permission check when serving file metadata and thumbnails through the drafts, scheduled posts, and post edit history endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has lost eligibility under the policy to view metadata and thumbnails of file attachments via those endpoints, even though direct file access is correctly denied. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00740
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 improper authorization allowed viewing build process details via agent stacktraces
Tanium addressed an improper input validation vulnerability in Discover.
Tanium addressed a server-side request forgery vulnerability.

The Nexter Blocks – Gutenberg Blocks, Page Builder & AI Website Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.10 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to create, modify, and delete entries in the site-wide global button-preset store, and inject arbitrary CSS rules into the generated plus-button-presets stylesheet served to all site visitors.

A flaw was found in lldpd. The service fails to verify that Link Layer Discovery Protocol - Media Endpoint Discovery (LLDP-MED) location records received from network neighbors match their declared lengths. An adjacent attacker on the local network can exploit this flaw by sending crafted packets, causing client applications using the liblldpctl library to read past buffer boundaries when parsing location data. This issue can lead to an information disclosure of adjacent process memory.

The Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to incorrect authorization in all versions up to, and including, 6.7.0. This is due to the 'ACF_Ajax_Query::get_args' method returning the user-supplied ''query' array directly without any key whitelisting or validation. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary query parameters to bypass field-configured role restrictions and exfiltrate sensitive user data including administrator email addresses, login names, and private user metadata via blind oracle techniques.

The BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data due to a misconfigured capability check on the 'update_item_permissions_check' function in all versions up to, and including, 14.4.0. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to enable and disable plugin components.

In OpenStack keystonemiddleware before 13.0.3, by supplying a malicious regular expression when creating an application credential (aka AppCred) access_rules entry, an authenticated user may consume resources in the consuming process making a service unresponsive.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to authenticated users, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to disclose the name and content of non-public templates stored on the site.
Race condition in the WebExtensions component in Firefox for Android. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161.
Side-channel in the Networking: HTTP component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161.
Tanium addressed a server-side request forgery vulnerability in Partner Integration

Missing authorization in Kibana Cases alert attachments can allow an authenticated user with permission to add case comments or attachments to modify case-link metadata in documents they are not authorized to access. An attacker can add false case links and prevent legitimate case linkage by exhausting the alert's case-link limit. Writes are limited to the kibana.alert.case_ids field in indices that Kibana's internal account can read and update and whose mappings accept that field. One of the two authorization defects was fixed earlier in 8.19.22, 9.4.8 and 9.5.5; the fixed versions listed in this advisory address both defects.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability in the UI module. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality.

FOE_read and FOE_write store the filename length as uint8_t, truncating it modulo 256. When (mbxheader.length - ESC_FOEHSIZE) is a multiple of 256, the length becomes 0. Additionally, a request whose mailbox length equals ESC_FOEHSIZE exactly also produces a length of 0 without any truncation. In both cases FOE_fopen calls strncmp with a length of 0, which always returns equal, so the first registered file whose password is 0 is opened regardless of the filename the master sent.

Certain EZVIZ devices are affected by a replay attack vulnerability (CWE-294). An attacker may intercept communication traffic and replay specific control commands, causing the device to execute unauthorized operations.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17 on Ubuntu and AlmaLinux, an unauthenticated user who obtains a valid Splunk Web session cookie before the affected user logs out could continue using the cookie after logout to access data and perform actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the logout flow does not invalidate the associated session token on affected deployments.
The attacker must obtain the valid session cookie before the affected user logs out of Splunk Web. The issue was reproduced in Splunk Enterprise installations on Ubuntu and AlmaLinux.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user could create and deliver an Entity Analysis dashboard link to a Splunk Enterprise Security user. If the Splunk Enterprise Security user opens the link, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the Splunk Enterprise Security user. The commands could expose or modify some data available to the Splunk Enterprise Security user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Entity Analysis dashboard inserts entity values from a link that an unauthenticated user creates into SPL searches without safely escaping the values.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Entity analysis dashboard (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/exposure-analytics-and-ueba/entity-analysis-dashboard) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_investigation_read capability could overwrite Mission Control preference records for other users and remove saved filters and analyst queue settings from those records.
The vulnerability is possible because the Mission Control user preferences Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not bind an update to the preference record that passes the authorization check.
The attack requires the user to obtain a preference record identifier that the product does not normally expose to that user. The user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Overview of Mission Control in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/mission-control/overview-of-mission-control-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.
In JetBrains Junie GitHub Action before 1.10.0 untrusted fork code could be processed in privileged workflow runs

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 prints SURREAL_PASS and SURREAL_TOKEN environment variable values in clear text in the --help and -h output of CLI commands such as surreal start, sql, import, export, and mcp, because the arguments do not set clap's hide_env_values. Anyone who later sees that terminal output, for example in shell logs, CI logs, or screen shares, can obtain root database credentials.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, the User extension’s onRequestResetPassword() handler in src/Http/Controllers/Login.php calls resetPassword() and mailSendResetPasswordRequest() only when an account matches. The resulting database write and reset-email send take longer than the nonexistent-account path despite the endpoint returning the same response, allowing timing measurements against a production deployment using a synchronous queue and real SMTP transport to disclose valid staff or customer email addresses. The advisory’s local log-mailer test showed no measurable timing difference, so the signal depends on mail configuration and is useful for follow-on phishing or credential stuffing rather than direct account access. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.
In JetBrains Kotlinx.serialization before 1.12.0 a DoS attack was possible via recursive JSON decoding

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains a Stack-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to a Denial of service.

@fastify/swagger-ui is the plugin that serves Swagger UI documentation for Fastify applications. In versions 2.1.0 through 6.1.4, the authentication hooks that applications register to protect the documentation are applied to every route the plugin adds except the bundled static asset instance. When the option that serves bundled UI files from a local directory is enabled, that instance exposes every file in the directory without credentials, so a specification file an operator meant to keep behind the documentation login becomes reachable by an unauthenticated client who knows or guesses its name. Access is read-only and limited to files in that directory. The issue is fixed in @fastify/swagger-ui 6.1.5, which applies the same authentication hooks to the static asset route, and users should upgrade to 6.1.5 or later.

A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or deliberately slow responses. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. Consequently, an attacker can exhaust host memory, drive CPU usage to capacity, or cause certificate requests to hang indefinitely.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When configured with a database that uses case-insensitive collation, Keycloak resolves realm URLs regardless of letter casing. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior by sending requests with alternate letter casing to bypass upstream reverse proxy access controls that rely on case-sensitive path matching. This issue can expose restricted authentication endpoints intended only for internal access, though Keycloak's internal authentication mechanisms remain intact.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data that populates the Endpoint Changes report. Another user who holds the "pci_analyst" role could later click a corresponding table row. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who clicked the row. The commands could access or modify data available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Endpoint Changes report does not treat dynamic report values as literal search values when it builds table-row drilldown searches.
For more information see Reports (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/user-manual/8.7/using-the-splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/reports) and Configure users and roles (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-the-app/configure-users-and-roles) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in network traffic data. Another user who holds the "pci_user" role could later click the corresponding row in the Traffic Detail panel of the Network Traffic Activity report. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who clicked the row. The commands could access data and perform actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Network Traffic Activity report does not treat network traffic values as literal search values when it builds the Traffic Detail drilldown search.
For more information see Network Traffic Activity (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/network-traffic-activity) and Configure users and roles (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-the-app/configure-users-and-roles) in the Splunk documentation.

The glob functions in the GNU C Library versions 2.44 and earlier may free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to the names it matched.  The names already rewritten are freed, but their pointers stay in the result vector, and the error path frees them again with globfree.

The allocation must fail after at least one name has been rewritten, so the issue can only be reached when the process is already close to its memory limit, for example under an address space limit (RLIMIT_AS) or on a 32-bit system.  The attacker needs control to make the result large enough to make the program or service run out of memory, either by controlling the glob pattern and having knowledge of the filesystem layout or through other means.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

Incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4 could have caused a target's device to reveal its IP information to an attacker if an attacker sent media from an attacker-controlled URL when a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message was rendered and displayed in a message thread. This issue may have been abused in conjunction with specific spam messages.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user could cause Splunk SOAR to store excessive data in the Ingestion Status history through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. When another user with permission to view system settings retrieves the Ingestion Status history, Splunk SOAR could use additional resources and return a larger response, which could degrade the availability of administrative monitoring.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not limit the amount of request data that it records for failed container creation before it stores the data in the Ingestion Status history.
For more information see REST Containers (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/6.4.0/container-endpoints/rest-containers), REST Roles and Permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/6.4.0/role-management-endpoints/rest-roles-and-permissions), and View ingested container statistics using Ingestion Status (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.1/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-system-health-and-performance/view-ingested-container-statistics-using-ingestion-status) in the Splunk documentation.
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 project members could detach inline comment threads of other users on articles

The Strava datasource plugin's resource handler POST /strava-api forwards a client-supplied endpoint string, and its query parameters, to the Strava API (https://www.strava.com/api/v3/<endpoint>) without validation.

When the datasource is not in OAuth pass-through mode, the request is made with the access token stored on the datasource, not the caller's identity. Grafana authorises plugin resource calls only on the datasources:query permission, which Viewers have by default. Any such caller could therefore request any Strava API path the connected account's OAuth grant allows, for example athlete/clubs or routes/{id}, and read the response.

The plugin's frontend (stravaApi.ts) only needs a fixed set of paths: athlete, athlete/activities, activities/{id}, activities/{id}/streams and segments/{id}.

Requests to Strava are GET only, so the issue is read-only.

Affected: plugin versions 1.2.0 through 1.7.2. The fix restricts endpoint to those five patterns and is pending release. The check runs before the access token is resolved, so a rejected request never causes a token refresh or any call to Strava. Paths with .. segments are rejected as well.

PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V1.1 uses a non-cryptographic function to generate security-sensitive appointment and invoice identifiers. The identifiers are generated within a restricted numeric range and are subsequently used in record lookup operations. This implementation exposes the application to identifier prediction or guessing attacks under conditions where the identifiers are relied upon as a security boundary.

Adobe Experience Manager is affected by an Incorrect Authorization vulnerability that could result in a Security feature bypass. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass security measures and gain unauthorized limited write access. Exploit depends on conditions beyond the attacker's control. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must visit a maliciously crafted URL or interact with a compromised web page. Scope is changed.

A flaw was found in the Ansible language server shipped with the vscode-ansible extension. The regular expression used to extract documentation fragments from Ansible module files is susceptible to quadratic-time scanning. A module file containing a crafted documentation string causes the language server to consume excessive CPU while indexing it, freezing the language service in the developer's editor. An attacker who can get a developer to open or index a workspace containing an attacker-supplied collection can cause a denial of service of the editor language features. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.

A flaw was found in ansible-builder. The regular expression used to strip comments from a collection's requirements.txt during introspection is susceptible to super-quadratic backtracking. A requirements file containing a line with a long run of internal whitespace and no comment character causes the comment-stripping routine to consume CPU time proportional to the square of the line length. An attacker who can get a victim to build an execution environment that includes an attacker-supplied collection can cause the ansible-builder build or introspect process to hang, resulting in a denial of service. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.

The Canva Desktop App before 1.128.0 stores encrypted application state on disk. The encryption key is hardcoded as a plaintext string in the main.js file and is identical across all Canva installations on Windows and macOS.

ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c dropped the caller's reference on an IPv4 packet whenever net_arp_prepare() returned NET_ARP_PKT_REPLACED. That return value is also used when ARP could not queue the packet because every ARP cache entry is already pending. In that case ARP holds no reference of its own, so the original packet was freed before the replacing ARP request was transmitted.

If transmitting the ARP request then failed (a driver send error or an ethernet_fill_header() failure), the error path called net_pkt_ref() on the freed packet. net_if_tx() then called net_pkt_unref() on it again. If the freed net_pkt slab slot was reallocated in between, the stray unref releases a reference owned by an unrelated packet, which is freed while still in use.

An attacker on the local link can drive the ARP cache into the all-pending state. CONFIG_NET_ARP_TABLE_SIZE defaults to 2, so it is enough to elicit replies to a few spoofed, non-responding on-subnet addresses. Reaching the memory corruption also needs a transmit failure the attacker does not directly control and a narrow slab-reuse race. The practical impact is corruption or a crash of the network stack (denial of service).

The OpenThread PSA crypto platform backend in modules/openthread/platform/crypto_psa.c only supported PSA key references. otPlatCryptoAesSetKey() copied aKey->mKeyRef into the AES context unconditionally. On an OpenThread Radio Co-Processor (RCP) build, CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA does not select CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_PLATFORM_KEY_REF, so OpenThread passes the MAC key as literal bytes and mKeyRef is uninitialized. psa_cipher_encrypt() in otPlatCryptoAesEncrypt() then fails without writing its output, and the error is only caught by an OpenThread assertion that is compiled to a no-op when CONFIG_ASSERT is disabled.

When the RCP handles transmit security in software, AES-CCM* is never keyed. That is the case with Thread 1.2 or later, where CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_MAC_SOFTWARE_TX_SECURITY_ENABLE defaults to y, on a radio driver without IEEE802154_HW_TX_SEC. Every MAC key-id-mode-1 frame goes out with its payload XORed against a single 16-byte pad of stale stack data, reused for every block, and with an unkeyed MIC. CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA is enabled by default since v4.4.0.

A passive attacker within 802.15.4 radio range can recover the pad from predictable plaintext (for example 6LoWPAN headers) and read the payload of the frames the device transmits. The practical impact is limited. The configuration is not the default (the default Thread version is 1.1), and the same defect makes peers reject every secured data frame, so an affected device cannot exchange data on the network. Received traffic and key distribution are not affected. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, the RCP halts on the first secured transmission instead.

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.13 fail to verify that the requesting user has read permission for a post's channel which allows an authenticated user to read attachment-bearing posts from private channels and direct messages they cannot otherwise access via a crafted {{post_id}} in a POST request to {{/plugins/com.mattermost.mscalendar/action/respond}}. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00708

The SDO Information Get Object Description and Get Entry Description responses copy the object or entry name into the mailbox data area and then write a null terminator byte. The copy loops ran up to the last available byte in the buffer, leaving no room for the terminator. When an object or entry name exactly fills the available space the terminator is written one byte past the end of the mailbox data buffer.

The YMC Filter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 3.14.1 via the 'post_status' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to extract retrieve rendered grid HTML containing titles, excerpts, author names, dates, categories, tags, and thumbnails of private, draft, pending, and future posts they do not have permission to view. Exposure only occurs when an administrator has configured at least one non-publish status in the filter grid's Appearance → Post Status setting, as attacker-supplied statuses are intersected with this administrator-defined allowlist before being passed to WP_Query.

Improper Content Security Policy (CSP) nonce implementation in HCL BigFix MCM allows a remote attacker to reduce the effectiveness of the Content Security Policy protection mechanism via an orphaned nonce value in the style-src directive of the CSP header without a corresponding nonce attribute on any <style> or <script> element.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, the POST /api/auth/login local-login validation path in api/strategies/localStrategy.js logs req.body, including the submitted plaintext password, during a Zod validation failure. The standard browser form validation makes this path less likely through the normal interface, but a direct invalid login request can reach it, and the logging formatter does not redact the password stored in metadata. A principal with access to application stdout, error logs, or journal output can recover the submitted credential. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.0.0 until 4.5.0, getoption_int in libatalk/util/netatalk_conf.c accepts an out-of-range server quantum value from afp.conf without applying the documented fallback to the default. An administrator can unintentionally configure a very large allocation whose failure causes AFP_PANIC at startup or a very small command buffer that disrupts DSI framing, leaving afpd unavailable until the configuration is corrected and the daemon is restarted. The option is read locally at startup and cannot be changed through the AFP protocol. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.0.0 until 4.5.0, afp_catsearch in etc/afpd/catsearch.c computes the spec2 pointer for FPCatSearch and FPCatSearchExt from the unvalidated 16-bit spec_len request field without checking it against the remaining input length. An authenticated AFP client can cause the CatSearch handler to read stale bytes beyond the supplied request data. The bytes are used only as internal comparison criteria and are not returned to the client, and testing under standard server quantum settings did not demonstrate a crash or information disclosure. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who holds a role that can edit and run playbooks in Splunk SOAR could cause Splunk SOAR to run non-read-only actions from a Safe Mode playbook, resulting in unauthorized state changes.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify that the playbook run context in an action request matches the context that the server provided.

The ProfilePress  WordPress plugin before 4.18.1 does not atomically consume the source subscription when processing a membership plan change, allowing a customer to submit concurrent plan-change checkouts against a single paid subscription and obtain several active memberships for the price of one.

The issue occurs because Splunk SOAR does not audit custom field definition changes.

The Envira Gallery  WordPress plugin before 1.16.4 does not apply its own gallery-permission policy until an administrator first opens its permissions screen, instead copying gallery-management capabilities onto each role from that role's core post capabilities after activation, which lets Contributor accounts create, edit and delete galleries that the policy is meant to restrict to higher roles.
