The vendored zcbor decoder's zcbor_any_skip() in boot/zcbor/src/zcbor_decode.c descends one C-stack frame per level of CBOR nesting. On a list or map it copies the decoder state (memcpy(&state_copy, state, sizeof(zcbor_state_t))) and recurses once per member, with no depth cap: the skip path does not use zcbor's backup stack, and ZCBOR_MAX_ELEM_COUNT is SIZE_MAX, so nothing bounds how deep the recursion goes.

That function is reached on attacker-controlled bytes before any authentication. MCUboot's serial-recovery command parser decodes SMP/CBOR requests with zcbor_map_decode_bulk() (boot/boot_serial/src/zcbor_bulk.c), which skips any map key it does not recognise by calling zcbor_any_skip() on the encoded value; the echo handler in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c calls it directly on the same footing. Both run during image upload, long before the uploaded image's signature is checked. The default receive buffer is MCUBOOT_SERIAL_MAX_RECEIVE_SIZE = 512 bytes and each nesting level costs a single byte to encode (0x81), so roughly 500 levels of nesting fit in one request — comfortably more than a bootloader's stack can absorb, since every frame carries a full zcbor_state_t copy plus locals.

The impact is availability only: the bootloader's stack overflows and the device faults or hangs during recovery. There is no controlled out-of-bounds write that escapes the DFU buffer, no disclosure, and no authentication bypass — the recursion grows the stack with the decoder's own internal state. Whether a given board actually exhausts its stack depends on that board's bootloader stack size, which we did not measure; the fix is nevertheless unconditional, because an unauthenticated pre-authentication code path must not have its safety depend on a per-board stack margin.

Exposure requires MCUBOOT_SERIAL (serial/SMP recovery), which is not enabled by default, and recovery entry is normally gated on a physical pin (CONFIG_BOOT_SERIAL_ENTRANCE_GPIO / PIN_RESET), with a no-valid-image fallback path. Products that expose serial recovery over an externally reachable transport, or that fall into recovery when no valid image is present, are the ones at risk.

The fix is to bound the skip: thread a recursion-depth counter through zcbor_any_skip() (or have zcbor_map_decode_bulk() reject values nested beyond a small constant) and fail once the limit is exceeded — equivalently, take the bounded-skip implementation from upstream zcbor.
Tanium addressed a denial of service vulnerability in Tanium Zone Server.

A vulnerability has been found in continuedev continue up to 2.1.0. In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2, 2026.1.6 hTML injection in pipeline notification emails was possible via commit messages

Rclone 1.49.0 before 1.76.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in Proxy.Call that lets revoked users keep access because cached auth-proxy answers are never revalidated. Revoked users of serve sftp, ftp, http, or webdav can reconnect within five minutes using their original credentials to retain access indefinitely.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki - CentralNotice Extension. This issue affects MediaWiki - CentralNotice Extension: 1.43, 1.45, 1.46.

Copeland XWEB Pro allows a remote, authenticated attacker to inject additional arguments into the wireless interface configuration command. Impact is limited to modification of the wireless interface state. Fixed in 1.16.1.

The html_to_markdown filter of twig/markdown-extra keeps an HtmlConverter for each distinct mapping of options it receives. They're kept in a static array, with no size limit and no eviction. The options are an argument of the filter. A template that passes options taken from the input, or a sandboxed template, can therefore make this cache grow without limit. The cache outlives the environment, so it fills the memory of long-running workers.

The cache now keeps at most 100 converters, like the formatter caches of IntlExtension.

The guard tag compiles only one of its branches, depending on whether a callable exists. The other branch was still parsed, though. The extends, use, macro and block tags in it registered their effects on the template. The sandbox doesn't see these tags, since that branch isn't compiled. A sandboxed template allowed to use guard could therefore extend a template, import blocks and define macros, while the policy doesn't allow these tags:

{% guard filter upper %}{% else %}{% extends "parent.html" %}{% endguard %}

The templates reached this way come from the loader of the sandbox, and they are sandboxed too.

What the branch that isn't selected registers on the parser is now discarded.

Cva::apply() converted the values of variants, default variants and compound variants with (array). These values come from the arguments of html_cva(). A sandboxed template could therefore pass any object of its context, and print the private and protected properties of that object:

{{ html_cva('base', {c: {p: user}}).apply({c: 'p'}) }}

Variant maps that are ArrayAccess objects were also read with a key that the template chooses, without the property check of the sandbox. The template then printed the offsets that the object returned.

Applications are affected when the sandbox allows the html_cva function and the apply method of Twig\Extra\Html\Cva.

A value that isn't an array is now treated as a single item, so objects are dropped and never match a variant. Variant maps are also only used when they're arrays.

Since Twig 3.28.0, the sandbox skips the toString() check of an argument whose PHP parameter can't hold a string, like an int. A spread argument was mapped to a single parameter, although it fills every parameter from its position on. A sandboxed template could therefore call a denied toString() method:

{{ tag(...[1, obj]) }}

Here, the first parameter of tag() is an int, and a later one accepts strings. Applications are affected when they allow such a function, filter or test in the sandbox. No built-in callable is affected.

A spread argument is now checked unless every parameter that it can fill has a safe type.

The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. It didn't check the input of tests. The PHP callable of a test may convert this input to a string, for example when its parameter is typed as string. PHP then calls toString() on an object without the sandbox checking it first:

{{ obj is upperish }}

Applications are affected when they register such a test and allow it in the sandbox. No built-in test is affected.

The sandbox now checks the input of tests like the input of filters. The built-in tests that never convert their input to a string still skip the check.

A stack-based buffer overflow in the DHCP Server helper of ASUSTOR ADM allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to trigger stack memory corruption by sending a crafted DHCP hostname to a device with DHCP Server enabled. This may disrupt DHCP service.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Arcane before 3.0.0 fails to enforce the requiresPasswordChange account flag on the server, allowing attackers with initial or temporary credentials to obtain fully privileged access tokens. Attackers can log in via /api/auth/login and call privileged endpoints such as POST /api/users to create users without completing the mandated password change.

SparkyFitness before 1.12.0 contains a weak password change vulnerability that allows attackers with a victim's session to change the account password without supplying the current password. Attackers can send a POST request with only newPassword to /api/identity/update-password to lock out the legitimate owner and retain persistent access.

SparkyFitness before 1.12.0 contains a missing ownership check in getNutritionixHeaders that allows authenticated users to use another user's Nutritionix API credentials via the providerId parameter. Attackers who know a victim's provider UUID can call the Nutritionix search, nutrients, item, or exercise endpoints to consume the victim's paid API quota.

In mcp-server-fetch from 2026.10.10 and before 2026.11.11, the check that blocks requests to non-public addresses treats IPv6 site-local addresses (fec0::/10) as public. A fetch to such an address passes the server-side request forgery guard. Practical impact is limited because many hosts have no route to this range.

Windmill 1.607.0 before 1.819.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows workspace members to resume or cancel suspended flows in other workspaces by abusing the jobs_u/resume and jobs_u/cancel endpoints. Attackers can mint a resume signature for an arbitrary job id via their own workspace's job_signature endpoint to approve or cancel another workspace's suspended flow steps.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an improper verification vulnerability that allows authenticated users to retain the emailVerified flag by changing their email address while EMAIL_VERIFICATION is disabled. Attackers with a previously verified account can set another person's address via the PATCH /email handler, receiving OIDC email_verified=true claims to impersonate that owner in relying applications.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because the POST /reset_password/passkey/end handler never calls endUserSessions(). Attackers holding a stolen session cookie keep authenticated access to the victim's account even after the victim recovers it by registering a new passkey.

ByteStash 1.5.0 before 1.6.1 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the /api/auth/oidc/callback handler because OIDC state is not bound to the initiating browser. Attackers can start an OIDC login with their own account and lure victims into opening the withheld callback URL, logging them into the attacker's account to read saved snippets.

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to delete other users' files by storing a crafted image value via PUT /api/v1/users. Attackers can set their image to a traversal key and upload a new profile photo, causing storage.Delete to remove other users' attachments or photos under the storage root.

Wfuzz through 3.1.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious target servers to inject script by returning crafted links written unescaped into HTML reports. When the links script and html printer are used, attacker-supplied href values close the unquoted anchor tag and execute JavaScript when the operator opens the report.

OpenAirInterface CN5G AMF before 2.2.2 contains a missing resource release vulnerability in amf_sbi::handle_itti_message() that leaves stale PDU session contexts when NRF lookup or SMF selection fails. Authenticated UEs can request PDU sessions while no SMF is selectable, causing deregistration to wait on SMF release timeouts and stall shared NAS processing for other UEs.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a missing resource release vulnerability in HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate that leaves CHF charging sessions open when PCF session rule application fails. Attackers can repeatedly trigger failed PDU session establishments to accumulate orphaned charging sessions on the CHF and degrade its availability.

Open5GS AMF through 2.8.0 contains a missing resource release vulnerability that allows authenticated UEs to orphan SMF sessions by triggering Create SM Context response processing failures. Attackers can repeatedly release the RAN UE context while responses are pending, causing AMF_SESS_CLEAR() without Release SM Context requests and degrading SMF availability.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a clickjacking vulnerability because src/hooks.server.ts never sets X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors headers on responses. Attackers on a same-site origin can embed the UI in an invisible iframe to trick authenticated users into stopping stacks, deleting resources, or changing settings.

Frappe ERPNext 15.94.2 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in a supplier portal endpoint whose party identity check ignores party type, failing to distinguish a Customer and a Supplier that share a name. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read buying-portal records.

Coder 2.32.0 before 2.34.17, 2.35.0 before 2.36.12, 2.37.0 before 2.37.9, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.5 contain a symlink-following flaw in the Coder Agents read_skill_file tool, which validates skill file paths lexically but follows symlinks outside the skill directory. Attackers who place a malicious skill containing a symlinked supporting file in a victim's workspace can leak other workspace files into the model context and chat history when the victim runs a chat using that skill.

Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.26, 2.30.0 before 2.34.18, 2.35.0 before 2.37.10, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability because CSRF exemption patterns in coderd/httpmw/csrf.go are matched as unanchored regular expressions, letting affected API routes skip CSRF token and same-origin checks. Attackers controlling a page same-site with the deployment can make signed-in users' browsers send forged POST requests that recreate dev containers or add users whose names contain derp to organizations.

better-auth from 0.8.1-beta.5 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and @better-auth/passkey from 1.6.25 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, let revoked sessions stay valid because secondary storage session lists are updated non-atomically and some routes trust cookie-cached sessions. An attacker holding a valid session can evade bulk revocation or bans, or use a revoked cached session to register a passkey or create a lasting session.

@better-auth/passkey 1.4.0-beta.16 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and the passkey plugin in better-auth 1.2.0-beta.18 before 1.4.0, do not confirm WebAuthn user verification when userVerification is "required" and take the expected origin from the request instead of configuration. Users can register or use passkeys without the required PIN or biometric check, and passkey responses created on another origin under the same relying party ID may be accepted.

Vikunja from 0.20.5 before 2.8.0 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the OpenID Connect callback in OpenIdAuth.vue that accepts a valueless state parameter. Attackers can send a crafted callback link with an empty state and their own authorization code to silently log victims into the attacker's account and view the victims' entered data.

Parse Server before 8.6.122 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.2 does not prevent dot notation keys from changing a field that a beforeSave trigger keeps constant or reverts, affecting Object, Array, GeoPoint, Polygon, Bytes (on MongoDB), and ACL fields on create and update. A client allowed to write the object can modify such a field, such as a constant role list, to bypass Cloud Code authorization checks.

A vulnerability was detected in continuedev continue 2.0.0/2.1.0. Affected by this issue is the function DocsCrawler of the file core/indexing/docs/crawlers/DocsCrawler.ts of the component Docs Crawler. The manipulation of the argument startUrl/useLocalCrawling results in server-side request forgery. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The attack requires a high level of complexity. The exploitation is known to be difficult. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

memtomem-stm is a short-term memory proxy gateway with proactive memory surfacing for AI agents. From 0.1.0 until 0.1.34, untrusted long-term and working-memory fields can introduce Markdown or HTML-compatible structure into the surfaced-memory envelope because those fields are not serialized as inert data. A crafted memory can create misleading structural boundaries or visually conceal surfaced content, affecting how a consuming agent interprets the memory context. Ordinary natural-language persuasion remains a residual model-level risk and is outside the structural serialization flaw. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.34.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), any PEM user can run the pem.send_webhook() function, which runs with elevated privileges and queues a payload for any configured webhook. The PEM agent then delivers it with that webhook's stored headers, OAuth token or client certificate, so a user can send forged notifications to endpoints they could not otherwise authenticate to.
From PEM 10.6.1, no PEM login role can call this function directly. PEM still sends webhook notifications through its own internal paths.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease that orphans SM contexts and UE IP addresses when PFCP session deletion fails. Attackers can send repeated PDU session establishment requests reusing an existing SUPI and PDU Session ID during PFCP deletion failures to exhaust the DNN's UE IP pool.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a resource leak vulnerability in HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate that leaves SM contexts unreleased when UDM access token retrieval fails. Attackers can trigger repeated PDU session establishment attempts while the NRF is unreachable, causing empty 200 responses and persistent SMF memory growth.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability because sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept returns early without calling RemoveSMContextFromAllNF on failures. Authenticated UEs repeatedly establishing PDU sessions during NRF or AMF failures leak SM contexts, UE IP addresses and TEIDs, exhausting the DNN IP pool.

When a ticket holder opens the ticket page of a ticket that is an add-on (possible since 2026.9) the HTML content of the page contains the secret link to the parent product, creating a potential data leak. Under different specific conditions, when a ticket contains user-uploaded files in response to a question, the page can even contain the secret link to the entire order.

StorageGRID (formerly StorageGRID Webscale) versions 12.1.0 and higher are susceptible to an information exposure vulnerability which allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to acquire low-sensitivity credentials via a Man-in-the-middle attack when certain non-default features are enabled.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Stored XSS via SQL field labels in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Labels and values of SQL field options were returned unescaped by the reload task and inserted into the page as HTML, allowing stored XSS if the statement reads user-supplied data.

sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to another host. Attackers controlling the scanned target or abusing an open redirect can make RedirectHandler.http_error_302 forward session cookies or bearer tokens to an attacker-controlled host.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject iframe attributes via the maxheight parameter of the GET /oembed endpoint. Attackers can supply a single quote in maxheight to inject an onload handler into the returned html, executing script in third-party oEmbed consumers that embed it unsanitized.

OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in PublicWebhookUrl::isPublicIp that fails to reject CGNAT, NAT64 and 6to4 address ranges. Authenticated users can configure webhook, form import or PDF image URLs resolving to these ranges to make the server send HTTPS requests to internal hosts.

SABnzbd before 5.2.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Sorter that allows attackers to write files outside the Complete folder via crafted propername, episodename or job name (%dn) values. Attackers can supply a malicious NZB with '...' sequences that collapse to '..' after single-pass replacement, moving downloaded files into arbitrary directories writable by SABnzbd.

Quasar before 2.35.3 contains a DOM clobbering vulnerability that allows attackers to break native wrapper detection by injecting HTML elements named Capacitor, cordova, or StatusBar. Attackers can place markup such as a div with id Capacitor into server-rendered or pre-rendered HTML so app.use(Quasar) throws and the application never mounts, or openURL() and AddressbarColor.set() throw.

Tiptap @tiptap/core 2.0.0-alpha.0 before 3.30.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM attributes via a __proto__ key passed to mergeAttributes(). Attackers can supply untrusted JSON attribute data whose __proto__ replaces the merged object's prototype, causing DOMSerializer.renderSpec to render injected event handlers that execute JavaScript.

In Eclipse Ditto versions 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the resolved policy view (`GET /api/2/policies/{policyId}?policy-view=resolved`) does not restrict merged policy content to what the caller may read in the policy it originates from. Imported and namespace-root entries are returned in full as soon as the caller may read any part of them in the source policy, entries of transitive imports and of the imports of namespace-root policies are only checked against the intermediate policy, and content copied into an entry by `references`, also from another entry of the same policy, is not checked against the referenced entry. An authenticated caller with READ on a policy can therefore read subjects, resources and granted/revoked permissions of policy entries that are hidden from them, including by explicit revokes, when reading the originating policy directly.

In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.8.15 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the policy enforcers do not let a revoke win over a grant in two kinds of permission checks. Checks of several permissions at once compare the highest grant weight with the highest revoke weight across all requested permissions instead of per permission, so the "check permissions" API (`POST /api/2/checkPermissions`, available since 3.7.0) can report a set of permissions as granted although one of them is revoked. Partial permission checks, which authorize retrieving Things and Policies and determine the receivers of events, count a grant on a sub-resource although the same permission is revoked on that sub-resource for another subject of the same authorization context (or, with the memory-optimized policy evaluator, for the same subject). A requester can thereby learn about the existence of Things and Policies and receive metadata without any readable content, and an application relying on the check permissions result may grant access the policy denies. The content of retrieved Things and Policies is still filtered correctly, and modifications are not affected.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in gv_send.php because the action=process step never validates a CSRF token via check_secure_form(). Attackers can host an auto-submitting form that makes a logged-in customer send their gift voucher balance to an attacker-controlled email address for redemption.

When payload encryption is enabled, failure messages and stack traces that temporal-proxy is configured to keep from the upstream Temporal service can reach it in plaintext, where anyone who can read the Workflow's history at the upstream can read them. When the proxy returns a failure to a Worker, it decrypts the failure's encoded attributes and copies the message and stack trace back onto the failure, keeping the attributes. A Worker that sends that failure back through the proxy, as SDKs do when an Activity failure becomes the cause of a Workflow failure, sends the restored text with it, and the proxy forwards the text unchanged because the failure already has encoded attributes. The upstream then stores the text in plaintext beside its encrypted copy. This affects deployments that enable failure encryption in the proxy, and deployments that leave it off while the SDK encodes failure attributes itself. Payloads are not affected. temporal-proxy versions 0.9.0 through 1.2.0 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.

When two templated upstreams in temporal-proxy render the same address, a request routed to one upstream can be sent under the other upstream's credential, namespace translation, and payload encryption keys. temporal-proxy pools connections for templated upstreams by rendered address and TLS server name only, although each upstream's outbound credential, namespace translation, and payload encryption keys, where configured, are attached to its connection. A request routed to one upstream can therefore be sent over the connection the other created, and the upstream Temporal service authorizes it as the other upstream's principal. Configuration validation rejects only identical hostPort values, so templates that differ in text but render the same address are accepted. This mixes the two upstreams' ordinary traffic, and a caller that an external authenticator restricts to one upstream's namespaces can use it to act under the other upstream's credential. Deployments with at most one templated upstream are not affected. temporal-proxy versions 0.1.0 through 1.1.1 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.0, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.

CAST Imaging has an access control flaw in the "/api/jobs/<uuid>/logs/download" endpoint. An authenticated low-privilege user can download log archives for any job whose UUID they know, even if they are not authorized to access it.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute. Network-positioned attackers can observe or induce plain-HTTP requests to https instances to capture the session token and impersonate the victim until expiry.

A Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information (CWE-319) vulnerability exists in the Android application "Imperial Palaces Guide" provided by The Imperial Household Agency. A man-in-the-middle attacker may be able to tamper with data transmitted between the application and the server, resulting in the display of modified content to users.

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11 fail to scope an incoming webhook's direct message target to the webhook's own team, which allows a team administrator to deliver a direct message to a user on a team they have no authority over via a webhook whose posting identity belongs to both teams.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00751

A vulnerability was identified in Backdrop CMS up to 1.35.2. Affected is the function get_argument of the file core/modules/views/plugins/views_plugin_argument_default_php.inc of the component Views Module. Such manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The config-import path enforces no 'use PHP for settings' check while the Views PHP-code argument plugin executes eval() without a permission check, confirming the authorization bypass. The vendor explains: "As per our security advisory policy, no security advisory is required when an exploit requires 'advanced permissions'."

A vulnerability was determined in Zefan-Cai R-KV up to 6715468b9872442be72e5c97322e4d9c9a2abf55. This impacts the function _shard_files of the file FlashInfer/rkv/loader.py of the component FlashInfer weight loader. This manipulation of the argument weight_map causes path traversal. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. Patch name: 0fdff6ed12b58ad4c33aab5a63f66e04555cafb6. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

A security vulnerability has been detected in ModelCloud GPTQModel up to 7.6.0. Affected by this vulnerability is the function gptqmodel.adapter.remote.resolve_path of the file gptqmodel/adapter/remote.py of the component Adapter Resolution Pipeline. Such manipulation of the argument adapter.path leads to improper input validation. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version 7.7.0 addresses this issue. The name of the patch is ed99ac8d59940bf27bb24ce2e80002ae9e44469f. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability was detected in declare-lab tango up to 34ecd38898508017ca937508a047b42817d2b070. Impacted is the function Tango.__init__ of the file tango.py of the component Model Loading. Performing a manipulation of the argument scheduler_name results in improper input validation. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. This product adopts a rolling release strategy to maintain continuous delivery. Therefore, version details for affected or updated releases cannot be specified. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A security vulnerability has been detected in XiangLi1999 Diffusion-LM up to 759889d58ef38e2eed41a8c34db8032e072826f4. This issue affects the function main of the file improved-diffusion/scripts/text_sample.py. Such manipulation of the argument out_dir leads to path traversal. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A weakness has been identified in XiangLi1999 Diffusion-LM up to 759889d58ef38e2eed41a8c34db8032e072826f4. This vulnerability affects the function os.system of the file improved-diffusion/scripts/infill.py. This manipulation of the argument notes causes os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. This product follows a rolling release approach for continuous delivery, so version details for affected or updated releases are not provided. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A flaw has been found in SEO Panel 6.0.0. Affected is an unknown function of the file controllers/siteauditor.ctrl.php of the component Site Auditor. Executing a manipulation of the argument order_col/order_val can lead to sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 7.0.0 is able to address this issue. This patch is called 2a2d4aeb718177327b0cd8ce17e2f40328772127. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability was detected in SEO Panel 6.0.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file controllers/siteauditor.ctrl.php of the component Site Auditor. Performing a manipulation of the argument order_col/order_val results in sql injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 7.0.0 will fix this issue. The patch is named 389783b5d8235f5637f4e4587f524b5fef07864d. The affected component should be upgraded.

A security vulnerability has been detected in SEO Panel 6.0.0. This affects the function mime_content_type of the file controllers/website.ctrl.php of the component Website Import. Such manipulation of the argument website_csv_file leads to unrestricted upload. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. A vulnerability was detected in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The affected element is the function Store/Update of the file modules/User/Http/Controllers/UserController.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The patch is named 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

A weakness has been identified in DWS Antik Browser 1.17.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file src/server/index.ts of the component Local API Server. Executing a manipulation can lead to origin validation error. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability has been found in louislam uptime-kuma up to e7420f8fa546a8baa7ac4bf9d10a32545d4346e0. Affected by this vulnerability is the function disableAPIKey/enableAPIKey of the file server/socket-handlers/api-key-socket-handler.js of the component API Key Management. The manipulation leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection') vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki - Score Extension. This vulnerability is associated with program files includes/Score.php. This issue affects MediaWiki - Score Extension: 1.43, 1.45, 1.46, 1.47.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki - UrlShortener Extension. This vulnerability is associated with program files includes/SpecialUrlShortener.php. This issue affects MediaWiki - UrlShortener Extension: 1.43, 1.45, 1.46, 1.47.

A vulnerability has been found in zhblue hustoj up to 26.08.19. This impacts an unknown function of the file trunk/core/judged/judged.cc of the component Judge Daemon Sandbox. The manipulation leads to execution with unnecessary privileges. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 26.10.31 will fix this issue. The identifier of the patch is 07c73e1434c4c8e49094396c7d93bb09d6f159a4/b5488154c7842fbfa0c38af93a737a85622cdf86. The affected component should be upgraded.

A vulnerability was identified in zhayujie CowAgent up to 2.2.1. This impacts the function _create_task of the file agent/tools/scheduler/scheduler_tool.py of the component Scheduler. Such manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 2.2.2 will fix this issue. The name of the patch is 566c941c1e09d295ea5d96eda4dd315260eab9b7. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

ex_aws_s3 builds x-amz-meta-* request headers by interpolating user-supplied object metadata directly into header names and values without any validation. In ExAws.S3.Utils.build_meta_headers/1 (lib/ex_aws/s3/utils.ex), each :meta entry is turned into a header as {"x-amz-meta-#{k}", v} with no check for carriage return (CR), line feed (LF), or other illegal header bytes.

Object metadata is routinely derived from end-user input (for example an upload service that lets users attach a comment or label to an object). When such input reaches ExAws.S3.put_object/4 or any other operation accepting the :meta option, a value containing CR/LF is carried unchanged into the outbound header list. If the configured HTTP adapter does not neutralize header values before writing them to the socket, the embedded CRLF starts a new header line, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary headers into (or split) the HTTP request the library sends to the S3 endpoint. This is an HTTP header (CRLF) injection leading to HTTP request splitting. The practical impact depends on the HTTP adapter, and no authentication is required beyond the ability to influence object metadata.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows HTTP header injection via an attacker-controlled copy-source key.

ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the x-amz-copy-source request header by interpolating the source bucket and object key directly into "/#{src_bucket}/#{src_object}" with no percent-encoding. The sibling function put_object_copy percent-encodes the bucket and each path segment before assembling the same header, but upload_part_copy skips encoding entirely.

When the source key is derived from untrusted input, reserved characters (spaces, ?, &, =) pass through verbatim and corrupt the copy-source reference, so the copy targets the wrong object or fails. A key containing \r or \n can split or inject additional headers into the outgoing HTTP request, depending on how the configured HTTP backend serializes headers.

Applications that pass a source bucket or object key derived from untrusted input to ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 are affected. Applications that only ever pass trusted, well-formed keys are not affected.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls tag keys or values to inject forged tag entries into S3 object and bucket tagging requests.

ExAws.S3.put_object_tagging/4 and ExAws.S3.put_bucket_tagging/2 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex build the <TagSet> request body by interpolating tag keys and values directly into <Key> and <Value> elements via to_string/1, without applying the module's existing escape_xml_string/1 helper (which delete_multiple_objects already uses for object keys). An application that forwards user-supplied data as a tag key or value lets an attacker close the intended element and inject attacker-chosen <Tag> entries. For example, a tag value of blue</Value></Tag><Tag><Key>owner</Key><Value>admin turns one intended tag into two tags on the wire. Because S3 honors tags in access-control conditions (aws:RequestTag, s3:ExistingObjectTag) and cost-allocation reporting, an injected tag can forge an authorization-relevant tag or corrupt the intended tag set.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.2 before 2.6.0.

Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpc module) allows HTTP Request Splitting.

httpc writes request header names and values to the wire without neutralizing CR, LF or NUL characters. On the default path http_request:mk_key_value_str/2, and with the headers_as_is option httpc_request:http_headers/2, build each header line by plain concatenation of the name, ": ", the value and CRLF. A CR/LF in a name or value ends the header line early. An attacker who controls data that an application puts into a header passed to httpc:request/4,5 can add or override request headers, or append a second request on the same connection.

Applications that pass only constant or validated header names and values are not affected. The request line is not affected, because uri_string rejects URLs that contain raw CR/LF.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

Improper Input Validation vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to bypass the input validation of the field types of a :keyword attribute or argument.

Ash.Type.Keyword.cast_input/2 in lib/ash/type/keyword.ex converts a map input to a keyword list in try_map_to_keyword/2, which casts each declared field with Ash.Type.cast_stored/3. That function is meant for trusted values read back from the data layer, so client input skips the cast_input/2 of each field type. apply_constraints/2 casts the result again with cast_input/2, but most types accept a value of their own type unchanged. An embedded resource field is built without its create action, so its validations and changes do not run and its non-public attributes can be set. A :function field accepts a capture string such as &Mod.fun/1, and a :term field decodes Erlang external term format.

This issue affects ash: from 3.24.0 before 3.38.1.

Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_kms (ExAws.KMS module) causes callers who import external key material to wrap their secret KMS key material with the deprecated PKCS#1 v1.5 padding scheme by default.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/kms.ex and program routine ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3.

ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3 defaults its wrapping_algorithm argument to "RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5". AWS KMS returns this value as the WrappingAlgorithm for the import operation, and it dictates the RSA padding scheme the caller uses to wrap (RSA-encrypt) their secret key material before calling ImportKeyMaterial. AWS KMS also supports the stronger RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1 and RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256 schemes. By defaulting to RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5, the library steers callers who do not explicitly override the argument toward the weakest of the three. PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is susceptible to Bleichenbacher adaptive chosen-ciphertext (padding oracle) attacks, which can recover the wrapped plaintext without the private key given an oracle that reveals whether a decrypted value was validly padded. Because the unwrap happens inside AWS KMS, which does not expose a padding oracle, the practical exploitability is low and this is a defense-in-depth weakness. Callers can avoid the weak default by explicitly passing "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256" (or "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1") as the wrapping algorithm.

This issue affects ex_aws_kms: from 2.1.0 before 2.7.0.

The sandbox allows every method of Twig\Markup objects, including their public constructor. A sandboxed template can therefore call __construct() on any Markup object that it reaches, and replace its content:

{% do banner.__construct('<script>alert(1)</script>', 'UTF-8') %}

A template gains nothing by rewriting its own output. The impact is on the Markup objects that come from the application and are also rendered elsewhere, like a global in a long-running worker. Their new content then ends up in trusted pages that aren't sandboxed.

The sandbox no longer allows calling the constructor of Markup objects.

MCUboot's Espressif port omits zeroization of two sensitive stack buffers in boot/espressif/hal/src/flash_encrypt.c. In check_and_generate_encryption_keys(), the freshly generated XTS-AES flash-encryption key is held in the stack array keys[BLOCKS_NEEDED][32] (flash_encrypt.c:216), written to eFuse via esp_efuse_write_keys(), and the function returns (flash_encrypt.c:243) without scrubbing it. In esp_flash_encrypt_region(), the plaintext flash sector buffer buf (flash_encrypt.c:454) retains the last sector's cleartext at both the success and flash_failed returns. Neither path performs a memset/bzero/mbedtls_platform_zeroize, even though the same port already does bzero for key digests in boot/espressif/hal/src/secure_boot.c.

The affected code runs only on the Espressif port with CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED, and only during the one-time first-boot provisioning pass when flash encryption is not yet enabled (boot/espressif/main.c); on subsequent boots the buffers are never created. Recovering the residue requires an out-of-band stack/RAM-disclosure primitive — JTAG/debug halt, UART ROM download, a core/crash dump, or a warm-boot RAM scrape — captured during that single provisioning boot. Under the recommended CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_RELEASE plus secure boot, those channels are fused off and no exposure exists.

The practical impact is a low-severity, defense-in-depth hardening gap: a flash-encryption key (and last plaintext sector) may linger in bootloader stack memory. Because the eFuse key block is burned read+write-protected, the transient stack copy is the only readable copy, and only during one boot; in a development build where a disclosure channel is open, an attacker with that capability can usually already read the still-plaintext flash directly, so the marginal confidentiality gain is small. Confirming real-world recovery depends on a specific SoC/debug configuration not exercisable from source alone.

In Eclipse iceoryx-rs, versions 0.0.11 to 0.0.13 and 0.1.0 as well as on the latest main branch.



`SampleReceiver::<T>::take()` and `Sample::<T>::deref()` are safe functions that hand the caller a `&T` pointing at a chunk written by another iceoryx process, but the subscriber path neither requires `T: ShmSend` nor verifies that the received chunk is at least `size_of::<T>()` bytes / `align_of::<T>()`-aligned. A peer process that publishes an undersized chunk, or any chunk at all when the subscriber chose a pointer-bearing `T`, drives a `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` subscriber into out-of-bounds reads of adjacent shared-memory chunks or dereference of a publisher-controlled pointer.



Resolution:



It will not be fixed since this is a known limitation in iceoryx as it is the users responsibility to specify the same data type on sender and receiver side.



[iceoryx2](https://github.com/eclipse-iceoryx/iceoryx2) is the successor of iceoryx-rs where the API is designed to prevent this by default.



It is strongly recommended to migrate to iceoryx2 which is actively maintained and receives security support.



The iceoryx-rs package has officially reached End-of-life and will not receive any features, bugfixes or security fixes.

Description

When StormCrawler fetches a host's `/robots.txt` and receives a redirect, `HttpRobotRulesParser`
resolves the `Location` header and re-fetches the target for up to five hops. The loop checks neither
the scheme, the host nor the port of the resolved target, and it is not governed by
`http.allow.redirects`, which only affects the page fetch. A crawled site can therefore point the
robots.txt fetch at any address reachable from the fetcher worker, including loopback interfaces,
private ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Every crawled URL triggers a robots.txt fetch on a cache
miss, so no unusual configuration is required to reach the loop.

The fetched body is only parsed as robots rules and is not returned to the caller, so the read itself
is blind. The more direct impact is on credentials: the okhttp protocol applies its configured request
headers, including the `Authorization` header built from `http.basicauth.user` and
`http.basicauth.password` and anything in `http.custom.headers`, to every request it makes. Because
StormCrawler follows the redirect itself and issues a new request, okhttp's own removal of the
`Authorization` header across a host change does not apply, and the operator's crawl credentials are
delivered to the host the redirect names.

The connection-time IP filter, `http.filter.ipaddress.include` and `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude`, is
installed as an okhttp network interceptor on the same client and does apply to these hops when it is
configured. It ships with no rules, which is why the path is reachable in a default configuration. URL
filtering never applies, because the robots.txt fetch does not pass through the outlink filter chain.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a robots.txt redirect is followed only when the target uses http or https and
shares scheme, host and port with the URL it was reached from. Deployments that legitimately serve
robots.txt through a cross-host redirect can restore the previous behaviour with
`http.robots.redirect.crosshost.allow`.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude` to cover loopback,
private, link-local and CGNAT ranges, which is enforced after DNS resolution and therefore also on
redirect hops. Operators who configure `http.basicauth.*` or `http.custom.headers` for a crawl should
assume those credentials may have been sent to third-party hosts and rotate them, and should scope
credentials by running a separate topology per origin.

Description

The SQL status backend serialises per-URL metadata into a single column by concatenating a tabulation,
the key, an equals sign and the value, with no escaping. On read-back the string is split on the same
two characters, so the round trip is not injective: a value that contains a tabulation returns as one
or more additional keys that were never written.

Values on that path are supplied by crawled servers. `FetcherBolt` records the raw `Location` header of
a redirect as `_redirTo`, and `_redirTo` is part of the default `metadata.persist` set, so a redirect
whose `Location` contains a tabulation followed by `key=value` pairs introduces those keys into the
crawler's own control metadata on the next scheduling cycle. Several control keys are read without a
prefix, so the injected keys are live: `http.proxy.host`, `http.proxy.port`, `http.proxy.user` and
`http.proxy.pass` among them, as well as scheduling and request-shaping keys such as `depth`,
`max.depth`, `crawl.delay`, `http.content.limit` and `isSitemap`.

Where a proxy manager is configured, the consequence is not limited to corrupted scheduling data.
`SingleProxyManager.getProxy(Metadata)` consults the per-URL metadata first and returns what it finds,
so an injected proxy host and port take precedence over the operator's configured proxy and subsequent
fetches, together with any configured `Authorization` header, are routed through a host the crawled
content chose. A related defect in `AbstractStatusUpdaterBolt` compounds this: an injected
`status.store.as.is.with.nextfetchdate` that is not a valid instant escapes the enclosing try/catch and
stops the bolt, and because the stored row is replayed the failure repeats.

Deployments using the OpenSearch or Solr status backends are unaffected, because those serialise
metadata structurally.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where the metadata column is written in an escaped form behind a format marker, rows
written by earlier versions are still decoded unchanged, and the stored next-fetch-date is parsed
defensively.

The fix does not repair rows written before the upgrade. Operators using the SQL status backend should
inspect the metadata column of an existing status table for tabulation characters and remove the
affected rows, and should assume any proxy credentials configured for the crawl may have been exercised
through an attacker-chosen proxy and rotate them. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can remove
`_redirTo` from `metadata.persist` to close the demonstrated path, though other crawled values reaching
persisted metadata remain.

Description

`CookieConverter.getCookies` decides which stored cookies to attach to an outbound request. The
applicability check is nested inside a test for the presence of a `Domain` attribute, so a cookie
without one, which is the ordinary form of a session cookie, skips scoping entirely and is returned for
whatever target URL was passed. RFC 6265 requires the opposite: a cookie with no `Domain` attribute is
host-only and belongs to the host that set it.

Two further defects sit in the same method. The domain comparison has no notion of a registrable
domain, so a `Domain` value of `com` matches every host under it, and the comparison returns true when
it throws, so a failure to evaluate the check admits the cookie. Neither the converter nor
`MetadataTransfer`, which carries the stored cookie to outlinks, ever considers the host that issued
it.

Cookie handling is opt-in: it requires `http.use.cookies` to be set to true, which is not the default,
and the cookie key to be listed in `metadata.transfer`. The documented recipe does not work as written,
because the `metadata.transfer` example in the internals documentation names `set-cookie` while the key
present in metadata is `protocol.set-cookie` and the transfer matches key names exactly. Deployments
affected are therefore those where an operator determined the correct key, enabled cookie handling and
crawls an authenticated site whose pages link or redirect to other hosts. In that case the session
cookie of the authenticated origin is sent to those hosts.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a cookie without a `Domain` attribute is sent only to the host that set it, a
single-label domain is rejected and the domain check fails closed. Because the protocol does not yet
record the host that issued a cookie, cookies without a `Domain` attribute are not sent at all until
that host is recorded; operators relying on cookie transfer will notice this. The documentation error
is corrected in the same release.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should confine an authenticated crawl to a topology whose URL
filters keep it on the origin that issued the credentials, and should not rely on cookie scoping as a
boundary. Rotating session credentials used for such crawls is advisable.

Description

`HostURLFilter.configure` reads the `ignoreOutsideDomain` parameter but tests the node belonging to
`ignoreOutsideHost` when deciding whether the domain mode was configured. A filter configuration that
names only `ignoreOutsideDomain`, which the class documentation presents as an independent mode, is
therefore discarded: the flag is forced to false, `filter` short-circuits on its guard and every URL is
returned unchanged. The filter enforces nothing while appearing to be configured, and the failure is
silent. The mirror-image configuration, naming only `ignoreOutsideHost`, fails with a
`NullPointerException` while the topology is starting.

The effect is the loss of a scope control the operator configured, so a crawled page's outlinks are
followed to hosts the operator intended to exclude. Impact beyond crawl scope depends on what the
crawler then fetches and is not claimed here. Projects generated from the StormCrawler Maven archetypes
are not affected, because all three shipped filter configurations set both parameters.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where each parameter is tested independently. Operators whose configuration sets only
`ignoreOutsideDomain` will find the crawl restricted to the source domain, as configured, which may
reduce the number of outlinks accepted.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set both `ignoreOutsideHost` and `ignoreOutsideDomain`
explicitly in the `HostURLFilter` configuration, which produces the intended behaviour on affected
versions.

Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

Allot's Subscriber Management Platform (SMP) v18.3.53 stores sensitive configuration credentials protected by a product‑wide, hard‑coded master password. The master key is constructed using a hard-coded string value plus a default key value. This results in an effective encryption key that is recoverable from shipped scripts and configuration files. The platform uses a deprecated and cryptographically insecure algorithm (PBEWithMD5AndDES) and no documented mechanism exists to change the key. An attacker with read access to configuration files, backups, or diagnostic bundles can recover credentials and TLS keystore/truststore passwords, and access to subscriber-management operations and subscriber PII.

A received message could include an attachment that referred to an arbitrary local file under a misleading name. If the user dragged that attachment into a message being composed and sent it, the contents of the referenced local file were included in the outgoing message. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

When a CardDAV address book was accessed through an HTTP proxy that requested authentication, Thunderbird could answer the proxy with the CardDAV server's username and password. This affected both setting up a new address book and syncing existing ones, where a saved password could be sent without any user interaction. A malicious or compromised proxy could use this to obtain the address book credentials, even for address books served over HTTPS. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

When a signed OpenPGP/MIME message had no Date header, or one that could not be parsed, Thunderbird did not compare the signature creation time with the message date. For S/MIME messages with more than one Date header, a later Date header could be used for the comparison. An attacker who had an old signed message could resend it and have it shown with a valid signature, despite the protection added for CVE-2022-2226. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

Thunderbird did not compare the signature creation time with the message date for messages that were both signed and encrypted with OpenPGP/MIME. An attacker who had an old signed message could encrypt it to the victim and resend it with a current date, and have it shown with a valid signature, despite the protection added for CVE-2022-2226. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

By combining several weaknesses, a crafted email could, when opened, inject commands into the authenticated IMAP connection, and load a web page with JavaScript enabled in place of the message. A bare carriage return in a header let the sender set Thunderbird's internal message flags, marking the message as a feed item and allowing its remote content to load. A reference to an embedded part placed inside an attribute value disclosed the message's internal IMAP URL to the sender. The message ID part of IMAP URLs was not validated, so loading a crafted variant of that URL sent arbitrary IMAP commands, which could modify or delete messages and folders. Finally, a frame reloading the message, together with a legacy feed marker in its content, caused the message pane to load a sender-chosen web page with scripting enabled. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

By adding a From header with lowercase name before the actual From header, an attacker could make Thunderbird display a different sender than the one used to verify an OpenPGP signature. Anyone whose key the victim had accepted could send messages that appeared to be validly signed by any other sender. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8.

Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments
while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer
a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than
the actual data sent.

Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that
accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer
may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the
receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent
STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends
many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first
byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any
data.

Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default
policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before
state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing
prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the
life of the connection.

The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can
pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and
connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is
limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a
non-default configuration.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the public project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating).



The public project API did not check that a project had been made public before granting the caller read access to it. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could give themselves lasting read access to other users' private projects and to the private workflows in them, including their version and execution history. Only deployments in which users have created projects are affected; the project feature is hidden in the web UI by default.



This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data.



If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy.



Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project_user_access table, which remains empty unless someone has used the feature: treat any READ grant on a project that is not listed in public_project, and that the project's owner did not give, as suspect. The upgrade deletes this table. Removing a grant does not remove copies the user may already have made of the workflows.

The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work.

Two other paths made the cost of a query grow faster than its size, without any regular expression:
- The filter evaluator scanned the whole expression for logical operators once per node. Its cost grew with the square of the number of chained clauses.
- Queries starting with $ inside a filter, like @.x == $.limit or length($.items), were evaluated again for every node the filter visits.

An application that evaluates an attacker-influenced JSONPath expression can therefore still be made to hold a PHP worker. A document of 2 MB and a query of 2.5 KB take 3.5 minutes of CPU.

JsonCrawler::find() now bounds the total regex work of one call, and throws an exception when that budget is exhausted. Filter expressions are parsed once per query, and absolute queries inside filters are evaluated once per query.

Most methods of Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path rely on Path::split(), which takes everything before the first :// as the root of a path. It doesn't check that this prefix is a URI scheme, so the .. segments in that prefix are never resolved. PHP sees a scheme only at the start of a string. So /base/../x://../secret.txt is a plain local path to /secret.txt for PHP, while Path::isBasePath('/base', '/base/../x://../secret.txt') returns true. canonicalize(), join(), makeAbsolute() and makeRelative() are affected the same way.

Some applications check a path built from user input with isBasePath() or canonicalize(), and then open it. They can be made to read or write files outside the expected directory.

On Symfony 6.4 and later, the AssetMapper component builds with Path::join() the path of the files that a remote package references from its CSS. A malicious or compromised package can therefore make importmap:require or importmap:install write a file of its choice outside assets/vendor. For example, the CSS url(../../../../../public/x://shell.php) writes public/x:/shell.php.

A prefix is now a scheme only when PHP would look for a stream wrapper with that name. That is two or more letters, digits, +, - or ., followed by :// at the start of the path. Other prefixes are regular path segments, and the .. segments after them are resolved. Real schemes such as phar://, file://, vfs:// or compress.zlib:// keep working.

When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to a front controller in a subdirectory. The base URL then kept everything before the script name, and the client chooses that part. A request URI starting with // or /\ made the base URL start with a host.

With SCRIPT_NAME=/public/index.php, a request for //evil.example/public/index.php/login is routed to /login, with the base URL //evil.example/public/index.php and the base path //evil.example/public. The URLs generated for that page then point to evil.example:
- links built with path() and the actions of forms, so a login form sends the credentials of the user to evil.example;
- redirects to generated URLs, such as the ones of redirectToRoute();
- assets referenced with a relative path through asset(), so the page can load scripts from evil.example.

The attacker has to make a user follow a crafted link, such as https://app.example//evil.example/public/index.php/login. framework.trusted_hosts does not help, since the host of the request is the real one.

Applications are affected when their front controller is in a subdirectory and the web server sends it URIs that do not start with that directory. A .htaccess file at the root of the project that rewrites every URL to public/ does that, for instance.

Applications are also affected when the web server sets SCRIPT_NAME to the path of the request. Some nginx configurations do that when they send every request to the front controller without fastcgi_split_path_info. php -S does it too, with a router script outside the document root. A request for /\evil.example/index.php then gets the base URL /\evil.example/index.php, which browsers read as a link to evil.example.

The configurations recommended in the Symfony documentation are not affected.

Request::getBaseUrl() now returns an empty base URL when the request URI starts with // or /\.

Since the fix for CVE-2025-64500, Request::getPathInfo() strips the script name from the start of the URL. It does so even when the script name is only the start of a longer path segment. With SCRIPT_NAME set to /index.php, a request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /admin and is routed like /admin. Encoded spellings such as /index%2Ephpadmin or /%69ndex.phpadmin work too. Before that fix, the path info was admin, which no route matched.

Rules enforced by Symfony are not affected: access_control and firewalls read the same path info as the router. Rules enforced in front of PHP are. The nginx configuration of the Symfony documentation and the .htaccess file of symfony/apache-pack make /index.php/admin unreachable, but they pass /index.phpadmin to the front controller. So a location /admin block in nginx, a <Location /admin> section in Apache, or a CDN or WAF rule on /admin can be bypassed.

The script name is now stripped only when it is followed by /, ? or the end of the URL. A request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /index.phpadmin.

The 3D Website Builder WordPress plugin through 2.0.3 does not perform any authorisation check in one of its publicly accessible AJAX actions, and the nonce guarding it is exposed to visitors on any page embedding the 3D Website Builder WordPress plugin through 2.0.3's shortcode, allowing unauthenticated users to permanently delete any of the 3D Website Builder WordPress plugin through 2.0.3's 3D builder objects and their slides.

XML::Sig versions before 0.74 for Perl allow code execution via a document's Algorithm attribute that verify resolves to a function name and calls.

The text after the last `#` in the DigestMethod and SignatureMethod Algorithm attributes is looked up with Digest::SHA->can. That returns a code reference for any fully qualified function name, Perl builtins in the CORE namespace included. The digest function is called on the canonical form of the referenced element, so the document picks both the function and its argument.

An attacker who can submit a signed document can run a command as the verifying process.

An information disclosure vulnerability in Zstandard versions 1.5.1 through 1.5.7 allows specially crafted compressed data to expose the contents of an internal buffer through decompressed output. The buffer is 64 KiB in the default configuration and may contain uninitialized memory or literals from earlier decompressions performed using the same decompression context. An attacker who can submit compressed data and observe the resulting output can recover the buffer's contents.

The ggml-rpc server suffers from an uninitialized heap memory disclosure vulnerability where the alloc_buffer function provides new clients with buffers containing stale data from previously freed allocations. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to perform an in-bounds read via get_tensor to recover sensitive information, such as model weights or KV-cache data, belonging to other clients sharing the same server.

In Phase2SecureConnections::OnPeerPublicKey of phase_2_secure_connections.cc, there is a possible way to learn the passkey used during pairing due to an incomplete check for a reflected public key. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is needed for exploitation.

In OnRxLeCreditBasedConnectionRequest of le_dynamic_channel.cc, there is a possible assertion failure due to improper input validation. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In LogicalLink::SignalError of logical_link.cc, there is a possible use after free due to an error callback that can synchronously destroy the link while its channels are still being iterated. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In HandleRxPdu of channel.cc, there is a possible use after free due to the channel being destroyed while it is still processing a received frame. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In NexustalkStream::PullFrameTask of nexustalk_stream.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is needed for exploitation.

In MediaFocusFidlImpl of media_focus_fidl_impl.cc, there is a possible use after free due to a race condition. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

The WordForm  WordPress plugin before 4.1.6 does not properly validate uploaded files, allowing unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files, including PHP, which leads to remote code execution.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not safely process the output of the external database dump tool when backing up large tables, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to store profile data that turns into SQL executed when an administrator later restores the backup, for example to grant themselves the administrator role.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve long database values byte-for-byte when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a serialized value that becomes a PHP Object Injection once an administrator backs up and restores the database.

No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or WordPress core, so the demonstrated effect is instantiation of an attacker-chosen class in the attacker's own requests. The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not correctly handle comment-like content found in the middle of a long SQL statement when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber who have stored crafted content in their own profile to have SQL executed when an administrator later restores a backup, and so escalate their account to administrator.

This is a different code path from the backup restore issue fixed in 1.26.10, and it does not depend on the database server's maximum packet size.

The Mapster WP Maps — Mapbox, MapLibre & Google Maps for WordPress plugin before 2.0.7 does not perform any authorization check when saving edits made through its bundled photo-gallery library, allowing any authenticated user with at least Contributor-level access to overwrite the title and content of, and write arbitrary metadata onto, any post, page or media attachment on the site regardless of ownership.

The GiveWP  WordPress plugin before 4.19.2.1 does not properly restrict access to sensitive donor information in one of its REST API endpoints, allowing any authenticated user who owns a donor record, such as a subscriber who has donated once, to retrieve the email address, phone number, name, postal address and company of all donors.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check that a requested Zoom meeting's recordings were published on the site before fetching them with the site's connected Zoom account, allowing unauthenticated users who know a meeting ID to retrieve that meeting's cloud recording details, including its topic, share link, passcode when returned by Zoom, and direct play and download links.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check authorization, or whether a meeting is restricted to logged-in users, password-protected or unpublished, before returning a meeting's join links, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the passcode-embedded join links of any meeting, including meetings the site restricts.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check that the requester is authorized to join a meeting before issuing a Zoom Meeting SDK signature for it, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain a valid signed join credential for an arbitrary meeting.

The GiveWP  WordPress plugin before 4.19.2.1 does not exclude donors who chose to give anonymously from one of its public REST API listings, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve those donors' names.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.10, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.10.26 does not guard all execution paths of its database restore process against second-order SQL injection, allowing a Subscriber-level user who has stored crafted content in their own account to escalate to administrator when an administrator later restores a backup.
This is due to an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-108761 in 1.26.9: the fix guards only one of the restore routine's execution paths, and a second path remains exploitable.

Use of cache containing sensitive information vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's ExpiresFilter caused by the filter removing cache-control header fields set by the authentication layer.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.1 through 7.0.109. Older unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released
